###### **assign_feedthrough_supply**

Assigns related supplies for feedthrough ports of a given net or net connected to a given
pin.

**Syntax**

status _assign_feedthrough_supply_
```
[-net nets ]
[-pin pins ]
[-verbose]
```

**Data Types**
```
nets   collection
pins   collection
```

**Arguments**
```
-net
```

Generates the related supplies for the feedthrough pins connected to the given
nets.
```
-pin
```

Generates the related supplies for the given feedthrough pins and feedthrough
pins on the net connected to these pins.
```
-verbose
```

Report driver of net which _assign_feedthrough_supply_ failed to propagate and
its failure reasons.

**Description**

The _assign_feedthrough_supply_ command determines the best supplies to use as related
supplies for the feedthrough ports on a given net or pin. The supplies are determined with
the goal of minimizing the use of dual rail cell buffer/inverters in feedthrough domains.

You must specify either _-net_ or _-pin_ option.

When the command runs it reports the following information messages:

 - The name of the output report ( _MV-1055_ )

 - The name of the report for failed nets ( _MV-1051_ )

 - The number of nets correctly processed by the command ( _MV-1056_ )




 - The number of nets which the command failed to process ( _MV-1057_ )

 - The number of nets which command skipped ( _MV-1052_ )

_=== Behavior on Soft Macro Ports ===_

User defined _set_port_attributes_ (SPA) on soft macro feedthrough ports are preserved
during command execution. When a soft macro port has a user defined SPA, the tool splits
port’s net into two segments: one where the port is a net's load and another, where the
port is the net's driver. As part of this process, some segments could only have driver and
loads ports, but no other feedthrough ports. In such case, those nets are skipped by the
command with message MV-1065.

_=== Behavior with Constant Net ===_

To derive driver supply of the constant nets, tool collects all loads supplies plus driver
domain primary supply. Only supply nets which are available in driver domain are
considered. The command assigns the supply which creates less dual-rails buffer. If two or
more supply nets generate the same result, the solution using driver supply is preferred.

For paths which includes soft macro, if there is a user specified receiver supply on any soft
macro port, tool considers the receiver supply as load supply, instead of traversing through
to the final load.

_=== Output Report ===_

By running this command, an output report file is created with the name
_assign_feedthrough_supply.report.<design_name>_ . The report contains information
for each net that was successfully processed by the command. The report starts with
application option section where application options, which can change command
behavior, are listed. After that section, each net is reported as a list of physical boundary
ports, where each port can show below information (attributes):

 - Constant/Undriven: When driver is constant or undriven e.g. _tie cell_, tool reports
"Constant/Undriven" instead of port name.

 - driver_supply: Port uses driver supply as related supply set. The attribute could appear
in any pin.

 - receiver_supply: Port uses load supply as related supply set. The attribute could
appear in any pin.

 - primary_supply: Port uses Power Domain's primary supply as related supply set. The
attribute could appear in any pin.

 - reference-only: The assigned supply set is not available in block power domain and
cannot used for buffering. The attribute could appear in any pin.

 - soft_macro: The port belongs to a soft-macro cell. The attribute appears in soft macro
ports.




 - refinable_macro: The port belongs to a refinable-macro cell. The attribute appears in
refinable macro ports.

 - user_spa: When the attribute is present it indicates the related supply set was assigned
by user or _split_contraints_ (it is in user section of UPF file). If it is not present, it means
the attribute was set by _assign_feedthrough_supply_ command (it is in derived section
of UPF file). This attribute can only appear on drivers and loads.

 - updated: When this attribute is present it means tool changed related supply set of this
port for a new one. For example, if the previous value was _SS1_ and the new value is
_SS2_, the _updated_ attribute will be reported. If both were similar (the previous value and
new value are _SS1_ ) or if there is no previous value, the _updated_ attribute will not be
reported. This attribute can only appear on physical boundary ports.

 - dangling: When _mv.hierarchical.propagate_driver_supply_for_empty_design_ is
enabled, _assign_feedthrough_supply_ reports unconnected endpoints as loads. This
attribute is meant to differentiate between real loads and unconnected endpoints.

Besides these attributes, the report also shows _feedthrough port level_ which is the deep
level starting from the driver pin to the reported pin. _Feedthrough port level_ for driver pin is
not showed in this report and it is assumed to be 0. Below there is an example for output
report:
```
--------------------------------------------------Application Options for assign_feedthrough_supply:
--------------------------------------------------mv.hierarchical.afs_create_reference_supply: true
mv.hierarchical.propagate_driver_supply_use_same_driver_receiver: false
mv.hierarchical.propagate_driver_supply_for_empty_design: true
mv.hierarchical.propagate_driver_supply_use_soft_macro_domain_primary:
false
--------------------------------------------------+ DRIVER_PIN in: SS0 (driver_supply, primary_supply, user_spa)
- (Level 1) MID0/in: SS0 (driver_supply)
- (Level 2) MID0/out: SS0 (driver_supply)
- (Level 3) MID1/in: SS2 (receiver_supply, primary_supply,
soft_macro)
- (Level 4) LOAD_PIN MID1/out: SS2 (receiver_supply, primary_supply,
soft_macro, user_spa)
- (Level 3) MID2/in: SS0 (driver_supply, soft_macro)
- (Level 4) LOAD_PIN MID2/out: SS0 (driver_supply, soft_macro,
user_spa)
```

In above example, there is a heterogeneous split fanout from driver _in_ to loads _MID1/out_
and _MID2/out_ where both loads are at the same feedthrough port level.

_=== Report for failed nets ===_




Whenever this command runs, it creates a report named
_assign_feedthrough_supply.report.<design_name>.failed_ . This file name is always
reported using message _MV-1051_ .

Similar to output report, it stars with the application option section and reports information
for failed nets only. You can check _-verbose report_ section to know which errors are
classified as _failed_ .

For each failed net, it shows following information:

 - Failed reason before driver pin:
```
Driver: in
MV-1061: Net driven by 'in' has Level Shifter Violation. Please, fix
the violation before continuing.
```

 - Report below information for driver, loads and feedthrough ports:
```
Level <feedthrough level> -- <pin name> (attributes)
Type: <Driver, Feedthrough or Load>
Pin Direction: <in, out, inout>
Power Domain: <power domain name>
Primary Supply: <supply set name>
Available Supplies: <list of supply nets>
Physical Block: <block name>
```

where attributes could be one or more of below:

 - undriven: If port is a driver but has no real driver. It can only appear on driver ports. •
dangling: If port is a dangling load. It can only appear on load ports. • constant: If port
is a driver connected to a constant zero or one. It can only appear on driver ports. •
soft_macro: If port is a soft_macro port. It can appear on any port. • refinable_macro: If
port is a refinable_macro port. It can appear on any port.

Similar to output report, feedthrough port level is also shown but it includes the
feedthrough port level for drivers.

Note that the report is always overwritten to have up-to-date information of the last run of
_assign_feedthrough_supply_ .

Below there is an example of report for failed nets:
```
--------------------------------------------------Application Options for assign_feedthrough_supply:
--------------------------------------------------mv.hierarchical.afs_create_reference_supply: true
mv.hierarchical.propagate_driver_supply_use_same_driver_receiver: false
mv.hierarchical.propagate_driver_supply_for_empty_design: true
mv.hierarchical.propagate_driver_supply_use_soft_macro_domain_primary:
false
--------------------------------------------------
```



```
Driver: in
MV-1061: Net driven by 'in' has Level Shifter Violation. Please, fix
the violation before continuing.
Level 0-- in
Type: Driver
Pin Direction: in
Power Domain: PD_TOP (Primary: SS0)
Physical Block: top:top.design
Level 1-- MID0/in
Type: Feedthrough port
Pin Direction: in
Power Domain: PD_MID0 (Primary: SS1)
Physical Block: top:mid_0.design
Level 2-- MID0/out
Type: Feedthrough port
Pin Direction: out
Power Domain: PD_MID0 (Primary: SS1)
Physical Block: top:mid_0.design
Level 3-- out[0]
Type: Load
Pin Direction: out
Power Domain: PD_TOP (Primary: SS0)
Physical Block: top:top.design
Level 1-- MID1/in
Type: Feedthrough port
Pin Direction: in
Power Domain: PD_MID1 (Primary: SS2)
Physical Block: top:mid_1.design
Level 2-- MID1/out
Type: Feedthrough port
Pin Direction: out
Power Domain: PD_MID1 (Primary: SS2)
Physical Block: top:mid_1.design
Level 3-- BOT/in
Type: Load
Pin Direction: in
Power Domain: PD_BOT (Primary: SS2)
Physical Block: top:mid_1.design
```

_=== -verbose report ===_




Using the _-verbose_ option can help you to understand why _assign_feedthrough_supply_
failed to process one or more nets. Below are the typical problems:

 - Net with bidirectional pins ( _MV-1058_ ): Bidirectional pins are not supported by this
command. This message is classified as _skipped_ .

 - Clock net ( _MV-1059_ ): Clock nets are supported by this command, but they must be
present in the list of permitted clock net (see _mv.upf.auto_ls_clock_nets_ for more
details). This message is classified as _skipped_ .

 - Analog net ( _MV-1060_ ): Analog nets pins are not supported by this command. This
message is classified as _skipped_ .

 - Level Shifter Violations ( _MV-1061_ ): tool try to fix Level Shifter Violations as part of
its normal run. However, there are cases where tool cannot solve them. In those
cases, _-verbose_ option will report _MV-1061_ . You can run other commands to get
more details about Level Shifter Violations like _check_mv_desing -level_shifter_,
_analyze_mv_feasibility -level_shifter_, _analyze_mv_design -level_shifter -through_ and
_report_mv_path -level_shifter -pin_ . This message is classified as _failed_ .

 - Bump Cell Driver ( _MV-1062_ ): Nets driven by Bump Cells are not supported by this
command. This message is classified as _skipped_ .

 - Undriven nets ( _MV-1064_ ): Undriven nets are only supported if
_mv.hierarchical.propagate_driver_supply_for_empty_design_ is true. This message is
classified as _skipped_ .

 - Skipped net because there is no feedthrough port to work with ( _MV-1065_ ): Net is
skipped since it has no assignable feedthrough ports. This message is classified as
_skipped_ .

**Examples**

The following is an example of the output report generated by _assign_feedthrough_supply_ :
```
prompt> set_port_attributes -driver_supply SS3 -ports MID1/out
prompt> assign_feedthrough_supply -pin in
prompt> sh cat assign_feedthrough_supply.report.*
--------------------------------------------------Application Options for assign_feedthrough_supply:
--------------------------------------------------mv.hierarchical.afs_create_reference_supply: true
mv.hierarchical.propagate_driver_supply_use_same_driver_receiver: false
mv.hierarchical.propagate_driver_supply_for_empty_design: true
mv.hierarchical.propagate_driver_supply_use_soft_macro_domain_primary:
false
--------------------------------------------------****************************************
Report : assign_feedthrough_supply

```



```

###### **assign_tsv**

Assigns the specified TSV (Through Silicon Via) in the TSV list to the specified logical net
and pins in the pin list.

**Syntax**

int _assign_tsv_
```
tsv_list
[-net net ]
[-pins pin_list ]
[-prefix prefix ]
[-force]
```

**Data Types**
```
net    net
pin_list  list
prefix   string
```

**Arguments**
```
tsv_list
```

Specifies the TSV to assign. If a TSV list is specified, the first TSV in the list
is the source point for routing. At least one TSV must be specified. This is a
required option.
```
-net net
```

Specifies the net to assign the TSV to. All specified objects are logically
connected to the net. If all objects are initially unconnected to any net, a new
net will be created with the given prefix that specified with option _-prefix_ . If
an existing net is already connected to some of the objects, the net will be
reused. To avoid user error, the command does not allow two existing nets to be
assigned together. This option and the _-pin_ option are mutually exclusive.
```
-pins pin_list
```

Specifies a list of pins to assign to the TSV. This option and the _-net_ option are
mutually exclusive.




```
-prefix prefix
```

Specifies a prefix for the name of a new net, if created.
```
-force
```

###### **associate_checkpoint_action**

Associates an action with checkpoint names.

**Syntax**
```
integer associate_checkpoint_action
[-before  {list_of_checkpoint_patterns} ]
[-after   {list_of_checkpoint_patterns} ]
[-replace  {list_of_checkpoint_patterns} ]
[-enable  name_of_action ]
[-disable  name_of_action ]

```



**Data Types**
```
list_of_checkpoint_names  list
name_of_action  string
```

**Arguments**
```
-before list_of_checkpoint_patterns
```

Specifies that the action should run before all checkpoints matching any of
the given checkpoint patterns. This option takes a Tcl list of checkpoint name
patterns as its parameter. Those names can be simple checkpoint names or
include glob-style * wildcard characters. Mutally exclusive with the -after and
-replace options.
```
-after list_of_checkpoint_patterns
```

Specifies that the action should run after all checkpoints matching any of the
given checkpoint patterns. This option takes a Tcl list of checkpoint name
patterns as its parameter. Those names can be simple checkpoint names or
include glob-style * wildcard characters. Mutally exclusive with the -before and
-replace options.
```
-replace list_of_checkpoint_patterns
```

Specifies that the action should run as a replacement for the Tcl commands
wrapped by the eval_checkpoint command. This happens for all checkpoints
matching any of the given checkpoint patterns. This option takes a Tcl list
of checkpoint name patterns as its parameter. Those names can be simple
checkpoint names or include glob-style * wildcard characters. Mutally exclusive
with the -before and -after options.
```
-enable name_of_action
```

Specifies the name of the action to enable at the matching checkpoint
patterns of the -before, -after, or -replace option. Mutually exclusive with the
-disable option. name_of_action must be an action previously defined with the
create_checkpoint_action command.
```
-disable name_of_action
```

Specifies the name of the action to disable at the matching checkpoint
patterns of the -before, -after, or -replace option. Mutually exclusive with the
-enable option. name_of_action must be an action previously defined with the
create_checkpoint_action command. If an action is both disabled and enabled at
a checkpoint, the disable setting takes precedence and the action will not run.




**Description**

This command configures an action to run at one more more checkpoints triggered by
the eval_checkpoint command in the flow scripts. Actions are defined in the checkpoint
system with the create_checkpoint_action command.

This command has two required options. The first is one of -enable or -disable, which
takes the name of the action as its parameter. This option specifies the name of the
action being associated, and whether that action should be enabled or disabled for the
patterns that will be given with the -before/-after/-replace option. -enable and -disable are
mutually exclusive on a single call to associate_checkpoint_action. But multiple calls can
be done to this command in sequence to give both enable and disable constraints. The
-enable and -disable settings from multiple invocations of associate_checkpoint_action are
time-sequenced. For example, enabling an action to run at * (all checkpoints), and then
disabling it to run at the 'create_placement' checkpoint will result in that action running at
all checkpoints except for 'create_placement'. This is a typical application of the disable
option, where an action is enabled to run at multiple checkpoints using a wildcard pattern,
but then disabled for one or more specific checkpoints that were matched by that pattern.

The second required option is one of -before, -after, or -replace. This option specifies the
timing of the execution of the action, relative to the checkpointed command. Only one of
-before, -after, or -replace can be given.

 - -before indicates that the action should run before the checkpointed command. A
typical before action is setting an app option before running a command.

 - -after indicates that the action should run after the checkpointed command. A typical
after action does some post-command cleanup, like changing constraints.

 - -replace indicates that the action should run in place of the checkpointed command. In
this case, the action is run but the original Tcl command/s wrapped by eval_checkpoint
do not execute. A typical usage of a replace action is to skip execution of a
command (by replacing it with nothing), or to modify the options of a command. The
'get_current_checkpoint -command' command can be run inside such a replacement
action to get the original command including it's options, so that they can be modified
by the action.

Any of the -before, -after, -replace options take a required parameter which is a Tcl
list of checkpoint name patterns at which to execute the action. For example, -before
"*placement* place_opt_initial_place" specifies that an action should execute before any
checkpoint with the name place_opt_initial_place, or with a name that includes the substring 'placement'.

Action definitions and associations should not be part of the golden flow scripts for the
design or project. They are intended to execute non-default actions that deviate from
the standard flow. They are typically included in the ./checkpoint.config.tcl file in your run
directory, which is automatically sourced by the checkpoint system.




**Examples**

Configures the gropto action to run before any *initial_drc checkpoints, to enable GRbased high-fanout synthesis in and place_opt
```
## In ./checkpoint.config.tcl
create_checkpoint_action gropto {
set_app_options \
-name place_opt.initial_drc.global_route_based \
-value true
}
associate_checkpoint_action -enable gropto -before *initial_drc
## Action will execute before this line in the flow script place_opt.tcl
eval_checkpoint place_opt_to_initial_drc {
place_opt -from initial_place -to initial_drc
}
```

Configures the high_eff_cong action to force high-effort congestion on all
create_placement* and refine_placement* checkpoints. get_current_checkpoint
-command is used to access and modify the original command options, and the -replace
option is used to replace the original command contents. ## In ./checkpoint.config.tcl
```
create_checkpoint_action high_eff_cong {
eval [get_current_checkpoint -command] -congestion_effort high
}
associate_checkpoint_action -enable high_eff_cong \
-replace "create_placement* refine_placement*"
## Action will execute as a replacement for checkpoints like these in the
flow scripts
eval_checkpoint create_placement_incr {create_placement -incremental}
eval_checkpoint refine_placement {refine_placement -effort high}

```

**See Also**

 - create_checkpoint_action

 - remove_checkpoint_actions

 - create_checkpoint_report

 - remove_checkpoint_reports

 - associate_checkpoint_report

 - eval_checkpoint

 - get_current_checkpoint




 - set_checkpoint_options

 - reset_checkpoints

 - get_checkpoint_data

###### **associate_checkpoint_report**

Associates a report with checkpoint names.

**Syntax**
```
integer associate_checkpoint_report
[-before  {list_of_checkpoint_patterns} ]
[-after   {list_of_checkpoint_patterns} ]
[-enable  name_of_report ]
[-disable  name_of_report ]
```

**Data Types**
```
list_of_checkpoint_names  list
name_of_report  string
```

**Arguments**
```
-before list_of_checkpoint_patterns
```

Specifies that the report should run before all checkpoints matching any of
the given checkpoint patterns. This option takes a Tcl list of checkpoint name
patterns as its parameter. Those names can be simple checkpoint names or
include glob-style * wildcard characters. Mutally exclusive with the -after option.
```
-after list_of_checkpoint_patterns
```

Specifies that the report should run after all checkpoints matching any of the
given checkpoint patterns. This option takes a Tcl list of checkpoint name
patterns as its parameter. Those names can be simple checkpoint names or
include glob-style * wildcard characters. Mutally exclusive with the -before
option.
```
-enable name_of_report
```

Specifies the name of the report to enable at the matching checkpoint
patterns of the -before, -after, or -replace option. Mutually exclusive with the
-disable option. name_of_report must be a report previously defined with the
create_checkpoint_report command.
```
-disable name_of_report
```

Specifies the name of the report to disable at the matching checkpoint
patterns of the -before, -after, or -replace option. Mutually exclusive with the




-enable option. name_of_report must be a report previously defined with the
create_checkpoint_report command. If a report is both disabled and enabled at
a checkpoint, the disable setting takes precedence and the report will not run.

**Description**

This command configures a report to run at one more more checkpoints triggered by
the eval_checkpoint command in the flow scripts. Reports are defined in the checkpoint
system with the create_checkpoint_report command.

This command has two required options. The first is one of -enable or -disable, which
takes the name of the report as its parameter. This option specifies the name of the
report being associated, and whether that report should be enabled or disabled for the
patterns that will be given with the -before/-after option. -enable and -disable are mutually
exclusive on a single call to associate_checkpoint_action. But multiple calls can be done
to this command in sequence to give both enable and disable constraints. The -enable
and -disable settings from multiple invocations of associate_checkpoint_action are
time-sequenced. For example, enabling a report to run at * (all checkpoints), and then
disabling it to run at the 'load_constraints' checkpoint will result in that action running at all
checkpoints except for 'load_constraints'. This is a typical application of the disable option,
where an action is enabled to run at multiple checkpoints using a wildcard pattern, but
then disabled for one or more specific checkpoints that were matched by that pattern.

The second required option is one of -before or -after. This option specifies the timing of
the execution of the report, relative to the checkpointed command. Only one of -before or
-after can be given.

 - -before indicates that the report should run before the checkpointed command. A
before report is used to measure QoR right before a command executes.

 - -after indicates that the action should run after the checkpointed command. An after
report is used to measure QoR right after a command executes.

Both the -before and -after options take a required parameter which is a Tcl list of
checkpoint name patterns at which to execute the report. For example, -after "*final
route_opt*" specifies that an report should execute after any checkpoint with a name
ending in 'final', as well as all route_opt checkpoints.

Typically, report are written to files in the ./checkpoint directory, but this is not enforced and
you can write reports to any disk location.

Report definitions and associations should not be part of the golden flow scripts for
the design or project. They are intended to separate reporting from the flow, such that
individual users can customize their reporting needs without touching the golden flow.
They are typically included in the ./checkpoint.config.tcl file in your run directory, which is
automatically sourced by the checkpoint system.




**Examples**

Save a block before route_opt for interactive debugging. get_current_checkpoint -name is
used to give the block a unique name.
```
## In ./checkpoint.config.tcl
create_checkpoint_report save_block {
save_block -as checkpoint_[get_current_checkpoint -name]
}
associate_checkpoint_report -enable save_block -before route_opt
## Block will be saved before this line from the route_opt.tcl flow
script
eval_checkpoint route_opt { route_opt }
```

Generate useful timing reports throughout the flow. Disables timing report generation at
the read_constraints checkpoints. Uses the get_current_checkpoint -name and -position
commands to give unique names to the reports before or after any checkpoint.
```
## In ./checkpoint.config.tcl
create_checkpint_report timing {
set name [get_current_checkpoint -name]
set pos [get_current_checkpoint -position]
redirect -file ./checkpoint/$name.$pos.qor.rpt { report_qor }
redirect -append ./checkpoint/$name.$pos.qor.rpt { report_qor -summary }
redirect -file ./checkpoint/$name.$pos.path.rpt { report_timing
-max_paths 10 }
}
associate_checkpoint_action -enable timing -before route_opt*
associate_checkpoint_action -enable timing -after *
associate_checkpoint_action -disable timing -after read_constraints

```

**See Also**

 - create_checkpoint_action

 - remove_checkpoint_actions

 - create_checkpoint_report

 - remove_checkpoint_reports

 - eval_checkpoint

 - get_current_checkpoint

###### **associate_mv_cells**

Associates the UPF strategies to the power management cells in the current design,
and reports the correlation between power management cells in the netlist and the UPF
strategies.

**Syntax**

status _associate_mv_cells_
```
[-isolation_cells]
[-level_shifters]
[-retention_registers]
[-power_switches]
[-all]
[-all_blocks | -blocks block_designs ]
[-host_options host_option_name ]
```

**Arguments**
```
-all_blocks
```

Associate MV cells for all the child blocks in the current design and the current
design itself. This option is mutually exclusive with _-blocks_ . Only one of them
can be specified at a time.
```
-blocks block_designs
```

Specifies the list of child block designs to associate MV cells. This option is
mutually exclusive with _-all_blocks_ . Only one of them can be specified at a time.
```
-host_options host_option_name
```

Specifies the host option to use for distributed processing. If not specified, the
tool uses the global host option if the option contains a distributed processing
settings.
```
-isolation_cells
```

Reports the correlation and discrepancies between isolation cells and isolation
strategies.
```
-level_shifters
```

Reports the correlation and discrepancies between level-shifter cells and levelshifting strategies.




```
-retention_registers
```

Reports the correlation and discrepancies between retention cells and retention
strategies.
```
-power_switches
```

Reports the correlation and discrepancies between power switches and UPF
power-switch strategies.
```
-all
```

Reports the correlation and discrepancies between all type of power
management cells and the strategies.

**Description**

The _associate_mv_cells_ command analyzes the current design and associates existing
power-management cells according to the UPF strategies. It also checks and reports the
correlation between the power-management cells in the netlist and the corresponding UPF
strategies. The checking is based only on the UPF strategies. This command does not
check for electrical violations.

If none of the power-management cell types are specified, this command associates all
types of the power-management cells in the design.

**Examples**

The following example shows the report from the _associate_mv_cells_ command when you
do not specify any argument. All types of power-management cells are reported.
```
prompt> associate_mv_cells
prompt>Information: Total 223 power switch cells have been associated.
(MV-021)
prompt>Information: Total 100 retention cells have been associated.
(MV-021)
prompt>Information: Total 40 isolation cells have been associated.
(MV-021)
prompt>Information: Total 50 level shifter cells have been associated.
(MV-021)
1

```

**See Also**

 - check_mv_design

 - mv.cells.rename_isolation_cell_with_formal_name

###### **associate_supply_set**

Associates a supply set or supply set ref to a supply set handle. The supply set handle
should be a pre-defined supply set for the power domain. User defined supply sets cannot
be used as supply set handle.

**Syntax**
```
string associate_supply_set
[-handle {supply_set_handle}*]
supply_set_ref

```

**Data Types**
```
supply_set_ref  string
supply_set_handle string
```

**Arguments**
```
-handle { supply_net_handle }*
```

Specifies the name of the predefined supply set of the given domain.
This should be the name constructed from the power domain name or
strategy name. Predefined _supply_set_handles_ for the power domain
include: _domain_name.primary_, _domain_name.default_isolation_ and
_domain_name.default_retention_ . This argument is required.
```
supply_set_ref
```

Specifies the supply set to be associated with the specified handle.

**Description**

The _associate_supply_set_ command associates a supply set with a power domain or
strategy handles. Handles are names rooted in the active scope. Handles should be
predefined supply sets for the power domain. If shall be an error if : 1) A supply set
handles are already associated with a supply set. 2) The associations of handles to supply
sets form a loop of associations.

**Examples**

The following example associates a supply set named SS1 to PD.primary




```
prompt> associate_supply_set SS1 -handle PD.primary

```

###### **attach_topology_nodes**

Attaches topology nodes to objects valid for association with topology node

**Syntax**

collection _attach_topology_nodes_
```
[ topology_node_list ]
```

**Data Types**
```
topology_node_list  collection
```

**Arguments**
```
topology_node_list
```

Specifies the set of topology nodes for association with valid objects. If this is
not specified then global selection set is used.




**Description**

The _attach_topology_nodes_ command associates specified topology nodes with
overlapped objects. Objects can be hierarchical. Allowed object types are pins, ports,
cells, voltage_areas, voltage_area shapes, shapes, placement blockages, routing
blockages, bounds, bound shapes, topology edges, bump regions, annotation shapes and
terminals. Only overlapped objects can be chosen.

Pins and ports are having higher priority over cells in the case of many overlapping
objects, and cells are having higher priority over all other types of objects. In addition, user
can set the list of desired object types to be used for association by win_set_select_class
command. When GUI is up and running the set of selectable object types is controlled by
the View Settings panel.

Overlapped cell object can be replaced by its pins associated with topology plan nets if
such pins are present and such replacement is not ambiguous.

If _topology_node_list_ is specified, topology nodes from the list are used in the command. If
it is not specified global selection is used.

The command returns collection of topology nodes for which attachment was established.

**Examples**

The following example makes attempt to find proper objects for attachment for all topology
nodes in the topology plan tp1.
```
prompt> attach_topology_nodes [get_topology_nodes -of_objects
[get_topology_plans tp1]]

###### **audit_scripts**
```

Reads in a script, examines the application options and variables used in the script, and
reports any changes to those application options or variables against a specified version of
the tool.

The command also reports references to .tbc files.

**Syntax**

status _audit_scripts_
```
-input script_name_or_path
[-skip_hidden]
[-from version ]
```

**Data Types**
```
script_name_or_path  string
version  string

```



**Arguments**
```
-input script_name_or_path
```

Specifies the location of the user scripts you want to audit. You can specify a
single Tcl file or a directory name. If you specify a directory, the command audits
all files in the directory with the .tcl suffix.

The tool issues an error message if _script_name_or_path_ is not a valid file or
directory.
```
-from version
```

A string specifying the tool version to compare your scripts against.

Note that only some tool versions are available for comparison, and that these
versions can change across releases. To get a current list of the tool versions
available for comparison, run the following command:
```
  prompt> audit_script -input . -from x
  Error: Value 'x' for option '-from' is not valid. Specify one of:
  18.06-sp5, 18.06-sp4, 18.06-sp2, 17.09-sp5 (CMD-031)
```

By default, if the -from option is not specified, the command compares your
script against the most current tool version available.
```
-skip_hidden
```

By default, the _audit_scripts_ command reports hidden application options,
variables, and Tcl commands. If you specify the -skip_hidden option, these items
will not be reported.

**Description**

The _audit_scripts_ command reads in one or more scripts, checks the scripts for any
deprecated, removed, or otherwise changed application options and variables, and reports
the results in an annotated version of each script. The annotated scripts are written to a
subdirectory named ./audit, each with the same name as the original file.

An annotated script contains AUDIT_INFO and AUDIT_ERROR comments that provide
information about each application option, application variable, and Tcl command change.
These comments are also written to the command line output as information messages.

An annotated script might look like this:
```
# AUDIT_INFO at line 105: application option 'cts.verbose.buf' is
unhidden.
# AUDIT_ERROR at line 147: application variable 'abor_enhance_inv_pair'
is removed.

```



```
# AUDIT_ERROR at line 156: system-default of application option
'cts.use_global_route_atree_topology' is changed from true to atree.
```

AUDIT_INFO comments identify the following:

Application options/variables that have become hidden or unhidden

Application options that have been deprecated

Application options whose scope has changed (global v. block-scoped)

Application variables that can be replaced by application options

References to .tbc files

AUDIT_ERROR comments identify the following:

Application options/variables that have been removed

Application options/variables whose data type has changed

Application options/variables whose value, user-default value, or system-default value has
changed (via an internal or user script)

Note that the _audit_scripts_ command evaluates application options and variables that have
been specified with the following commands only:
```
set_app_options
reset_app_options
get_app_option_value
get_app_options
report_app_options
help_app_options
set
set_app_var
get_app_var
report_app_var
write_app_var
printvar
```

The _audit_scripts_ command also evaluates commands that access application variables
as Tcl variables:
```
set variable_name value
echo $ variable_name
```

To repair any changed application options or variables in your scripts, you may either

Manually repair the application options/variables in your original scripts

Manually repair the application options/variables in the annotated scripts, and then copy
the annotated scripts to the location of your original scripts




**Examples**

The following example audits the input script test.tcl and writes out an annotated test.tcl
script to the ./audit directory:
```
prompt> audit_scripts -input test.tcl
```

This second example audits all the Tcl scripts in the scripts directory and writes out the
annotated scripts to the ./audit directory:
```
prompt> audit_scripts -input scripts

```

**See Also**

 - set_app_options

 - get_app_option_value

 - set_app_var

 - get_app_var

###### **auto_partition_design**

Partitions a design by regrouping logical hierarchies.

**Syntax**
```
collection auto_partition_design
[-from value ]
[-to value ]
[-check_only]
[-solution_to_select filename ]
[-verbose]
```

**Arguments**
```
-from value
```

Specifies one of the values (generate_solutions | select_solution
| apply_solution). On the basis of value, auto partition flow starts.
generate_solutions: To perform the auto partitioning select_solution: To select
the solution generated by above step. apply_solition: To commit the solution
```
-to value
```

Specifies one of the values (generate_solutions | select_solution
| apply_solution). On the basis of value, auto partition flow ends
generate_solutions: To perform the auto partitioning select_solution: To select
the solution generated by above step. apply_solition: To commit the solution




##### **b**


```
-check_only
```

Performs sanity checks on the constraints set by set_auto_partition_constraints
command.
```

```

Provides the filename as input to perform the selection of auto partition results.
```
-verbose
```

Shows detailed information.

**Description**

Partitions a design by regrouping logical hierarchies. Each partition is represented as a
virtual group. You need to specify maximum cell count allowed in a partition or maximum
number of partitions to be created using application options. You can specify the maximum
pin count of a partition using application option. You can specify application option to make
the partitioning physical aware.
