###### **check_frontside_fibs**

Checks FIB module logical and physical correctness, and coverage requirements.

**Syntax**

status _check_frontside_fibs_
```
[-bbox bounding_box ]
[-percent_goal percent_goal ]
[-prefix name_prefix ]
[-max_route_layer layer_name ]
```

**Data Types**
```
bounding_box    list
percent_goal    float
name_prefix    string
layer_name     string

```



**Arguments**
```
-bbox bounding_box
```

Specifies the area in which check needs to be performed.
```
  {{ llx lly } { urx ury }}
-percent_goal percent_goal
```

Specifies the expected coverage.
```
-prefix name_prefix
```

Specifies the prefix to identify fib cells. Default is "fib_logic_".
```
-max_route_layer layer_name
```

Specifies the maximum routing layer. If this value is less than top routing layer, it
will assume this is a sub-block.

**Description**

This command scans the area indicated by _-bbox. If not specified, entire core area is_
_scanned._

Starting from the lower left corner of -bbox or core area, the check
area is divided into windows. Scan window size is set by app option
eco.post_silicon_debug.fs_fib_check_window_size. Default is 50um. The command will
check number of windows with nand, nor, inv, and buffer type fib cells and report coverage
percentage for each type of fib cells.

It will also report if tie cells missing or not routed in the top 2 routing layers. It also checks
if there are any short/open fib nets.

**Examples**
```
prompt> check_frontside_fibs -percent_goal 25 \\
-bbox {{10 50} {50 85}} \\
-prefix "pe_" -max_route_layer M5
```

SH "SEE ALSO"
```
create_frontside_fibs(2)

###### **check_hier_design**
```

Checks a hierarchical design for possible issues related to top-level closure. This
command can be configured to report, tolerate or repair the errors. Messages generated
by this command are captured in an EMS database file and in the log file.




**Syntax**

status _check_hier_design_
```
[-stage timing | pre_placement | pre_clock_tree | pre_route |
pre_compile]
[-references  reference_design_names ]
```

**Data Types**
```
reference_design_names  list
```

**Arguments**
```
-stage timing | pre_placement | pre_clock_tree | pre_route |
pre_compile
```

Performs atomic checks for the specified design stage.

_-stage timing_ performs timing-related checks.

_-stage pre_placement_ performs both timing and pre-placement related checks.

_-stage pre_clock_tree_ performs timing, pre-placement, and pre-clock-tree
checks.

_-stage pre_route_ performs pre-route checks.

_-stage pre_compile_ performs checks to ensure that blocks linked to top are
ready for compile.

By default, only timing checks are run if this option is not specified.
```
-references reference_design_names
```

Specifies the names of design references, for physical hierarchies in the toplevel design, on which to run checks. By default, all physical hierarchies are
checked if this option isn't specified.

**Description**

This command performs design checks for use in the top-level closure flow. The checks
that report error can be alternatively configured to issue warning or repair the underlying
issue.

check_hier_design command honors the error, tolerate and repair policy settings of
hierarchical checks configured using _set_early_data_check_policy_ command. The policies
can be configured for each hierarchical check for each physical hierarchy reference.




 - error - When the check fails, command issues error. This is the default behavior of the
command.

 - tolerate - When the check fails, command issues warning.

 - repair - When the check fails, command performs repair work to resolve the error
condition and issues information on successful repair and error message in case of
repair failure.

The repairs performed are saved to the block within the check_hier_design command. To
ensure that the repair work gets saved to the sub-block, following are required:

 - Editability should be enabled on the sub-blocks on which repair has to be performed.

 - Ref-libs containing the sub-blocks should be opened for edit.

Repairs will be allowed to happen only if the bound view is read only abstract view or
editable design view.

When the repairs are performed, the records of the repair shall be created. The
records of the repair shall be saved when the repair gets saved to the design.
Use _get_early_data_check_records_ to get a collection of the records. Use
_report_early_data_checks -verbose -hierarchical_, to get the exact detail on the repair
done.

The command writes the Error, Warning and Information messages to Enhanced
Messaging System(EMS) database file and into text log file.

**Examples**

The following example performs timing-related checks.
```
prompt> check_hier_design -stage timing
```

The following example performs pre-placement checks on the RISC_CORE block.
```
prompt> check_hier_design -stage pre_placement -references RISC_CORE
```

The following example performs timing-related checks and writes the results to the EMS
database named check_hier.ems
```
prompt> create_ems_database check_hier.ems
prompt> check_hier_design -stage timing
prompt> save_ems_database -all
```

The following example sets repair policy on hier.block.missing_frame_view check.
```
prompt> open_block -ref_libs_for_edit ORCA.nlib:ORCA.design
prompt> set_early_data_check_policy -policy repair -check
hier.block.missing_frame_view -references RISC_CORE
prompt> set_editability -blocks RISC_CORE -value true
prompt> check_hier_design -stage pre_placement -references RISC_CORE

```



**See Also**

 - check_design

 - create_ems_database

 - save_ems_database

 - set_early_data_check_policy

 - report_early_data_checks

 - get_early_data_check_records

###### **check_host_options**

Checks that the specified host option is working properly in your environment.

**Syntax**
```
status check_host_options
-host_options  host_option_name
-target     target_value
[-work_dir   directory ]
[-timeout    timeout_value ]
```

**Data Types**
```
host_option_name   string
target_value     string
directory      string
timeout_value    int
```

**Arguments**
```
-host_options host_option_name
```

Specifies the name of the host option to be checked. Host options are created
using the _set_host_options_ command. This is a required option.
```
-target target_value
```

Specifies the name of the target application.
```
-work_dir directory
```

Specifies a working directory where various data and log files will be written.
By default, the directory is ./work_dir. This directory must be a network disk
accessible by all workers.




```
-timeout timeout_value
```

Specifies the maximum time to run the command. Value should be greater than
or equal to 0.

**Description**

This command tests the specified distributed processing host option to ensure that the
host option is correctly specified for your environment. The command launches a worker
process using the host options. This worker process only informs the master process that
it is alive and exits.

You should use this command to test your host option settings before beginning a
distributed processing run. If this command does not complete successfully, do not use the
given host option with any other command because it will not work. Instead, determine the
reason for the failure and fix the given host option, or run without distributed processing.

If you have problems getting this command to complete successfully, try first using a
simpler host option. You can also try using rsh rather than LSF or GRD.

**Examples**

This simple example sets the host option named myLSFtest for LSF distributed
processing, then checks the setting.
```
prompt> set_host_options -name myLSFtest -submit_command "bsub"
1
prompt> check_host_options -host_options myLSFtest
Checking host option: myLSFtest
check_host_options successful.

```

**See Also**

 - set_host_options

###### **check_io_placement**

Performs I/O placement checking.

**Syntax**

list _check_io_placement_
```
[-cells cell_collection ]
[-matching_types matching_type_collection ]
[-io_guides io_guide_collection ]
[-pad_assignment_file file ]
[-filename filename ]
[-output_directory directory ]
[-error_view view_name ]
[-overlap all | pad2pad | pad2filler | filler2filler | bump | corner2pad]

```



```
[-bump_assignment]
[-pad_to_guide_assignment]
[-signal_constraints]
[-power_constraints]
[-unplaced]
[-flipping]
[-gap]
[-min_pitch]
```

**Data Types**
```
cell_collection      list
matching_type_collection  list
io_guide_collection    list
file            string
filename          string
directory         string
view_name         string
```

**Arguments**
```
-cells cell_collection
```

Specifies cell instances, such as bumps, pads, fillers, for I/O placement
checking. If this option is used, only the specified cells are checked. If this option
is used but the specified cells are not valid objects for some specified checks,
the specified cells are ignored for those checks. Option _-cells_ cannot be used
together with option _-signal_constraints_, _-power_constraints_, _-min_pitch_, and
_-gap_ .
```
-matching_types matching_type_collection
```

Specifies user-defined matching types for I/O placement checking. If
this option is used, only the specified matching types are checked. If this
option is used and the specified matching types are not valid objects for
the specified checks, this specified matching types are ignored for those
checks. Option _-matching_types_ cannot be used together with option
_-pad_to_guide_assignment_, _-signal_constraints_, _-power_constraints_, _unplaced_,
_-min_pitch_, _-gap_ and _-flipping_ .
```
-io_guides io_guide_collection
```

Specifies the I/O guides for I/O placement checking. If this option is used, only
the specified I/O guides are checked. If this option is used and the specified
guides are not valid objects for the specified checks, this specified matching
types are ignored for those checks. Option _-io_guides_ cannot be used together
with option _-bump_assignment_, _unplaced_ and _-flipping_ .
```
-pad_assignment_file file
```

Specifies the file which contains a list of I/O pad cells and corresponding I/O
guides that are allowed for the I/O pad. Entries in this file specify a constraint




that limits the pad placement to only the listed I/O guide candidates. If the file is
not specified or file cannot be opened, the limitations in file will not be checked.
This option can only be used with option _-pad_to_guide_assignment_ .

The pad assignment file lists the constraints for the specified I/O pads. Each line
contains one or more pad names followed by a list of allowed I/O guide names.
I/O guides not in the list cannot be used to place the pads. If more than one pad
is listed on one line, the pads must be placed within a pair of curly braces. No
curly braces are needed for I/O guides. Each line must end with a semicolon.
```
  {pad1 pad2} guide1 guide2;
  pad3 guide1 guide3 guide0;
-filename filename
```

Specifies the name of the file where the reports of I/O placement checking
are written. Only 10 lines are printed to prompt for each report. In the file,
the complete reports are shown. The option cannot be used together with
_-output_directory_ option.
```
-output_directory directory
```

Writes individual report files for each check (overlap, bump assignment, and so
on) to the specified directory. The report file names are the name of the check.
If the directory does not already exist, the command tries to create the directory.
If creation is successful and write permissions are appropriate, the output is
written to individual files created in this directory instead of the console. The
option cannot be used together with the _-filename_ option.
```
-error_view view_name
```

Specifies the name of the generated error view. The command saves the error
view data to a file in XML format with the specified name. No attachment is
created nor saved in to the design database. If the view_name file already exists
under the current run directory, the command overwrites the file.

If this option is omitted, the error view data is stored as an attachment to the
design database. When the design is closed and saved, the error view data
is saved to the design database as well. The saved error view data does not
change until the next _check_io_placement_ command.
```
-overlap all | pad2pad | pad2filler | filler2filler | bump | corner2pad
```

Checks different kinds of overlaps, including pad-pad overlap, pad-filler overlap,
filler-filler overlap, bump overlap and corner-pad overlap. One or multiple valid
strings must be provided to enable corresponding checks. The valid strings are
all, pad2pad, pad2filler, filler2filler, bump. If "all" is specified, the other string is
ignored and all kinds of overlap are checked.




If a certain type of overlap checking is specified and invalid objects are
specified, only the valid objects are checked and the invalid objects are ignored.
For example, if bump overlap checking is specified and some bumps cells and
filler cells are specified, the filler cells are ignored.
```
-bump_assignment
```

Checks if bump assignment after place_io is consistent with defined matching
types (if any) and logical nets. This option works alone or together with _-cells_
and _-matching_types_ . If the option is specified by itself, all bumps are checked
for correct bump assignment. If the other type of objects are specified, they are
ignored for this checking.
```
-pad_to_guide_assignment
```

Checks if current pad-to-guide assignment is consistent with the definition.
If the option is specified by itself, all pads are checked for placement on the
correct guides. Use the _-cells_ option to specify the pads to check. If _-io_guides_
is specified, all pads that should be placed on specify I/O guides are checked.
To use together with _-pad_assignment_file_ option, a pad assignment file must
be provided. All the pads mentioned in the file are checked. The other type of
objects are ignored for this checking.
```
-signal_constraints
```

Checks if there are signal I/O pads violating constraints set by
_set_signal_io_constraints_ . Signal I/O constraints include order, pitch, spacing,
offset of pads and boundary-spacing. If the option is specified by itself, all I/O
guides with signal I/O constraints are checked.

Note that option _-cells_ cannot be used with _-signal_constraints_, as signal I/O
constraints can only be set with guides. And in some cases, such as specifying
one cell to check for signal pads order, it does not make sense.
```
-power_constraints
```

Checks if there are power pads violating constraints set by
_set_power_io_constraints_ . Power I/O constraints include share, ratio, spacing
and offset.

Note that option _-cells_ cannot be used with _-power_constraints_, as power I/O
constraints can only be set with guides. And in some cases, such as specifying
one cell to check for power pads ratio, it does not make sense.
```
-unplaced
```

Checks if there are any unplaced pads. If this option is specified by itself, all
pads are checked if it is unplaced. If other types of cells are specified, such as
fillers, those cells are still checked but with a warning indicating those cells are
not pads. If no cells are specified, by default only all pads are checked.




```
-flipping
```

Checks if the I/O pads are consistent with the is_flipped attribute as set in the
design. If a pad is not placed on any guide, the pad is also considered to violate
placement.
```
-gap
```

Checks if there is a gap between any two adjacent cells on I/O guides. The
unfilled space that is outside the length of the I/O guides are not considered as
gap. The valid cell types include pads, corners, fillers and break cells.
```
-min_pitch
```

Checks if the min_pitch set with I/O guides are honored by place_io.

**Description**

This command performs one or multiple kinds of I/O placement checks and return
a collection of cells with violations. All options are optional. If no option is used, the
command runs all checks. As each checking has different valid objects and options to
work with, each check finds the valid objects for the check within the specified objects.
Each check ignores the options that specify invalid objects. If the objects specified by an
option is not valid for any checking, a warning is issued to indicate the option is not used.

By default, the reports of checks are printed to the console. Each check is written out in
a section in report and each section can shows 10 lines of violations at most. You can
choose to write out the complete report to files or a directory with options.

**Examples**

The following example checks bump assignment for all bumps and signal I/O constraints
for specified guides.
```
prompt> check_io_placement -bump_assignment -signal_constraints
-io_guides [get_io_guides *]

```

**See Also**

 - create_io_guide

 - create_matching_type

 - place_io

 - set_power_io_constraints

 - set_signal_io_constraints




###### **check_isolation_coverage**

Reports isolation violations, that are not handled between power domain boundaries in a
UPF design.

**Syntax**

status _check_isolation_coverage_
```
-dft_signals
[-from power_domain_name_list ]
[-to power_domain_name_list ]
[-clamp_value clamp_value_list ]
[-ignore_unimplemented_strategies]
[-suggest_domain_based]
```

**Data Types**
```
power_domain_name_list  list
clamp_value_list     list
```

**Arguments**
```
-dft_signals
```

Restrict the report to only check logic signal paths involving DFT signal pins.

The following are the supported DFT signal types: scan_clock, scan_in,
scan_out, scan_in_out, scan_enable, test_mode, input_wrp_shift,
output_wrp_shift, wrp_shift, wrp_clock, wrp_ded_capture_in,
wrp_ded_capture_out, wrp_ded_capture_inout, wrp_td_test, wrp_safe_in,
wrp_safe_out, pse_clock, los_pipeline_enable, test_point_clock,
test_point_test_mode.
```
-from power_domain_name_list
```

Restrict the report to only show isolation violations where the driver is located
in one of the power domains named in _power_domain_name_list_ . All domain
names included in _power_domain_name_list_ are required to references an
existing power domain in the design.
```
-to power_domain_name_list
```

Restrict the report to only show isolation violations where the sink is located
in one of the power domains named in _power_domain_name_list_ . All domain
names included in _power_domain_name_list_ are required to references an
existing power domain in the design.
```
-clamp_value clamp_value_list
```

Restrict the report to only show applicable isolation strategies that match
the one the clamp values listed in _clamp_value_list_ . Values allowed for




_clamp_value_list_ are: 1, 0, latch, all. A value "all" is equivalent to {1, 0, latch} and
is the default assumed if _-clamp_value_ is not used.
```
-ignore_unimplemented_strategies
```

This option causes the tool to ignore unimplemented isolation strategies when
evaluating if a signal path has an isolation violation.
```
-suggest_domain_based
```

set_dft_isolation strategy suggestions use -dft_target_domain/dft_source_domain instead of -dft_sink_supply/-dft_source_supply

**Description**

The _check_isolation_coverage_ command reports logic signal paths containing isolation
violations that are not handled, that is, signal paths that:

\- Contain at least one power domain boundary crossing between the driver and the load

where the violation is found."

\- No isolation strategy is found to be defined (either implemented or yet to be
implemented)

on any of the domain boundaries in between the driver and load. Note that a
signal path with an applied isolation strategy whose isolation supply cannot drive
its loads, is still considered as "covered" by said isolation strategy.

The report consists of several section tables, each one corresponding to a
'driver power domain' and "load power domain" pair containing:

\- Driver power domain info

Information about the 'driver power domain', including: domain name, primary
supplies and available secondary supplies.

\- Load power domain info

Information about the 'load power domain', including: domain name, primary
supplies and available secondary supplies.

\- Violating paths info

Information about the logic signal paths found to contain an isolation violation
that is not handled, between its driver and its loads. The driver is expected to
reside inside the 'driver power domain' and its loads are expected to reside
inside the 'load power domain'




\- Applicable isolation strategies from the 'driver power domain'.

Details of existing isolation strategies in the 'driver power domain' found to be
usable to address some of the isolation violations found on the reported signal
paths.

\- Applicable isolation strategies from the 'load power domain'.

Details of existing isolation strategies in the 'load power domain' found to be
usable to address some of the isolation violations found on the reported signal
paths.

By default, section tables for all 'driver power domain' to 'load power domain'
pairs where isolation violations that are not handled are detected and included
in the report. You can make use of the _-from_ and _-to_ options to control which
section tables are shown.

**Examples**

The following command generates a report that includes all signal paths with an isolation
violation not covered by an existing isolation strategy.
```
prompt> check_isolation_coverage -dft_signals
```

The following command filters out any violating signal path whose global driver is not
located on either power domain PD1 or PD2.
```
prompt> check_isolation_coverage -dft_signals -from {PD1 PD2}
```

The report generated by this command only shows available isolation strategies with a
clamp value of 0.
```
prompt> check_isolation_coverage -dft_signals -clamp_value {0}

```

**See Also**

 - commit_dft_isolation

 - set_dft_isolation

 - set_isolation

###### **check_legality**

Checks the legality of the current placement.

**Syntax**

status _check_legality_




```
[-verbose]
[-cells list_of_cells ]
[-chipfinishing auto ]
[-check_distance distance ]
[-cell_violation]
[-info_violation]
[-max_info number ]
[-output_tcl]
```

**Data Types**
```
list_of_cells  collection
mode      string
distance    float
number     integer
```

**Arguments**
```
-verbose
```

Prints a detailed report of all possible violations. By default, the command
reports only a summary of all violations.
```
-cells list_of_cells
```

Specifies the cells to check.

When you use this option, the _check_legality_ command performs legality check
only on the specified cells and cells within the checking distance, which reduces
runtime.

By default, the checking distance is three row heights. To adjust the checking
distance, use the _-check_distance_ option.
```
-chipfinishing auto
```

Specifies the chipfinishing mode to check.

When you use the option, the _check_legality_ command performs legality check
for chipfinish stage. (advanced legalizer only)

The _chipfinishing auto_ checks basic rules such as _overlap_, _cell_on_site_, and
_legal_orient_, and AL rules such as _spacing_rule_, and chipfinishing rules such as
_tap_coverage_, _continuity_ and so on.
```
-check_distance distance
```

Specifies the checking distance in number row heights. The specified distance
must be a float value greater than or equal to zero.

The checking distance determines the neighboring cells to include in legality
checking when you use the _-cells_ option.




By default, the distance is three row heights.

This option can be used only with the _-cells_ option.
```
-cell_violation
```

The command will return all violated cells as a collection. You can assign the
return value of the check_legality command to a TCL variable to process the
collection of violated cells.
```
-info_violation
```

The command will return a TCL list of all violations. You can assign the return
value of the check_legality command to a TCL variable. The option _-max_info_
can be used to limit the number of returned violations.
```
-max_info number
```

Limits the number of returned violations from option _-info_violation_ .
```
-output_tcl
```

Writes a Tcl file that contains all illegal cells with different violation types. The
current process ID (pid) is appended to the file name so the tool can determine if
the Tcl file was created in this session.

This option applies only to the classic legalizer. When the advanced legalizer
is enabled (the _place.legalize.enable_advanced_legalizer_ application option is
_true_ ), the command does not write a Tcl file. Instead, the command writes an
error file that you can view in the GUI error browser.

By default, no Tcl file is generated.

If you are using the classic legalizer and you use this option, by default, the
generated Tcl file contains all moveable cells with violations. You can change
this by modifying two variables in the Tcl file, GLOBAL_VIOLATION_TYPE and
GLOBAL_VIOLATION_MODE. For information about the valid values for these
variables, see the header section at the beginning of the Tcl file.

You can use the generated Tcl file for different purposes, such as

   - Fixing violations based on a specific violation type rather than all violation
types. For example, use this file to select only overlapped cells and leave
other violations as-is.

   - Highlighting all violated cells or specific types of violations and avoid parsing
the output of the _check_legality -verbose_ command.




   - Selecting violated cells based on moveable, application fixed, or fixed
type. For example, you can select only CTS spacing violations marked as
application fixed.

   - Using the script information with your own scripts after the collection is
created. The generated collection can be used with your own scripts.

**Description**

The _check_legality_ command checks the legality of the current placement and output a
report of violation statistics.

By default, the command runs the classic legalizer. To run the advanced legalizer, set the
_place.legalize.enable_advanced_legalizer_ application option to _true_ .

The reported violations can be classified as

 - Cells that are not on rows

 - Cells overlapping each other

 - Cells overlapping blockages

 - Cells with orientation that is not allowed for the row on which the cell is placed

 - Cells with a core site type not equal to that of the row on which the cell is placed

 - Cells with power strap violations

 - Cells with advanced technology (20 nm and below) violations

 - Cells with placement spacing rule violations

**Multicorner-Multimode Support**

This command has no dependency on scenario-specific information.

**Examples**

The following example checks the legality of all cells and prints a summary of all violations.
```
prompt> check_legality
```

The following example checks all BUF* cells in the design.
```
prompt> check_legality -cells [get_cells BUF*]
```

The following example checks cells in the my_cell_list collection.
```
prompt> check_legality -cells $my_cell_list
```

The following example checks cells added in the my_cell_list collection and cells within 5.5
row heights.




```
prompt> check_legality -cells $my_cell_list -check_distance 5.5
```

The following example checks all BUF* cells in the design using the default three row
height checking distance and writes out a Tcl file including all violated cells.
```
prompt> check_legality -cells [get_cells BUF*] -output_tcl
```

The following example checks chipfinishing related rules.
```
prompt> check_legality -chipfinishing auto
```

The following example returns a collection of violated cells.
```
prompt> set violated_cells [check_legality -cell_violation]

```

**See Also**

 - create_placement

 - legalize_placement

 - place.legalize.enable_advanced_legalizer

###### **check_legalizer_sanity**

Does a series of sanity checks on the design to handle dirty data input.

**Syntax**

status _check_legalizer_sanity_

**Description**

The _check_legalizer_sanity_ command performs a series of sanity checks on the current
design (eg. - testing the library, user input design constraints) to avoid legalizer issues.

Running this command before running legalize_placement helps user identify dirty (bad
design) inputs that might cause issues like long runtime or hang later, beforehand. The
output generated is in the form of Error/Warning messages.

This command helps the user to save time by debugging the cause before legalization
runs into problems at later stages; and decide how to proceed.

**Examples**

The following example runs the _check_legalizer_sanity_ command:
```
prompt> check_legalizer_sanity

```



**See Also**

 - check_legality

###### **check_libcell_pin_access**

Check pin accessibility between abutted standard cells for the reference libraries of current
library.

**Syntax**
```
status check_libcell_pin_access
-mode analyze_lib_cell | analyze_lib_pin | single_cell |
single_cell_vertical | cell_by_cell | design_under_test |
congested_random_placement | composite_cell
[-from prepare | place | report_place | route | report_route]
[-to prepare | place | report_place | route | report_route]
```

**Arguments**
```
-mode analyze_lib_cell | analyze_lib_pin | single_celll |
single_cell_vertical | cell_by_cell | design_under_test |
congested_random_placement | composite_cell
```

Specifies the checking mode with different analyzing methods or different cell
combinations.

This is a required argument.

   - _analyze_lib_cell_ :

Creates a fake design with all or the specified library cells and runs
_analyze_lib_cell_placement_ command, which tests a collection of library cells
for their ability to be placed in the current floorplan. It reports a pass rate for
each library cell tested.

No cell placement and routing is performed in this mode. Uses this mode to
detect problematic cells before legalization and to avoid long runtime or hang
issue in early stage due to certain cells are hard to find a legal location.

   - _analyze_lib_pin_ :

Creates a fake design with all or the specified library cells, legalize them, and
then runs _report_cell_pin_access_ command, which reports number of access
points for pins of each library cell. The report will reflect current settings for
the _place.legalize.advanced_layer_access_check_ application option.

In the end of run, the tool generates a report file called
risky_pin_access_[pin_extMode].rpt and prints script in the report to list the




cells with potential pin access issue. The extension mode can be set by the
_pin_check.analyze.report_cell_pin_access_mode_ application option.

- _single_cell_ :

Performs fast checking on the target cell to against the cell itself and ensures
there is no pin accessibility issue within a cell itself. The target cells can be
set by the _pin_check.input.cells_ application option.

A separate block is generated for each target cell, named single_cell/
cell_[refCellName].design. This mode considers horizontal cell abutment,
here is an example of target cell A to against itself.
```
 +---+---+---+ +---+---+---+
 | A | A | A | | A | A | A |
 +---+---+---+ +---+---+---+
```

- _single_cell_vertical_ :

Performs fast checking on the target cell to against the cell itself and ensures
there is no pin accessibility issue within a cell itself. The target cells can be
set by the _pin_check.input.cells_ application option.

A separate block is generated for each target cell, named
single_cell_vertical/cell_[refCellName].design. This mode considers vertical
cell abutment, here is an example of target cell A to against itself.
```
 +---+
 | A |
 +---+
 | A |
 +---+
 | A |
 +---+
 +---+
 | A |
 +---+
 | A |
 +---+
 | A |
 +---+
```

- _cell_by_cell_ :

Checks the target cell to against other cells in the reference libraries.
This mode is easy to isolate one cell against all the other cells at a time.
The against cells can be set by the _pin_check.input.include_for_checking_
application option.




A separate block is generated for each target cell, named cell_by_cell/
cell_[refCellName].design. The horizontal cell abutment for target cell A to
against cell B, C ... is like below.
```
 +---+---+---+ +---+---+---+  +-----+---+-----+
 +-----+---+-----+
 | B | A | B | | B | A | B |  | C | A | C | | C | A |
 C | ...
 +---+---+---+ +---+---+---+  +-----+---+-----+
 +-----+---+-----+
```

Cells that are checked against the target cell can be filtered by pin count.
The control is by the _pin_check.input.filter_cells_by_pin_count_ application
option.

Or cells can be enumerated and instantiated in multiples per target cell. (The
control is only for congested_random_placement mode.) The control is by
the _pin_check.input.checking_multiplier_ application option.

Here is an example with checking_multiplier 2.
```
 +---+---+---+ +---+---+---+
 | B | A | B | | B | A | B |
 +---+---+---+ +---+---+---+  ...
 | B |  | B | | B |  | B |
 +---+  +---+ +---+  +---+
```

- _design_under_test_ :

Surrounds the target cell by other cells, which are placed with minimum
placement spacing rules. This mode considers both horizontal and vertical
cell abutment.

A separate block is generated for each target cell, named design_under_test/
cell_[refCellName].design. The cell abutment for target cell A to against cell
B, ... is like below.
```
 +---+---+---+
 | B | B | B |
 +---+---+---+
 | B | A | B |  ...
 +---+---+---+
 | B | B | B |
 +---+---+---+
```

User can create multiple copies of the DUT cell by the
_pin_check.place.design_under_test_multiplier_ application option. Here is an
example with design_under_test_multiplier 2.
```
 +---+---+---+---+
 | B | B | B | B |

```



```
   +---+---+---+---+
   | B | A | A | B |  ...
   +---+---+---+---+
   | B | B | B | B |
   +---+---+---+---+
```

   - _congested_random_placement_ :

Provides additional routing and horizontal/vertical adjacent cells into the test
design. User can set the connectivity across cells from all directions by the
_pin_check.common.random_netlist_ application option.

A separate block is generated for each target cell, named
congested_random_placement/cell_[refCellName].design. The target cells
A are spreaded in the design as below, and the other checking cells are
randomly added surrounding A in the design.
```
   A  A  A
   A  A  A  A  A
   A  A  A  A  A
   A  A  A  A  A
   A  A  A
```

   - _composite_cell_ :

Provides composite cells into the test design for analysis. User can specifies
number of cells by instance count or cell ratio and control the routing
complex by the pin distance and fanout factor to simulate the real case.
These are the application options provided for this mode:
```
   pin_check.analyze.composite_cells
   pin_check.analyze.composite_inst_count
   pin_check.analyze.composite_cell_ratio
   pin_check.analyze.composite_core_width
   pin_check.analyze.composite_core_height
   pin_check.analyze.composite_pin_dist
   pin_check.analyze.composite_fanout_num
```

After checking, the command reports the cell instance count and DRC for
each library cell. It provides a score to predict cell routability based on the
equation, score = [1 - (DRC count / Instance count)] * 100 The DRC issue
cells in the report will be reviewed by user.
```
-from prepare | place | report_place | route | report_route
```

Specifies the starting step for pin accessibility checking. The default value is
"prepare".




For a new design library, user can only start from "prepare" step.

For an existing design library, user can start from next step of current state.
```
  - If the test design is prepared already, user can start from
  "place".
  - If the test design is placed already, user can start from
  "report_place" or "route".
  - If the test design is routed already, user can start from
  "report_route".
```

User can also start from the step ahead the existing state to overwrite current
result.

The option is ignored when _-mode_ is analyze_lib_cell or analyze_lib_pin.
```
-to prepare | place | report_place | route | report_route
```

Specifies the ending step for pin accessibility checking. The default value is
"report_route".

User can stop at any step behind the _-from_ step.
```
  - When the command is ending at "prepare", the test design is
  prepared and saved.
  - When the command is ending at "place" or "report_place", the
  test design is placed and saved.
  - When the command is ending at "route" or "report_route", the
  test design is routed and saved.
```

The option is ignored when _-mode_ is analyze_lib_cell or analyze_lib_pin.

**Description**

The _check_libcell_pin_access_ command checks the reference libraries pin accessibility
between abutted standard cells.

The recommanded flow for the pin accessibility checking is as below.
```
(1) Baseline cell analysis.
# Analyzes the library cells for the ability to be placed.
check_libcell_pin_access -mode analyze_lib_cell
# Analyzes the routability by pin access check and finds the risky
cells.
check_libcell_pin_access -mode analyze_lib_pin
(2) Baseline checks for risky cells.
set_app_options -as_user_default -name pin_check.input.cells -value
$riskyCells
# simple check

```



```
check_libcell_pin_access -mode single_cell
# check against all other cells
check_libcell_pin_access -mode cell_by_cell
(3) Multidimensional checks.
check_lib_cell_pin_access -mode design_under_test
check_lib_cell_pin_access -mode congested_random_placement
```

The command has five steps in the full checking process.
```
- "prepare": Creates test design for each target cell and generates cell
combination and netlist.
- "place": Initializes the floorplan and performs cell placement and
legalization.
- "report_place": Performs check_legality and reports the ligalization
errors.
- "route": Performs routing commands, such as route_auto, route_detail
or route_eco .
- "report_route": Performs check_routes and reports the routing DRC.
```

The command uses the _pin_check.*_ application options to control the whole checking flow,
including six categories.
```
pin_check.input.* : setting for target cells, excluding cells, against
cells, cell filter
 pin_check.common.* : general setting such as tech_node, netlist,
parallel control, PG routing, ...
 pin_check.analyze.* : setting for -mode analyze_lib_cell,
analyze_lib_pin and composite_cell
 pin_check.place.* : setting for placement and legalization
 pin_check.route.* : setting for routing
 pin_check.report.* : setting for signoff_check_drc and derive cell
spacing constraints
```

The command supports GRD-based parallel P&R.
```
set_app_options -as_user_default -name pin_check.common.grd -value true
set_app_options -as_user_default -name pin_check.common.grd_command
-value $grdCmd
set_app_options -as_user_default -name
pin_check.common.num_cells_per_run -value 20
or
set_app_options -as_user_default -name pin_check.common.num_jobs -value
10
```

The command supports PG routing before or after placement, or user can specify the PG
script file.




```
set_app_options -as_user_default -name pin_check.common.route_pg -value
before_placement
set_app_options -as_user_default -name pin_check.common.pg_script_file
-value $pgFile
```

**Limitations**

Current library must exist and which is created by command _create_pin_check_lib_ .

**Examples**

Example 1) Run pin accessibility checking in one run for all library cells. The preplaced
option file is required for placement.
```
prompt> set_app_options -as_user_default \\
-name pin_check.place.preplace_option_file -value
preplace_options.tcl
prompt> create_pin_check_lib myTestLib -technology a.tf -ref_libs STD
prompt> check_libcell_pin_access -mode cell_by_cell
```

Example 2) Run pin accessibility checking in multiple jobs. Each job runs 5 cells in placing
and routing.
```
prompt> set_app_options -as_user_default -name
pin_check.common.num_cells_per_run -value 5
prompt> set_app_options -as_user_default \\
-name pin_check.place.preplace_option_file -value
preplace_options.tcl
prompt> open_lib myTestLib
prompt> check_libcell_pin_access -mode cell_by_cell
```

Example 3) Reroute violated nets in cells with DRC violations.
```
prompt> set_app_options -as_user_default \\
-name pin_check.route.reroute_drc_cells_only -value true
prompt> open_lib myTestLib
prompt> check_libcell_pin_access -mode cell_by_cell -from route
```

Example 4) Report DRC on all routed cells.
```
prompt> open_lib myTestLib
prompt> check_libcell_pin_access -mode cell_by_cell -from report_route
```

Example 5) Derives cell spacing constraints.
```
prompt> set_app_options -as_user_default \\
-name pin_check.report.derive_cell_spacing_constraints -value
cell_spc_rules.tcl
prompt> open_lib myTestLib
prompt> check_libcell_pin_access -mode cell_by_cell -from report_route
```

Example 6) Update placement for the DRC cells with the derived cell spacing file.




```
prompt> set_app_options -as_user_default \\
-name pin_check.place.cell_spacing_rule_file -value
cell_spc_rules.tcl
prompt> open_lib myTestLib
prompt> check_libcell_pin_access -mode cell_by_cell -from place

```

**See Also**

 - create_pin_check_lib

 - translate_pin_check_ui

###### **check_license**

Checks the availability of the specified license feature.

**Syntax**

status _check_license_
```
feature_name
[-quiet]
```

**Data Types**
```
feature_name   string
```

**Arguments**
```
feature_name
```

Feature name to be checked for existence in the license server.
```
-quiet
```

Do not print any error message if the check failed.

**Description**

The _check_license_ command checks for the existence of the feature in the license server.
It does not check out the license feature. If the feature exists on the server, the command
returns 1. Otherwise, the command prints an error message and returns 0. The printing of
this message can be suppressed via _-quiet_ option.

The _list_licenses_ command provides a list of the features that are currently checked out.

**Examples**

This example checks the availability of the Fusion-Compiler-AG license feature:
```
prompt> check_license Fusion-Compiler-AG
1

```

###### **check_lvs**

Checks for inconsistencies in the physical layout of the current design.

**Syntax**

status _check_lvs_
```
[-nets collection_of_nets ]
[-checks {short open floating_routes all}]
[-max_errors maximum_number_of_errors ]
[-check_child_cells true | false]
[-exclude_child_cell_types exclude_types ]
[-check_zero_spacing_blockages true | false]
[-check_top_level_blockages true | false]
[-open_reporting { bounding_box | detailed }]
[-report_floating_pins true | false]
[-treat_terminal_as_voltage_source true | false]
[-ignore_filler_cells true | false]
[-filler_cell_name_prefix specific_filler_cell_name ]
```

**Data Types**
```
collection_of_nets     collection
maximum_number_of_errors  integer
exclude_types        list
specific_filler_cell_name  string
```

**Arguments**
```
-nets collection_of_nets
```

Specifies the nets to check. By default, all nets are checked.
```
-checks {short open floating_routes all}
```

Specifies the types of errors to check as follows:

   - _short:_ check for shorts between nets.

   - _open:_ check for open nets.

   - _floating_routes:_ check if any floating routes exist.

   - _all:_ check all error types above




By default, all error types are checked.
```
-max_errors maximum_number_of_errors
```

Specifies the maximum number of errors for each type of violations specified
with the _-checks_ option. Set the value to 0 to specify an unlimited error count.
The default is 20.
```
-check_child_cells true | false
```

Specifies whether to check shorts between child cells and top-level shapes. If
true, all shapes in child cells are checked. The default is true.
```
-exclude_child_cell_types { exclude_types }
```

Specifies cell types to ignore when checking shorts between child cell and
top-level shapes. Specify one or more of the following cell types: _abstract_,
_analog_, _black_box_, _corner_, _cover_, _diode_, _end_cap_, _fill_, _filler_, _flip_chip_driver_,
_flip_chip_pad_, _lib_cell_, _macro_, _module_, _pad_, _pad_spacer_, _physical_only_, and
_well_tap_ .

You must specify the _-check_child_cells_ option with this option.
```
-check_zero_spacing_blockages true | false
```

Specifies whether to check shorts on zero spacing blockages. The default is
false.
```
-check_top_level_blockages true | false
```

Specifies whether to check shorts on top-level blockages. The default is true.
```
-open_reporting { bounding_box | detailed }
```

Specifies how open violations are shown in the error browser.

   - _bounding_box:_ Report bounding box of open net

   - _detailed:_ Report the detailed open locations in the error browser; it might
require longer runtime to find detailed open locations

When the number of connected components of an open net is more than 100
and the _-open_reporting_ option is set to _detailed_, 100 approximated open
locations will be reported. The default is bounding_box.
```
-report_floating_pins true | false
```

Specifies whether to report floating pins when checking open or floating_routes
violations. The default is false.
```
-treat_terminal_as_voltage_source true | false
```

When set to true, the check_lvs command assumes that all terminals of pg nets
are voltage sources. The default is false.




```
-ignore_filler_cells true | false
```

Specifies whether to ignore the filler cell checking. The default is false.
```
-filler_cell_name_prefix specific_filler_cell_name
```

Specifies different prefix in "create_stdcell_fillers". The default name of
filler_cell_name_prefix is same as the prefix in create_stdcell_fillers. If you don’t
specify different prefix in "create_stdcell_fillers", you don’t need to specify "filler_cell_name_prefix" in check_lvs.

**Description**

The _check_lvs_ command detects physical layout versus schematic errors. Violations
discovered by the checker are available as an error set for browsing with the GUI error
browser.

The command can use multiple CPU cores to generate the report based on the
_set_host_options -max_cores_ command setting. If this value is not set, the command runs
on a single core.

The command generates an error file named "block_name"_lvs.err. To view the errors on
GUI, load the error file by using the Error Browser. Users could also get information of
errors by get_drc_errors and get_drc_error_types.

**Multicorner-Multimode Support**

This command has no dependency on scenario-specific information.

**Examples**

The following example reports shorts, opens, and floating route violations for all nets in the
design.
```
prompt> check_lvs
```

The following example reports only short violations for all nets in the design.
```
prompt> check_lvs -checks short
```

The following example reports short, and open violations for net N1, N2, and N3.
```
prompt> check_lvs -nets {N1 N2 N3} -checks {short open}
```

The following example reports short violations without checking shapes in child cell.
```
prompt> check_lvs -checks short -check_child_cells false
```

The following example reports open violations in detail on error browser.
```
prompt> check_lvs -checks open -open_reporting detailed
```

The following example reports short violations without checking for filler cell.




```
prompt> check_lvs -checks short -ignore_filler_cells true
The following example shows the way to get information of errors by
get_drc_errors and get_drc_error_type command after executing check_lvs.

prompt> check_lvs -checks open
prompt> set error_data $design_lvs.err
prompt> set data [open_drc_error_data $error_data]
prompt> #get number of open nets
prompt> sizeof_collection [get_drc_errors -of_objects
[get_drc_error_types -error_data $data "Open"] -error_data $data]
prompt> #get name of the open nets
prompt> get_attribute [get_drc_errors -of_objects [get_drc_error_types
-error_data $data "Open"] -error_data $data] objects

```

**See Also**

 - check_routes

 - set_host_options

 - get_drc_errors

 - get_drc_error_types

###### **check_macro_pin_access**

Check pin accessibility between abutted macro/pad related type cells for the reference
libraries of current library.

**Syntax**
```
status check_macro_pin_access
-mode horizontal | vertical
[-from prepare | place | report_place | route | report_route]
[-to prepare | place | report_place | route | report_route]
```

**Data Types**
```
NA
```

**Arguments**
```
-mode horizontal | vertical
```

Specifies the checking mode with different cell abutment direction.




This is a required argument.

   - _horizontal_ :

The targe cells are put in horizontal direction, which can be set by the
_pin_check.input.cells_ application option.

A separate block is generated for each target cell, named "horizontal/
cell_[refCellName].design". Here is an example of target cell A to against
itself.
```
   +---+---+---+ +---+---+---+
   | A | A | A | | A | A | A |
   +---+---+---+ +---+---+---+
```

   - _vertical_ :

The targe cells are put in vertical direction, which can be set by the
_pin_check.input.cells_ application option.

A separate block is generated for each target cell, named "vertical/
cell_[refCellName].design". Here is an example of target cell A to against
itself.
```
   +---+
   | A |
   +---+
   | A |
   +---+
   | A |
   +---+
   +---+
   | A |
   +---+
   | A |
   +---+
   | A |
   +---+
-from prepare | place | report_place | route | report_route
```

Specifies the starting step for pin accessibility checking. The default value is
"prepare".

For a new design library, user can only start from "prepare" step.

For an existing design library, user can start from next step of current state.
```
  - If the test design is prepared already, user can start from
  "place".
  - If the test design is placed already, user can start from
  "report_place" or "route".

```



```
  - If the test design is routed already, user can start from
  "report_route".
```

User can also start from the step ahead the existing state to overwrite current
result.

The option is ignored when _-mode_ is analyze_lib_cell or analyze_lib_pin.
```
-to prepare | place | report_place | route | report_route
```

Specifies the ending step for pin accessibility checking. The default value is
"report_route".

User can stop at any step behind the _-from_ step.
```
  - When the command is ending at "prepare", the test design is
  prepared and saved.
  - When the command is ending at "place" or "report_place", the
  test design is placed and saved.
  - When the command is ending at "route" or "report_route", the
  test design is routed and saved.
```

**Description**

The _check_macro_pin_access_ command performs pin accessibility checking on the target
cell to against the cell itself in horizonal or vertical cell abutment.

The command supports macro/pad related design types, which are: macro, pad, analog,
block_bbox, flip_chip_pad, flip_chip_driver, abstract, pad_spacer, module.

To control the spacing between abutment cells, please set
_pin_check.place.macro_spacing_ .

The command has five steps in the full checking process.
```
- "prepare": Creates test design for each target cell and generates cell
combination and netlist.
- "place": Initializes the floorplan and performs cell placement and
legalization.
- "report_place": Performs check_legality and reports the ligalization
errors.
- "route": Performs routing commands, such as route_auto, route_detail
or route_eco .
- "report_route": Performs check_routes and reports the routing DRC.
```

The command uses the _pin_check.*_ application options to control the whole checking flow,
including six categories.
```
pin_check.input.* : setting for target cells, excluding cells, against
cells, cell filter
 pin_check.common.* : general setting such as tech_node, netlist,
parallel control, PG routing, ...

```



```
 pin_check.analyze.* : setting for -mode analyze_lib_cell and
analyze_lib_pin
 pin_check.place.* : setting for placement and legalization
 pin_check.route.* : setting for routing
 pin_check.report.* : setting for signoff_check_drc and derive cell
spacing constraints
```

The command supports GRD-based parallel P&R.
```
set_app_options -as_user_default -name pin_check.common.grd -value true
set_app_options -as_user_default -name pin_check.common.grd_command
-value $grdCmd
set_app_options -as_user_default -name
pin_check.common.num_cells_per_run -value 20
or
set_app_options -as_user_default -name pin_check.common.num_jobs -value
10
```

**Limitations**

Current library must exist and which is created by command _create_pin_check_lib_ .

**Examples**

Example 1) Run pin accessibility checking in one run for all library cells. The preplaced
option file is required for placement.
```
prompt> set_app_options -as_user_default \\
-name pin_check.place.preplace_option_file -value
preplace_options.tcl
prompt> create_pin_check_lib myTestLib -technology a.tf -ref_libs MACRO
prompt> check_macro_pin_access -mode vertical
```

Example 2) Run pin accessibility checking in multiple jobs. Each job runs 5 cells in placing
and routing.
```
prompt> set_app_options -as_user_default -name
pin_check.common.num_cells_per_run -value 5
prompt> set_app_options -as_user_default \\
-name pin_check.place.preplace_option_file -value
preplace_options.tcl
prompt> open_lib myTestLib
prompt> check_macro_pin_access -mode vertical
```

Example 3) Reroute violated nets in cells with DRC violations.
```
prompt> set_app_options -as_user_default \\
-name pin_check.route.reroute_drc_cells_only -value true
prompt> open_lib myTestLib
prompt> check_macro_pin_access -mode vertical -from route
```

Example 4) Report DRC on all routed cells.




```
prompt> open_lib myTestLib
prompt> check_macro_pin_access -mode vertical -from report_route

```

 - create_pin_check_lib

###### **check_mib_alignment**

Checks the alignment of each multiply instantiated block (MIB) instance against power
straps, ground straps, standard cell rows, and wire tracks in the current design.

**Syntax**

int _check_mib_alignment_
```
[-pg]
[-cell_row]
[-wire_tracks]
[-layers layers ]
[-blocks blocks ]
[-verbose]
```

**Data Types**
```
layers collection
blocks collection
```

**Arguments**
```
-pg
```

Checks the alignment of each MIB instance against the power and ground
straps that intersect MIB instances in the current design. If any MIB instances
are not aligned correctly with power and ground straps, the command issues a
warning message with the location of the misalignment.
```
-cell_row
```

Checks the alignment of each MIB instance against standard cell rows and
cell row site which intersect the MIB in the current design. If any MIB instances
are not aligned correctly with cell rows or cell row site, the command issues a
warning message.
```
-wire_tracks
```

Checks the alignment of each MIB instance against wire tracks in the current
design. If any MIB instances are not aligned correctly with wire tracks, the
command issues a warning message.




```
-layers layers
```

Specifies the layers on which to check the alignment of MIB instances against
power straps, ground straps, and wire tracks. This option is used with the _-pg_ or
_-wire_tracks_ options.
```
-blocks blocks
```

Specifies the reference block name to which the MIB instances belong, for
checking the alignment of MIB instances against power straps, ground straps,
and wire tracks.
```
-verbose
```

Prints complete misalignment report for the checked MIB instances. Without this
option, the command prints a compact report (default).

**Description**

This command checks alignment of each MIB instance against power straps, ground
straps, cell rows, and wire tracks respectively or checks all of them without corresponding
options. The misaligned MIB instances cannot be pushed down successfully. Misalignment
messages are reported in GUI->Window->Message Browser Window when EMS
database is created using command create_ems_database.

**Examples**

The following example checks for power and ground strap alignment across all the MIB
instances in the design.
```
prompt> check_mib_alignment -pg -verbose
```

The following example checks for MIB alignment against wire tracks.
```
prompt> check_mib_alignment -wire_tracks -verbose

```

**See Also**

 - push_down_objects

 - report_mibs

###### **check_mib_for_pin_placement**

Checks multiply instantiated block (MIB) instances for potential pin placement issues.

**Syntax**

string _check_mib_for_pin_placement_
```
[-swapped_connections]
[-top_level_terminal_locations]

```



```
[-asymmetric_connections]
[-cells list_of_blocks ]
[-nets net_collection ]
```

**Data Types**
```
list_of_blocks  list
net_collection  collection
```

**Arguments**
```
-swapped_connections
```

Checks and reports pins on MIB instances that do not connect to the
corresponding pins across the instances of the reference block. The check can
be run before and after pin placement. The check is limited to comparing two-pin
nets that connect MIB instances.
```
-top_level_terminal_locations
```

Checks and reports top-level terminals that connect to the same MIB pin, but at
difference locations. The check can be run before and after pin-placement.
```
-asymmetric_connections
```

Checks for pins across MIB instances where the MIB block pin does not connect
to the same number or type of pins (asymmetric pins). The check can be run
before and after pin placement. Unlike the _-swapped_connections_ check, the
_-asymmetric_connections_ check is not limited to two-pin nets that connect two
unique MIB instances. Instead, this check examines all MIB pins in the design
for asymmetry. By definition, swapped connections are a subset of asymmetric
connections. The command skips pins that are connected to tie-high or tie-low
nets. When this option is used the command returns asymmetric connections/
pins as well as pins connected to these asymmetric connections to help with
further analysis.
```
-cells list_of_blocks
```

Specifies a list of blocks or cells for checking. The check considers all the MIB
blocks in the design for checking, but limits reporting and the collection of pins to
the set of blocks specified in the _list_of_blocks_ .
```
-nets net_collection
```

Specifies a collection of nets for mib checking. The check considers all the MIB
blocks in the design for checking, but limits reporting and the returned collection
of pins to those pins that connect to the specified set of nets. If this option is not
specified the command looks at all MIB pins.




**Description**

This command checks and reports potential multiply instantiated block (MIB)
pin placement issues. If an issue is detected, the command returns a collection
of pins with potential problems. The command can be used before or after pin
placement to detect potential issues with MIB pins. You must specify at least one of
_-top_level_terminal_locations_ or _-swapped_connections_ options.

The _set_editability_ can enable/disable this command for blocks or levels of physical
hierarchy. This command has no effect on the blocks that are disabled by _set_editability_ .

MIB pins that are dangling or tied-off are ignored by this command. That is the
comparisons of MIB pin connectivity are limited to those pins that are neither dangling nor
tied off.

**Examples**

The following example checks for swapped MIB pin connections pins on all blocks.
```
prompt> check_mib_for_pin_placement -swapped_connections

```

**See Also**

 - place_pins

 - report_feedthroughs

 - set_editability

###### **check_multibit_library**

Reports the compatible multibit and single bit cells in the library for banking and
debanking.

**Syntax**

status _check_multibit_library_
```
-stage rtl | physical | all
[-banking]
[-debanking]
[-combinational]
[-generate_map_file file_name ]
```

**Arguments**
```
-stage rtl | physical | all
```

Specifies the stage, _rtl_ or _physical_, to report compatible library cells, for RTL or
physical banking and debanking, repectively. The value _all_ reports the library
compatibility information for both RTL and physical multibit stages.




```
-banking
```

Reports all compatible multibit library cells for each single bit library cell for RTL
banking stage, physical banking stage, or both if the value of _-stage_ is specified
to be _rtl_, _physical_, or _all_, respectively.
```
-debanking
```

Reports all compatible single bit library cells for each multibit library cells for
RTL debanking stage, physical debanking stage, or both if the value of _-stage_ is
specified to be _rtl_, _physical_, or _all_, respectively.
```
-combinational
```

Reports all compatible single bit library cells for each combinational multibit cell.
```
-generate_map_file file_name
```

Specifies the name of output file that contains the mapping information. The file
contains a series of function equivalent library cell groups for single bit cells. The
file also contains the mapping of multibit bit-width to the combination of lower
multibit library cells in each function equivalent group.

**Description**

This command lists all the compatible library cells for RTL and/or physical banking
and debanking. The report also includes the reasons of incompatibility. The report lists
the compatible and incompatible multibit library cells for each single bit library cell if
the -banking option is specified. On the other hand, the report lists the compatible and
incompatible single bit library cells for each multibit library cell if -debanking option is
specified.

If the -generate_map_file option is specified, the output file is generated. The output
file contains a collection of the functional equivalent library cells. The output file also
shows how to use the lower multibit library cells to compose a multibit cell whose bit-width
is under 32 for each function equivalent group. The -generate_map_file option is only
applicable for the physical multibit stage.

**Multicorner-Multimode Support**

This command has no dependency on scenario-specific information.

**Examples**

The following example generates a compatible library cells report for RTL banking and
debanking.
```
prompt> check_multibit_library -stage rtl -banking -debanking
****************************************
Report : check_multibit_library
Flow  : RTL BANKING

```



```

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------SB_Reg_Lib1          COMPATIBLE      MB_Reg_Lib1
MB_Reg_Lib2
MB_Reg_Lib3

SB_Reg_Lib2         MISSING ATTRIBUTE   MB_Reg_Lib4
MB_Reg_Lib5
MB_Reg_Lib6

Single-bit With No Multibit Equivalents
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------SB_Reg_Lib3
SB_Reg_Lib4
SB_Reg_Lib5
****************************************
Report : check_multibit_library
Flow  : RTL DEBANKING
****************************************

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------Multibit Lib cell        Compatibility    Single bit Lib cell
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------MB_Reg_Lib1            COMPATIBLE     SB_Reg_Lib1
SB_Reg_Lib2
SB_Reg_Lib3

MB_Reg_Lib2            DONT_USE      SB_Reg_Lib4
SB_Reg_Lib5
SB_Reg_Lib6

Multibit with NO Singlebit Equivalents
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------MB_Reg_Lib3
MB_Reg_Lib4
MB_Reg_Lib5

```



```
The following example generates a compatible library cells report for
physical banking
and generates an output map file.
prompt> check_multibit_library -stage physical -generate map_file.txt
****************************************

of MB_Reg_Lib9 multibit lib cells.

The following example checks the compatible single-bit equivalent cell of
combinational

```
multibit library cells.

combo_sbit_lib_cell2
combo_mbit_lib_cell2       PVT mismatch
combo_sbit_lib_cell3
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------```

**Appendix**

The following table lists the incompatible reasons and the details of the incompatibility.
```
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Reason for Incompatibility  | Comment
|
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| LIB_CELL_EXCLUDE       | The lib cell is excluded by
"set_lib_cell_purpose -exclude" or the attribute "valid_purposes" of lib
cell is not suitable.
|
| DONT_USE           | The lib cell is set to true by the
"set_dont_use" command or the attribute "dont_use" of lib cell is set to
true or the attribute "valid_purposes" of lib cell is not suitable. |
| DONT_TOUCH          | The lib cell is set to true by the
"set_dont_touch" command or the attribute "dont_touch" of lib cell is
set to true.
|
| VOLT_INCOMPATIBLE      | PVT is not consistent for single bit and
multibit library. Please check with the "report_pvt" command.
|
| FRAME_VIEW_DOES_NOT_EXIST  | The lib cell frame view does not exist.
|

```



```
| SITE_HEIGHT_INCOMPATIBLE   | The cell height is incompatible with
site height.
|
| PIN_ORDER_MISMATCH      | Type of pins do not match for mapping
given in "mb_pin_map" attribute of multibit lib cell. Scan pins are
mapped to non-scan pins or vice-versa.                 |
| LIB_ARC_MISMATCH       | Please use "get_lib_timing_arcs" command
to check arc mismatch between single bit and multibit lib cells.
|
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

```

 - identify_multibit

 - split_multibit

###### **check_mv_design**

Checks for violations in a multi-voltage design.

**Syntax**

status _check_mv_design_
```
[-max_message_count message_count ]
[-erc_mode]
[-voltage_threshold threshold ]
[-power_domain]
[-supply]
[-isolation]
[-level_shifter]
[-retention]
[-power_switch]
[-repeater]
[-terminal_boundary]
[-pgmux]
[-diode]
[-model]
[-tieoff]
[-pg_pin]
[-analog]
[-physical_block_pin]
[-signal_pin]
[-pg_netlist]
[-all]
[-interface_only]
[-objects]

```



**Data Types**
```
message_count     integer
threshold       float
```

**Arguments**
```
-max_message_count message_count
```

Sets the maximum number of occurrences for each error type. If you set it to
zero or 'all', that means the number of occurrences of the message is unlimited.
If this option is not specified, the limit is 20 by default.
```
-erc_mode
```

If specified, the command runs in electrical-rule-checking mode and ignores any
UPF strategies specified in the power intent. If this option is not specified, the
command considers UPF strategies.
```
-voltage_threshold threshold
```

Sets the voltage threshold for level shifting violations. If this option is not
specified, the threshold is zero by default.
```
-power_domain
```

Checks power domains of the design. This is optional.
```
-supply
```

Checks supply nets, supply sets and supply ports of the design. This is optional.
```
-isolation
```

Checks isolation strategies, isolation cells, and isolation of the design. This is
optional.
```
-level_shifter
```

Checks level shifter strategies, level shifter cells, and voltage shifting of the
design. This is optional.
```
-retention
```

Checks retention strategies, retention cells of the design. This is optional.
```
-power_switch
```

Checks power switch strategies, switch cells of the design. This is optional.
```
-repeater
```

Checks repeater of the design. This is optional.




```
-terminal_boundary
```

Checks terminal boundaries of the design. This is optional.
```
-pgmux
```

Checks PG MUX of the design. This is optional.
```
-diode
```

Checks diode cells of the design. This is optional.
```
-model
```

Checks models of the design. This is optional.
```
-tieoff
```

Checks tie-off connections of the design. This is optional.
```
-pg_pin
```

Checks PG pin rule of the design. This is optional.
```
-analog
```

Checks analog nets of the design. This is optional.
```
-physical_block_pin
```

Checks physical block pins of the design. This is optional.
```
-signal_pin
```

Checks signal pins of the design. This is optional.
```
-pg_netlist
```

Checks pg nets and power and ground connections of the design. This is
optional.
```
-all
```

Checks all the rules above of the design. This is optional.
```
-interface_only
```

Checks violations related to block boundary interface of current block and subblocks only and other internal violations are excluded. This is optional.
```
-objects
```

This option recieve a list of pins, or ports as input. It checks level shifting and
isolation violations on the paths through the given pins and/or ports. The option
must be specified with one of -level_shifter and -isolation, or both, and it is an
error to specify -objects with the options other than -level_shifter or -isolation.
The same violations will not be reported more than once.




**Description**

The _check_mv_design_ command checks multi-voltage related electrical rules for the
design, and issues error and warning messages as appropriate.

By default, all multi-voltage checks except pg net and pg connection checks are included
unless a specific type of checks or _-all_ option is specified,

###### **check_netlist**

Checks the netlist for any connectivity errors or violations and issues warning messages
accordingly.

**Syntax**

int _check_netlist_
```
[-cells]
[-nets]
[-ports]
[-hierarchical]
[-multiple_designs]
[-summary]
```

**Arguments**
```
-cells
```

Specifies that netlist checks to be performed on cell instances. This option
involves checking the input and output pin connections of the cell instances as
well as the inside connections for hierarchical cell instances.
```
-nets
```

Specifies that netlist checks to be performed on nets. This option involves
checking for drivers, loads and multiple drivers of a net. It also checks if a net is
constant driven or it is three state net.
```
-ports
```

Specifies that netlist checks to be performed on ports. This option involves
checking of the port connections such as whether an output port is being driven,
an input port has a load.
```
-hierarchical
```

Performs the checks on the objects across all levels of physical hierarchy. This
option is FALSE by default.




```
-multiple_designs
```

Reports warning messages related to multiply-instantiated designs.
```
-summary
```

Displays a summary of the warning messages instead of one message per
warning. This does not affect the way error messages are issued.

**Description**

The command checks the design for netlist connectivity errors and any design violations.
This command gives a preliminary information about the state of the netlist and if there are
any potential problems with the netlist. This informs about the potential errors that might
occur during the later stages.

The command performs checks cells/nets/ports based on the options provided. The
command by default performs checks on cells, net and ports. When no option is given, the
_check_netlist_ command performs checks for cells, nets and ports of the top level hierarchy.
If _-hierarchy_ is given, the command would perform the checks across all levels of physical
hierarchy. The option _-multiple_designs_ flags multiple instances of a module. If a module is
instantiated in two different designs, a warning message is issued.

If an open EMS database exists before this command is executed, the messages are
saved to the EMS databse. The Message Browser window in GUI provides a summary of
the number of messages for each check type as well as each individual message.

This command has no dependency on scenario-specific information.

###### **check_objects_for_push_down**

Checks a collection of nets or charging stations for potential problems before running the
_push_down_objects_ command.

**Syntax**

collection _check_objects_for_push_down_




```
object_collection
[-cells cells ]
```

**Data Types**
```
object_collection   collection
cells         collection
```

**Arguments**
```
object_collection
```

Specifies the collection of signal nets or charging stations to be checked. The
collection can only include signal nets or charging stations, but not both. This
option is required.

Only _signal_routing_ objects and charging stations are checked by this command.
The _signal_routing_ objects include wires, paths, vias, via arrays and terminals
that connect to signal nets. The charging stations are non-primary voltage areas
that contain repeater buffers.
```
-cells cells
```

Specifies the block instances to check for pushing down objects. By default, all
blocks are checked for push-down readiness.

**Description**

This command checks signal nets or charging stations for potential issues before pushing
them into blocks with the _push_down_objects_ command. The check returns a collection of
nets or charging stations that might have problems. You can check only one object type,
net or charging station, at a time.

If the command finds no problems with any of the objects passed (nets or charging
stations), the command returns an empty collection. If the command encounters some
problem unrelated to specific checks for objects, the command returns a "0" status rather
than a collection.

When nets or shapes of nets are included in the object collection, this command traverses
the routing and looks for 1) collinear routes and vias, 2) problems with physical routing that
are incompatible with the logical definition of the net, 3) incomplete routing at the top level.

If charging stations are included, the command checks that the voltage area is nonprimary and finds the deepest block that the voltage area overlaps. The depth of hierarchy
that is examined is controlled by the _set_editability_ command. Use this command to define
the range of hierarchy depth or the blocks to check. The command checks if that block has
the necessary UPF objects (PG supply nets) for receiving that voltage area.

This command uses the option settings specified by the _set_push_down_object_options_
command. Set all options for the net or charging station objects that are planned for pushdown before running the _check_objects_for_push_down_ command.




For net routing, the command checks the routing and determines whether feedthrough
ports are required. By default, feedthrough requirements (such as top-level continuity,
and logical-vs-physical consistency of the routing) are not checked unless the command
detects pin constraints for the net that indicate that the _push_down_objects_ command
would be free to allow feedthroughs on the net. If so, and the routing requires a
feedthrough port on the block, feedthrough requirements are checked for the net.

Feedthroughs for nets can be enabled or disabled by the _set_individual_pin_constraints_
_-nets netname -allow_feedthroughs true|false_ command.

**Examples**

The following example checks the routing objects for nets NETA and NETB for potential
push down problems.
```
prompt> check_objects_for_push_down [get_nets {NETA NETB}]
```

The following example checks the charging station named "gas_station" for potential push
down problems.
```
prompt> check_objects_for_push_down [get_voltage_areas gas_station]

```

**See Also**

 - push_down_objects

 - remove_push_down_object_options

 - report_push_down_object_options

 - set_push_down_object_options

 - set_individual_pin_constraints

###### **check_pg_connectivity**

Verifies physical connectivity of the power ground network.

**Syntax**

status _check_pg_connectivity_
```
[-nets pg_nets ]
[-write_connectivity_file file_name ]
[-check_macro_pins one | all | none]
[-check_block_pins one | all | none]
[-check_pad_pins one | all | none]
[-check_std_cell_pins one | all | none]
[-max_floating_cluster_size size ]
[-remove_floating wire | via | all]
[-error_view_name file_name ]

```



**Data Types**
```
pg_nets      collection
file_name     string
size        integer
```

**Arguments**
```
-nets pg_nets
```

Specifies the power ground nets to be checked. By default, the command
checks all power ground nets.
```
-write_connectivity_file file_name
```

Specifies the output file name. If specified, the tool writes detailed net
connectivity information to the file.
```
-check_macro_pins one | all | none
```

Specifies how macro pins are checked for the specified nets. "one" means that a
macro is connected if at least one pin shape of the net is connected. "all" means
that a macro is connected only if all pin shapes of the net are connected. "none"
means that macro pins are not checked. By default, the value is "one".
```
-check_block_pins one | all | none
```

Specifies how block pins are checked for the specified nets. "one" means that a
block is connected if at least one pin shape of the net is connected. "all" means
that a block is connected only if all pin shapes of the net are connected. "none"
means that block pins are not checked. By default, the value is "all".
```
-check_pad_pins one | all | none
```

Specifies how pad pins are checked for the specified nets. "one" means that a
pad is connected if at least one pin shape of the net is connected. "all" means
that a pad is connected only if all pin shapes of the net are connected. "none"
means that pad pins are not checked. By default, the value is "one".
```
-check_std_cell_pins one | all | none
```

Specifies how std cell pins are checked for the specified nets. "one" means
that a std cell is connected if at least one pin shape of the net is connected.
"all" means that a std cell is connected only if all pin shapes of the net are
connected. "none" means that std cell pins are not checked. By default, the
value is "one".
```
-remove_floating wire | via | all
```

Specifies how to remove the floating vias and wires identified by this command.
If a floating via or wire belongs to a via matrix or shape pattern, then the
occupancy position of the via or wire in the corresponding via matrix or shape
pattern are set empty. "wire" means that all the floating wires should be




removed. "via" means that all the floating vias should be removed. "all" means
that all the floating wires and vias should be removed. By default, the floating
vias and wires will not be removed if this option is not set.
```
-max_floating_cluster_size size
```

Specify the maximum size of floating cluster to be returned by the command and
reported by the error browser.
```
-error_view_name file_name
```

Specifies the error view name. If not specified, the default error view name will
be "[block_name]_floatingPG.err".

**Description**

This command checks the physical connectivity of the power ground network. The
command generates information for floating wires, vias, pads, macro pins, and standard
cell pins. Those wires/vias of disjoint groups are all floating objects. The information can
be viewed by using the error browser. More detailed info can also be written to a file. The
command also returns a collection of floating vias and wires. If some of the floating vias
and wires belong to via matrixes and shape patterns, the corresponding via matrix and
shape pattern objects will be returned. Use the -remove_floating option to remove the
floating vias and wires.

**Examples**

The following example checks the connectivity of the VSS net, and checks whether all
macro power ground pins are connected to the network.
```
prompt> check_pg_connectivity -nets VSS -check_macro_pins all

```

**See Also**

 - check_pg_missing_vias

 - compile_pg

 - connect_pg_net

###### **check_pg_drc**

Verifies and reports technology routing design rules violations and illegal overlaps of PG
