 - compute_area

 - compute_polygons

 - resize_polygons

 - split_polygons

 - get_shapes

 - transform_polygons

###### **copy_useful_skew**

Copies useful skew to newly added scenarios for consistent timing reports.

**Syntax**

status _copy_useful_skew_
```
[-no_user_bp]
```

**Arguments**
```
-no_user_bp
```

Ignore user-defined delay balance points when copying.

**Description**

When a pin has CTS balance point offsets defined in only a subset of the active scenarios,
the command copies the offset to the scenarios where the offset is missing. To do so, the
average value of the offset, scaled to the CTS reference corner, is computed across all




scenarios where a balance point offset is defined, and that value is scaled back in each
active scenario using the scaling factor of the scenario corner. The command also ensures
that corresponding set_clock_latency constraints are set on all pins and scenarios where
a new offset value is computed. Flow commands such as place_opt or compile_fusion
run this command under the hood in order to ensure that previously defined offsets are
available across all active scenarios. Use this command after enabling new scenarios
when you want to generate timing or QoR reports using commands which do not call
copy_useful_skew under-the-hood, like report_timing.


**See Also**

 - place_opt

 - compile_fusion

 - report_timing

###### **cputime**

Retrieves the overall user time associated with the current process.

**Syntax**

float _get_cputime_
```
[-all]
[-format]
string format
```

**Arguments**
```
all
```

If specified then it gives cpu time for this process and it's children.
```
format
```

This argument takes a _printf_ style formatting string for a floating point number.

**Description**

The _get_cputime_ command returns the accumulated user time, in seconds, for the current
process. If the _format_ string is omitted, an integer number of seconds is returned. If
the format string is specified, a floating point number is returned. The number includes
fractions of a second elapsed and is formatted in accordance with given specifier. Refer
to the Unix man page for _printf_ for a detailed description of how to format a floating point
argument.




```
prompt> get_cputime "%g"
3.74

```

**See Also**

 - get_mem

###### **create_3d_mirror_bumps**

Copies and places bumps and bump clusters or bond pads from the source die to the
target die.

**Syntax**

status _create_3d_mirror_bumps_
```
-from source_chip_name
-to target_chip_name
[-ref_cell lib_cell ]
[-prefix prefix_name ]
[-bumps bump_list ]
[-cluster_bump_mapping pattern_cell_pair_list ]
[-bond_pad]
[-bond_pad_list bond_pad_list ]
[-pins pin_list ]
[-bump_region]
[-bump_region_list bump_region_list ]
[-pseudo_bump_list pseudo_bump_list ]
[-to_bump_region bump_region_list ]
[-force]
[-strip_away_prefix prefix_name ]
[-bond_pad_def bond_pad_def_name ]
[-bump_cluster_list edit_group_list ]
[-no_snap]
[-skip_physical_check]
[-use_port_names]
[-top_nets net_list ]
[-group_to_one]
[-offset offset ]
[-naming_style format_list ]
[-propagate_user_attributes]
[-boundary boundary_spec ]
```

**Data Types**
```
source_chip_name     string
target_chip_name     string
lib_cell         string
prefix_name       string
bump_list        list
pattern_cell_pair_list  list

```



```
pin_list         list
bond_pad_list      list
bump_region_list     list
pseudo_bump_list     list
bond_pad_def_name    string
edit_group_list     collection
net_list         collection
offset          float_pair
format_list       string
boundary_spec      float
```

**Arguments**
```
-from source_chip_name
```

Specifies the source chip or sub-block in chip as a master die. This option is
required.
```
-to target_chip_name
```

Specifies the target chip or sub-block in chip as a slave die. This option is
required.
```
-ref_cell lib_cell
```

Specifies the library cell or design_block. The cmd will search the ref_cell
from target die's library and reference libraries, if there are multiple lib_cell or
design_block in different reference libraries have the same name, please specify
full design name to ease the ambiguity. This option is required for bump and
cannot be specified with the _-bond_pad_ option.
```
-prefix prefix_name
```

Specifies the prefix of the target mirrored objects.
```
-bumps bump_list
```

Specifies the bump list in source chip to be mirrored. By default, all bumps are
mirrored.
```
-cluster_bump_mapping pattern_cell_pair_list
```

Specifies the bump cluster pattern cells in source chip and target chip. The
pattern cell pair list is specified as {{source_pattern_cell target_pattern_cell}
{} ...}. This option cannot be specified with the _-bond_pad_ option.
```
-bond_pad
```

Mirrors bond pads from source chip to target chip.




```
-pins pin_list
```

If source chip is a hard macro, this option can be used to specify the pin list in
the source chip to be mirrored. By default, all pins will be mirrored if the source
chip is a hard macro.
```
-bond_pad_list bond_pad_list
```

Specifies the bond pad list in source chip to be mirrored. By default, all bond
pads are mirrored.
```
-bump_region
```

Mirrors bump regions from source chip to target chip. This option is required for
pseudo bumps and cannot be specified with the _-bond_pad_ option.
```
-bump_region_list bump_region_list
```

Specifies the bump region list in source chip to be mirrored. By default, all bump
regions are mirrored. This option must be specified with the _-bump_region_
option.
```
-pseudo_bump_list pseudo_bump_list
```

Specifies the pseudo bump list in source chip to be mirrored. The tool will create
a freeform bump region to coverr these mirroed pseudo bumps. This option
cannot be specified with the _-bump_region_ option.
```
-to_bump_region bump_region_list
```

Specifies the target bump region in target chip to be mirrored the specifed
pseudo bumps. This specified bump region must be freeform type. This option
must be specified with the _-pseudo_bump_list_ option.
```
-force
```

Specifies whether to mirror the objects if there are overlaps.
```
-strip_away_prefix prefix_name
```

Strip away the prefix of source bump name. The design already has source
bumps prefixed with ${strip_prefix}, and the tool would like to remove the
prefix from destination bump without changing name of source bump. If the
name of target bump is empty after striping away prefix, the command will use
"SYNOPSYS" as default.
```
-bond_pad_def bond_pad_def_name
```

Specifies the name of bond pad def, the bond pad def will be used to create
bond pad, this option must be used with “-bond_pad”.
```
-bump_cluster_list edit_group_list
```

Specified the bump clusters from source chip to target chip.




```
-no_snap
```

Prevent snapping to grid when mirroring.
```
-skip_physical_check
```

Skip checking the bump face when mirroring the bump cells from one die to
another die. When this option is specified, the command doesn't require the
source die and target die are vertical neighboring, and mirrors the source
bumps/bond_pads/pseudo_bumps that faced to target die if "-bumps/bond_pad_list/-bump_region_list" is not specified. If "-bumps/-bond_pad_list/
-bump_region_list" is specified with this option, the command mirriors all the
specified objects without checking their bump face.
```
-use_port_names
```

Rename the mirrored bump name using its connected port if it is existed.
```
-top_nets net_list
```

Choose the source bumps/bond_pads that connect to the specified top nets to
mirror.
```
-group_to_one
```

These bumps that connect to one top net will be mirrored to one bump, the
location of target bump is the center of group of source bumps. It must be used
with "-top_nets" option.
```
-offset offset
```

Specifies the offset value from center of from_object to center of to_object.
```
-naming_style format_list
```

Specifies the name style, including source_die_io_port and io_port: Values:
connect_die_port, io_port, source_die_io_port. Connect_die_port: the target
mirror bump will be named with the port name which connect t o source bump,
it’s same with the behavior of option “-use_port_name”. Io_port: the target mirror
bump will be named with "IOportName". Source_die_io_port: the target mirror
bump will be named with "sourceDieName_IOportName".
```
-propagate_user_attributes
```

Propagate user attributes from source bumps to mirrored bumps.
```
-boundary boundary_spec
```

Specifies the boundary, these bumps that are fully covered with the specified
boundary of source chip will be mirrored.




**Description**

This command copies and places bumps and bump clusters or bond pads from the source
die to the target die when the dies are stacked vertically. Hierarchy bumps are supported.

**Examples**

The following example copies bump cells from chip "Logic" to chip "Interposer" with the
library cell "UBUMP", using the prefix "synopsys".
```
prompt> create_3d_mirror_bumps -from Logic -to Interposer \\
-ref_cell UBUMP -prefix synopsys
```

The following example copies bump cluster which has pattern cell "BUMP8" from chip
"Logic" to chip "Interposer" with pattern cell "BUMP4".
```
prompt> create_3d_mirror_bumps -from Logic -to Interposer \\
-cluster_bump_mapping {{BUMP8 BUMP4}}

```

**See Also**

 - set_cell_location

###### **create_3d_virtual_blocks**

Creates virtual interface blocks.

**Syntax**

collection _create_3d_virtual_blocks_
```
[-design design ]
[-blocks { { die1 [: num_layers ] die2 [: num_layers ] }... }]
[-layers num_layers ]
[-in_netlist]
[-die_separation separation_value ]
```

**Data Types**
```
design       collection
die1        string
num_layers     integer
die2        string
separation_value  float
```

**Arguments**
```
-design design
```

Specifies the design in which to create the virtual interface blocks. If no design is
specified, the virtual interface blocks are created in the current design.




```
-blocks { { die1 [: num_layers ] die2 [: num_layers ] }... }
```

Specifies the die cells between which to create the virtual interface block. One or
more pairs of die cell names can be specified. The number of routing layers to
copy from each die can be specified after each name, which overrides the value
specified by the _-layers_ option.
```
-layers num_layers
```

Specifies the number of routing layers to copy from each die. If not specified,
three layers are copied from each die. This can be overridden on a per-die basis
in the _-blocks_ specification.
```
-in_netlist
```

Connects the virtual interface blocks to the top netlist between the dies. If not
specified, the virtual interface blocks are not connected to the top netlist.
```
-die_separation separation_value
```

Specifies the die separation distance used for micro bumps in the virtual
interface blocks.

**Description**

This command creates virtual interface blocks between the specified dies or interposer
cells. If no dies or interposer cells are specified, this command creates virtual interface
blocks between all die and interposers in design which have their z-offset values set.

**Examples**

The following example creates virtual interface blocks between all dies and interpose in
the design based on their z-offset values. The virtual interface blocks are connected to the
top netlist.
```
prompt> create_3d_virtual_blocks -in_netlist
```

The following example creates a virtual interface block between two dies containing four
routing layers from each die.
```
prompt> create_3d_virtual_blocks -blocks {die1 die2} -layers 4
```

The following example creates a virtual interface block between two dies containing two
routing layers from the first die and three routing layers from the second die.
```
prompt> create_3d_virtual_blocks -blocks {die1:2 die2:3}

```

**See Also**

 - remove_3d_virtual_blocks




###### **create_abstract**

Creates abstract view of designs.

**Syntax**
```
status create_abstract
[-placement]
[-estimate_timing]
[-timing_level none | boundary | compact | full_interface]
[-host_options host_option_name]
[-work_dir path]
[-blocks block_designs ]
[-all_blocks]
[-force_recreate]
[-read_only]
[-include_objects { include_objects_collection }]
[-target_use implementation | planning]
[-preserve_block_instances true | false]
```

**Data Types**
```
block_designs  list
include_objects_collection  collection of ports, pins and nets
```

**Arguments**
```
-placement
```

Creates the abstract view with no timing information. When this option is
specified, the tool will not trace timing paths to the ports of the design. Instead,
the tool examines the logical hierarchy of the design, and creates an abstract
view with the necessary netlist data for top-level global placement. If the design
has timing constraints loaded, constrained objects in the interface logic will be
included in the placement abstract. A placement abstract is always editable.
So this option overrides _-read_only_ . By default, the generated abstract view
contains timing information.
```
-estimate_timing
```

Run the _estimate_timing_ command on interface logic and incorporate the
estimated timing result in the abstract view.
```
-timing_level none | boundary | compact | full_interface
```

Specifies the amount of timing detail to include in the abstract. Abstracts with
less detail require less memory and CPU.




You can select one of three timing levels:

 - _none_ : The abstract excludes timing information at the top level. This is the
default abstract type when _-placement_ is specified.

Use this abstract for pure physical operations (all design planning steps prior
to _estimate_timing_, doing some purely physical operations at top-level).

The value 'none' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

 - _boundary_ : The abstract includes minimal netlist ensuring connectivity of
block ports to the first level of logic. Pure feedthrough, clock combinational
feedthrough and internal clock path driving output port are retained

Use this abstract for better transition fixing of the top level segment of
boundary nets when abstract is linked to top.

 - _compact_ : The abstract includes timing information for all critical setup and
hold paths at the boundary of the original design. When the abstract is
instantiated at the top level, you can use the abstract to show the best and
worst timing through any input port or output port of the abstracted design.
These abstracts have a very high level of compression when compared to
the full design, and have significant runtime and memory benefits. This is the
default when _-placement_ is not specified.

When you build a "compact" timing abstract, it is necessary to evaluate
timing paths in the design that is being abstracted. Because of this, you
should have the following SDC constraints defined in your block, prior to
creating the "compact" abstract:

  - All clocks and all generated clocks

  - All set_case_analysis and set_disable_timing

  - All exception constraints ( _set_false_path_, _set_multicycle_path_ ) that affect
timing paths that enter or leave the block.

Use this abstract for all top-level implementation flows.

 - _full_interface_ : The abstract includes timing information for almost all paths
at the boundary of the original design. Because all boundary paths are
represented, it is not necessary to prepare a full SDC file for the original
design before creating the abstract. However, you should have the following
SDC constraints defined in your block before creating the "full_interface"
abstract:

  - All clocks and all generated clocks

"Full_interface" abstracts contain nearly all of the boundary logic in the
original design; some boundary logic is filtered out to reduce the abstract




size. In particular, logic connected only to high-fanout networks is filtered.
Usually, the filtered logic includes clock networks, scan enable, and reset.
For these signals, only the essential part of the logic is kept. You can control
the filtering of high-fanout networks by setting the "abstract.high_fanout_limit"
app option.

Use this abstract when your block SDC is not ready.
```
-host_options host_option_name
```

Specifies that the given host option should be used for distributed processing. If
not specified, the tool will look for the global host option and use the global host
option if it has distributed processing settings.

When _-blocks_ or _-all_blocks_ is specified, the tool might need to create abstract
view for more than one block. Some of the blocks can run at the same time,
depending on the hierarchy nesting.
```
-work_dir path
```

Specifies the directory to put all generated scripts and log files. This option is
only used when _-blocks_ or _-all_blocks_ is specified. When _-blocks_ or _-all_blocks_
is specified, the tool need to create abstract view for one or more child blocks of
the current block. Scripts and log files are generated for abstract view creation at
the child blocks' level. The tool puts all the scripts and log files under a directory
on disk.

If this option is not specified, the _work_dir_ setting for the specified host option
would be used. If no _-host_options_ is specified, the _work_dir_ of the global host
option would be used. If there is no global host option and no _-host_options_ is
specified, the default is _./work_dir_ .
```
-blocks block_designs
```

Specifies the list of child block designs to create abstract view. The parent
design will switch to use the abstract view as reference for the instantiations of
the corresponding designs, if they are not referencing to abstract view already.
This option is mutually exclusive with _-all_blocks_ . If no _-blocks_ or _-all_blocks_ is
specified, the abstract view for the current design is created.

In a multi-level physical hierarchy design, only one level of physical hierarchy
can be abstract view.
```
-all_blocks
```

Specifies that abstract view is to be created for all the child blocks in the current
design, given that the block is the lowest in the physical hierarchy tree that is
allowed to have abstract view. The parent design will switch to use the abstract
view as reference for instantiations of the corresponding designs, if they are
not referencing to abstract view already. This option is mutually exclusive with




_-blocks_ . If the _-blocks_ or _-all_blocks_ option is not specified, the command creates
an abstract view for the current design.

In a multi-level physical hierarchy design, the tool will create abstract for the
lowest level of block.
```
-force_recreate
```

This option only works with _-blocks_ or _-all_blocks_ . Without _-blocks_ and
_-all_blocks_, the command will always re-create the abstract view of the current
block.

When _-blocks_ or _-all_blocks_ is specified, the tool would first search the physical
hierarchy tree looking for the blocks to create abstract view. After the tool finds
a certain block that should create abstract view for, it checks whether the block
already has an abstract view and whether this abstract view is of the same type
the user wants to create now. By default, the tool would not attempt to re-create
the abstract view if the existing one is of the same type.

If the _-force_recreate_ option is specified, the tool would do the proper view
merge, delete the existing abstract view, and create a new abstract view, even if
the existing one is of the correct type. This can be useful when the user wants to
make sure that the blocks use the up-to-date abstract views.
```
-read_only
```

Specifies that the abstract view being created is read-only. By default, when an
abstract view is created, the design view of the block is locked and becomes
read-only. By specifying this option, you are asking the tool to make the abstract
view read-only and keep the editability of the design view.

This option has no effect when _-placement_ is specified. The two options are
mutually exclusive.
```
-include_objects { include_objects_collection }
```

Specifies that some objects need to be retained in the abstract. These objects
can be ports, leaf pins, hierarchical pins or nets. Specifying a pin (leaf or
hierarchical) will cause the cell of the pin to be included in the abstract.
Specifying a net _n_ will cause the pins on the same flat net as _n_ that are also
specified in the _include_objects_collection_ to be connected in the abstract. At
least one leaf-level driver and one leaf-level load on the flat net containing _n_
need to be specified for the connection to occur.

This option can be used for both timing and placement abstracts. This option
cannot be used together with options _-blocks_, _-all_blocks_ and _-estimate_timing_ .




```
-target_use implementation | planning
```

Specifies the stage in which the created abstract is targeted to be used. Based
on the target stage, tool will apply appropriate internal settings.

You can select one of the two stages:

   - _implementation_ : The abstract is targeted to be used in top-level
implementation.

Abstract creation is allowed in any level of physical hierarchy.

   - _planning_ : The abstract is targeted to be used in design planning.

Abstract creation by default is allowed only on blocks which does not have
any descendant block that can be abstract view. This can be overridden by
setting the _abstract.allow_all_level_abstract_ application option to true.
```
-preserve_block_instances true | false
```

This option is relevant to designs with nested physical hierarchies. This option
determines whether lower levels of physical hierarchies are preserved or
whether the hierarchy is made part of the current hierarchy. If this option is set to
false, tool will create a flattened abstract. The default value of the option is true.

**Description**

This command creates an abstract view of the current block. If the block already has an
abstract view, this command removes the existing abstract and generates a new abstract
view. All leaf cells of the block needs to be mapped prior to abstract creation.

This command also saves the current block to disk.

Abstract view contains all the information that is needed for design planning. For toplevel implementation, in addition to abstract, create a frame view using the _create_frame_
command.

By default, the abstract view is editable and the design view is locked and becomes readonly. You can open and modify the design view, but _save_block_ or _save_lib_ would not be
able to save the modified design view to disk. If you want to save the modified design
view, you have a choice. You can either call _remove_abstract_ to remove the abstract view
and release the write lock on the design view, or call _create_abstract_ to remove the old
abstract view, save the modified design view to disk and create a new abstract view.

**Design Flow for Abstracts**

By default, an editable abstract view is created. At the same time, the design view of the
block is locked and becomes read-only.




After the abstract view of the block is created, you can change the instantiation of the
block in a parent block to reference to the abstract view using the _change_abstract_
command.

If the abstract view is editable and instantiated in a parent block, you can make changes
to it in the parent block context. Changes in the abstract view are brought back into the full
netlist design view through merge. Merge happens automatically when the design view is
loaded. You can also call merge explicitly using the command _merge_abstract_ .

The merge operation requires that the full netlist design view remain unchanged between
the time that the abstract is created with the _create_abstract_ command and the abstract is
merged back to the design view.

**Resuming Editing of the Full Netlist**

When an editable abstract view is created. At the same time, the design view of the block
is locked and becomes read-only. The read-only design view can still be opened and
modified in memory. But if you want to commit the in-memory modifications to disk, you
won't be able to do it with _save_block_ or _save_lib_ command. There are three ways to save
the in-memory modification of an abstract-locked design view to disk:

1. You can save it to another design using _save_block -as xxx_ .

2. If you no longer need to use the abstract view, you can call _remove_abstract_ to delete
the abstract view and release the lock on the design view. Then, you will be able to use
_save_block_ or _save_lib_ to save the design view.

3. If you want to get an updated abstract view according to the latest design view inmemory, you can call _create_abstract_ command. The _create_abstract_ command
will delete the existing abstract view, release the lock on the design view, save the
design view to disk, create the new abstract view, and lock the design view again if no
_-read_only_ is specified.

**Summary for timing abstract creation**

When a timing abstract is created, the tool by default retains

 - Data and clock paths needed for analysis and optimization at top-level

In addition, some cells in the interface logic are retained because they are used in
timing constraints or exceptions. The log will contain a summary reporting how many
cells were kept because of exceptions. The summary also reports how many pins in




the design were affected by each type of exception or constraint. Specifically, the report
includes:

   - _User size only_ : Number of pins on cells that are size only (set by the command
set_size_only)

   - _Exception_ : Number of pins referred to by timing exceptions like set_false_path,
set_multicycle_path, set_max_delay etc.

   - _Clock_ : Number of pins that are a clock source, a generated clock source or a
master pin for a generated clock.

   - _Clock Gating_ : Number of pins that belong to clock gating cells.

   - _Constraint_ : Number of pins referred to in constraints like set_input_delay,
set_output_delay, set_max_time_borrow etc.

   - _Case analysis_ : Number of pins with case analysis values (defined with
set_case_analysis command).

   - _Cell mode_ : Number of pins that have cell mode constraints (defined with
set_cell_mode command).

   - _Disable timing_ : Number of pins that have disable timing exception (defined using
the set_disable_timing command).

   - _CTS exception_ : Number of pins that have CTS exceptions on them, for example
set_clock_balance_points.

   - _PVT_ : Number of pins that have PVT exceptions, like set_operating_conditions,
set_voltage, set_temperature etc.

   - _Latency_ : Number of pins that have a clock latency set (this affects only pins that
are not on sequential cells).

   - _Clock sense_ : Number of pins that have a set_clock_sense set.

**Multi-mode and multi-corner support**

During create_abstract, the tool

 - identifies and retains the timing level based interface logic across all active modes

 - Retains interface logic pins with constraints across all modes (active and inactive)

 - Retains parasitics for all corners (active and inactive)

Ensure that all the scenarios used at top-level are defined and active while creating
abstract.




**Multivoltage support**

During create_abstract, the tool

 - stores the UPF relevant to the retained interface logic. This is promoted to the top-level
during linking.

**Multi-level physical hierarchy design**

 - Creating abstract for using in Design Planning Flow

In a multi-level physical hierarchy design, only one level of physical hierarchy can be
an abstract view. By default, it's the lowest level of blocks.

 - Creating abstract for Top-level Place and Route

Nested abstracts are supported for top-level place and route. Set the
abstract.allow_all_level_abstract application option.

**Creating abstracts with power annotation**

 - Set the abstract.annotate_power application option to create abstracts with power
information. This enables you to perform power analysis of the complete design while
at top-level

**Creating abstracts for Signal EM Analysis**

 - Set the abstract.enable_signal_em_analysis application option to true before running
_create_abstract_ . This enables you to signal EM analysis inside abstracts while at toplevel

**Examples**

The following example creates an abstract view, with timing information, for the current
design.
```
prompt> create_abstract
```

The following example creates an abstract view that is suitable for top-level global
placement.
```
prompt> create_abstract -placement
```

The following example creates an abstract view that is suitable for top-level optimization.
```
prompt> create_abstract
```

The following example runs _estimate_timing_ on the interface logic of the current design,
then creates an abstract view that includes the result of the estimated (virtually optimized)
timing.
```
prompt> create_abstract -estimate_timing

```



The following example calls _create_abstract_ from the top level, finds all the child blocks
that are abstract view or can be an abstract view, and create the up-to-date abstract view
including merging any changes from existing abstract view to the design view, also change
the instantiations in parent blocks to reference to the block's abstract view.
```
prompt> create_abstract -all_blocks -force_recreate
```

In the following example we assume that the design contains a net n1 that connects
a driver D1 to loads L1, L2, L3, L4. Using the sequence of commands shown, will
ensure that the abstract contains the cells of the pins D1 and L3 and that D1 and L3 are
connected by a net in the abstract.
```
prompt> set c_pins [get_pins {D1 L3}]
prompt> set c_nets [get_nets {n1}]
prompt> set cAll [add_to_collection $c_pins $c_nets]
prompt> create_abstract -include_objects $cAl
```

The following example creates a flattened abstract if a block has nested blocks in it. If the
block does not have any nested blocks, it simply creates abstract for the block.
```
prompt> create_abstract -preserve_block_instances false

```

**See Also**

 - change_abstract

 - create_frame

 - estimate_timing

 - get_abstract_type

 - merge_abstract

 - remove_abstract

 - report_abstracts

 - abstract.allow_all_level_abstract

 - abstract.annotate_power

 - abstract.enable_signal_em_analysis

 - abstract.high_fanout_limit

 - abstract.latch_levels

 - plan.flow.design_view_only




###### **create_abut_rules**

Creates spacing rules or keepout margins for cells in a design.

**Syntax**

status _create_abut_rules_
```
[-soft_keepout]
[-hard_keepout]
[-keepout_width width ]
[-number_of_references number ]
[-use_lib]
[-output] filename
```

**Data Types**
```
width float
number int
filename string
```

**Arguments**
```
-soft_keepout
```

Uses soft keepout margins instead of spacing rules.
```
-hard_keepout
```

Uses hard keepout margins instead of spacing rules.
```
-keepout_width width
```

Specifies the soft keepout margin width to use, in microns. This option should
only be used if the _-soft_keepout_ or _-hard_keepout_ option is used. The default
value is the site width.
```
-number_of_references number
```

Specifies the number of top pin_density values, from which to obtain references
to apply spacing rules or keepout margins. The default is 6.
```
-use_lib
```

Specifies that library reference cells are used as a source for top pin_density lib
cells, instead of reference cells found in the design.
```
-output filename
```

Specifies the output command filename.




**Description**

The _create_abut_rules_ command helps to improve routability of a design by spacing cells
further apart with the use of keepout_margins or by flipping cells. Before running this
command, run the _check_routes_ command to ensure that the DRC error information is upto-date.

The command _create_abut_rules_ creates either spacing rules (default) or soft/hard
keepout margins on reference cells with the top six (default) largest pin_density values.
These reference cells are found in the design. If the _-use_lib_ option is specified, then the
libraries are used to derive the reference cells. An output file is written out.

**Examples**

The following example runs the _create_abut_rules_ command using the top 4 pin density
values to derive reference cells found in the design to apply spacing rules to.
```
prompt> create_abut_rules -number_of_references 4 -output abut_4.tcl
```

The following example creates a soft keepout margin of width 2 microns using the libraries
as reference cells to apply soft keepout margins to.
```
prompt> create_abut_rules -number_of_references 5 -output soft_abut_5.tcl
\\
-soft_keepout -keepout_width 2

```

**See Also**

 - check_routes

 - create_keepout_margin

 - set_placement_spacing_label

 - set_placement_spacing_rule

###### **create_alignment_marker_cell**

Given a 3D-IC design, create appropriate alignment marker cells on the required host dies
according to the alignment marker rules.

**Syntax**

status _create_alignment_marker_cell_
```
[-rules rule_list]
[-host_dies host_die_list]
[-adjacent_dies adjacent_die_list]

```



**Data Types**
```
rule_list        list
host_die_list      list
adjacent_die_list    list
```

**Arguments**
```
-rules
```

Specify a list of alignment marker rules to create alignment marker cells. By
default, all rules within the current block will be considered.
```
-host_dies
```

Specify the host dies for alignment marker rules to create alignment marker
cells. By default, all dies in the current design will be considered.
```
-adjacent_dies
```

Specify the adjacent dies for the alignment marker rules. By default, all dies
in the current design will be considered. For each host die, the command will
identify the suitable adjacent dies from the adjacent_die_list to create the cells.

**Description**

The _create_alignment_marker_cell_ command creates new alignment marker cells in the
current design. If the created cells exceed the boundary of the host die or overlap with
another cell with the same reference, the creation will fail.

**Prerequisites**
```
create_alignment_marker_rule
```

**Multicorner-Multimode Support**

This command has no dependency on scenario-specific information.

**Examples**

Assuming the current design includes an interposer, Die1, and Die2, where only Die1 is an
adjacent die of the interposer.

When we create an alignment marker rule and the reference object of this rule is host die:
```
prompt> create_alignment_marker_rule -name AMR1 -reference_die HOST
-type CORNER -reference_object DIE_BOUNDARY -x_offset 500 -y_offset 800
-lib_cell AM_L -reference_corner bottom_left
```

The following examples will create the same alignment marker cell on the interposer.
```
prompt> create_alignment_marker_cell -rules {AMR1} -host_dies
{interposer}

```



```
prompt> create_alignment_marker_cell -host_dies {interposer}
```

When we create an alignment marker rule and the reference object of this rule is adjacent
die:
```
prompt> create_alignment_marker_rule -name AMR2 -reference_die ADJACENT
-type CORNER -reference_object DIE_BOUNDARY -x_offset 500 -y_offset 800
-lib_cell AM_L -reference_corner bottom_left
```

The following examples will create the same alignment marker cell on interposer reference
to the adjacent die.
```
prompt> create_alignment_marker_cell -rules {AMR2}
prompt> create_alignment_marker_cell -rules {AMR2} -host_dies
{interposer}
prompt> create_alignment_marker_cell -rules {AMR2} -host_dies
{interposer} -adjacent_dies {Die1}
prompt> create_alignment_marker_cell -rules {AMR2} -host_dies
{interposer} -adjacent_dies {Die1 Die2}
prompt> create_alignment_marker_cell -rules {AMR2} -adjacent_dies {Die1}
prompt> create_alignment_marker_cell -rules {AMR2} -adjacent_dies {Die1
Die2}

```

**See Also**

 - create_alignment_marker_rule

 - check_alignment_marker

###### **create_alignment_marker_rule**

Creates one alignment marker rule object.

**Syntax**

status \create_alignment_marker_rule
```
[-name rule_name ]
[-type rule_type ]
[-lib_cell lib_cell design ]
[-reference_die The reference chiplet object ]
[-projection_map list of pair of ref_marker and host_marker ]
[-reference_object Reference shape object in reference chiplet ]
[-reference_object_name Reference object name ]
[-reference_layer Reference layer for reference object shape type layer ]
[-reference_corner Reference corner of the ref_shape ]

```



```
[-orientation Orientation of alignment marker cell ]
[-x_offset Pre shrink X offset value ]
[-y_offset Pre shrink Y offset value ]
[-x_step Pre shrink X step value ]
[-y_step Pre shrink Y step value ]
[-x_num Pre shrink X num value ]
[-y_num Pre shrink X num value ]
```

**Data Types**
```
rule_name        string
rule_type        string
lib_cell         list
reference_die      string
projection_map      list
reference_object     string
reference_object_name  string
reference_layer     string
reference_corner     string
orientation       string
x_offset         integer
y_offset         integer
x_step          integer
y_step          integer
x_num          integer
y_num          integer
```

**Arguments**
```
-name rule_name
```

Specifies the name of the alignment marker rule to be created. Empty rule name
and already used name cannot be provided.
```
-type rule_type
```

Specifies the type of the alignment marker rule to be created. Rule type
enumeration values can be one of from none, step, corner, or projection. Default
rule type is none.
```
-lib_cell list of lib_cell design
```

Specifies one lib_cell design.
```
-reference_die Die type enum string
```

The reference chiplet object to define the alignment marker location. Die type
enumeration values can be one of from host, adjacent, or projection. Default
value for this option is host. This option must be provided when creating rule of
type default or step or corner.




```
-projection_map List of pair of strings
```

Specifies list of pair of reference_marker and host_marker strings. This option
must be provided only when creating rule of type "projection". Command
options -lib_cell, reference_object, -reference_object_name, -reference_layer,
-reference_corner, -orientation, -x_offset, -y_offset, -x_step, -y_step, -x_num,
and -y_num are mutually exclusive with -projection_map.
```
-reference_object Reference shape object
```

Specifies reference shape object in reference chiplet to define the alignment
marker location. Reference object enumeration values can be any of from
die_boundary, seal_ring, scribe_line, stitching_zone, layer_shape or custom.
Default value for this option is die_boundary.
```
-reference_object_name Reference object name
```

Optionally specifies reference object name for alignment marker rule.
```
-reference_layer Reference layer
```

Optionally specifies reference layer for reference object shape type layer. This
option must be providede if -reference_object is of type layer_shape only.
```
-reference_corner Reference corner
```

Specifies reference corner of the reference shape. It's value can be any one
from top_left, top_right, bottom_left or bottom_right. Default value for this option
is bottom_left. This option is mandatory when creating rule of type step or
corner.
```
-orientation Orientation
```

Specifies orientation of the alignment marker cell. It's values can be any one
from R0, R90, R180, R270, MX, MXR90, MY, or MYR90. Default value for this
option is R0. This option is mandatory when creating rule of type step or corner.
```
-x_offset X_Offset
```

Specifies pre shrink horizontal offset from ref_corner to lower left corner of
alignment marker cell placement after orient. Default value for this option is 0.
This option can be provided only when creating rule of type step or corner.
```
-y_offset Y_Offset
```

Specifies pre shrink vertical from ref_corner to lower left corner of alignment
marker cell placement after orient. Default value for this option is 0. This option
can be provided only when creating rule of type step or corner.
```
-x_step X_Step
```

Optionally specifies pre shrink x step value. Default value for this option is 0.
This option can be provided only when creating step rule.




```
-y_step Y_Step
```

Optionally specifies pre shrink y step value. Default value for this option is 0.
This option can be provided only when creating step rule.
```
-x_num X_Num
```

Optionally specifies pre shrink x num value. Default value for this option is 0.
This option can be provided only when creating step rule.
```
-y_num Y_Num
```

Optionally specifies pre shrink y num value. Default value for this option is 0.
This option can be provided only when creating step rule.

**Description**

This command creates a new alignment_marker_rule with the given name.

**Examples**

The following example creates an alignment marker rule object of step type.
```
prompt> create_alignment_marker_rule -name AMR1 \\
-type step -reference_die
ADJACENT \\
-reference_object DIE_BOUNDARY \\
-x_num 4 -y_num 6 -x_step 30
-y_step 40 \\
-x_offset 10 -y_offset 20 \\
-lib_cell tcbn90glvt/AN2LVTD0 \\
-orientation R0 -reference_corner
top_left
```

The following rule creates an alignment marker rule object with reference_object of type
projection.
```
prompt>  create_alignment_marker_rule -name AMR2 \\
-type projection -reference_die
PROJECTION \\
-projection_map {{"ref1"
"host1"} {"ref2" "host2"}}
```

The following rule creates an alignment marker rule object with reference_object of type
layer_shape.
```
prompt>  create_alignment_marker_rule -name AMR3 \
-reference_die ADJACENT \
-reference_object LAYER_SHAPE \
-x_num 4 -y_num 6 -x_step 30 -y_step 40 \
-x_offset 10 -y_offset 20 \
-lib_cell tcbn90glvt/AN2LVTD0 \

```



```
-orientation R0 -reference_corner top_left \
-reference_layer M2
```

The following example creates an alignment marker rule object of default type and
reference_object of type custom.
```
prompt> create_alignment_marker_rule -name AMR1 \\
-type none -reference_die
ADJACENT \\
-reference_object custom \\
-reference_object_name STZONE \\
-x_num 4 -y_num 6 -x_step 30
-y_step 40 \\
-x_offset 10 -y_offset 20 \\
-lib_cell tcbn90glvt/AN2LVTD0 \\
-orientation R0 -reference_corner
top_left

```

**See Also**

 - report_alignment_marker_rules

 - get_alignment_marker_rules

 - remove_alignment_marker_rules

###### **create_always_statement**

Creates 1 RTL always statement.

**Syntax**

collection _create_always_statement_
```
rtl_statement
-sensitivity_list sensitivity_list
[-name name ]
[-type type ]
[-module module | -cell cell ]
[-scope scope ]
```

**Data Types**
```
rtl_statement    collection
sensitivity_list  collection
name        string
type        string
module       collection
cell        collection
scope        collection

```



**Arguments**
```
rtl_statement
```

Specifies only 1 RTL statement used for the always statement. This can be
a begin statement, which contains various statements. This is a required
argument. The following RTL statements are supported:

   - rtl_assignment • rtl_begin_end • rtl_case • rtl_for • rtl_foreach • rtl_if_else

    - rtl_repeat • rtl_package • rtl_parameter • rtl_variable • rtl_expression •
rtl_while
```
-sensitivity_list sensitivity_list
```

Specifies the RTL statement of type expression used for the always statement.
```
-name name
```

Specifies the name used for the always statement.
```
-type type
```

Specifies the type of the always block. The default type is standard. The
available values are standard, flip-flop, latch, or combinational.
```
-module module
```

Specifies the module to create the always statement in. This option is mutually
exclusive with the _-cell_ option.
```
-cell cell
```

Specifies the cell to create the always statement in. This option is mutually
exclusive with the _-module_ option.
```
-scope scope
```

Adds the newly created always statement in the scope provided by the RTL
statement.

**Description**

This command creates an RTL always statement. The always statement is created in
the specified module or cell. If the _-module_ or _-cell_ option is not specified, the always
statement is created in the current instance.

**Examples**

The following example creates 1 always statement in the current instance with the begin
end statement named _one_ and sensitivity list named _two_ .
```
prompt > create_always_statement [get_statements -filter "type ==
begin_end" one] \\

```



```
-sensitivity_list [get_statements -filter "type == expression" two] \\
{"RTL_ALWAYS_1"}
```

The following example creates 1 always statement named _two_always_ in the current
instance with the begin end statement named _one_ and sensitivity list named _two_ .
```
prompt > create_always_statement [get_statements -filter "type ==
begin_end" one] \\
-name two_always -sensitivity_list [get_statements -filter "type ==
expression" two] \\
{"two_always"}

```

**See Also**

 - get_statements

 - remove_statements

###### **create_anchor**

Creates an anchor in the current block.

**Syntax**

collection _create_anchor_
```
-dependent_object object
[-name name ]
[-type location | location_x_y]
[-anchor_object object ]
[-anchor_x_object object ]
[-anchor_y_object object ]
[-dependent_object_position center | bbox_center | bbox_ll | bbox_ul |
bbox_ur | bbox_lr]
[-anchor_object_position center | bbox_center | bbox_ll | bbox_ul |
bbox_ur | bbox_lr]
[-anchor_x_object_position center | bbox_center | bbox_ll | bbox_ul |
bbox_ur | bbox_lr]
[-anchor_y_object_position center | bbox_center | bbox_ll | bbox_ul |
bbox_ur | bbox_lr]
[-offset distance_list ]
[-anchor_orientation]
```

**Data Types**
```
object     collection
name      string
distance_list  float

```



**Arguments**
```
-dependent_object object
```

Specifies the dependent (anchored) object. The object must be in the same
block as the anchor being created. Note that if the dependent object gets
subsequently removed, this anchor also be automatically removed.

An object might be the dependent object of no more than one anchor. It is an
error to specify an object that is already the dependent object of an existing
anchor. Also, the dependent object might not belong to an edit group.

This is a required argument.
```
-name name
```

Specifies the name of the anchor. If unspecified, the command generates
a name automatically using the prefix "ANCHOR" with a system-generated
number appended.
```
-type location | location_x_y
```

Specifies the type of the anchor. If type is "location", then the
dependent_object's location is anchored to a single object, specified by the
_-anchor_object_ argument. If type is "location_x_y", then the dependent_object
is anchored to two objects, specified by the _-anchor_x_object_ and
_-anchor_y_object_ arguments. If unspecified, the type defaults to "location".
```
-anchor_object object
```

Specifies the anchor object, to which the dependent object specified by the
_-dependent_object_ argument is anchored. This argument might only be specified
if the anchor type is "location".

When the anchor object is set, the dependent (anchored) object's
location is shifted (translated)such that the points defined by the
_-dependent_object_position_ option on the dependent object and
_-anchor_object_position_ option on the anchor object are separated by the
distance specified by the _-offset_ attribute. As the location of the anchor object
changes, so does the dependent object's location to maintain the specified
offset.

If the _-offset_ argument is not specified, then the offset is automatically computed
based on the current locations of the dependent and anchor objects, such that
the dependent object is not be shifted by this command.

The value of this argument must be a collection of a single object. Many object
classes that have physical extent, such as cells, shapes, vias, terminals,
voltage_areas, edit_groups, and so on might be specified as the anchor object.




```
-anchor_x_object object
```

Specifies the anchor x object, to which the x-coordinate of the dependent object
specified by the _-dependent_object_ argument is anchored. This argument might
only be specified if the anchor type is _location_x_y_ .

When the anchor x object is set, the dependent (anchored) object's
location's x-coordinate is adjusted such that the points defined
by _-dependent_object_position_ on the dependent object and
_-anchor_x_object_position_ on the anchor x object are separated by the distance
specified by the x component of the _-offset_ attribute. As the location of the
anchor x object changes, so does the dependent object's x-coordinate to
maintain the specified offset.

If the _-offset_ argument is not specified, then the offset is automatically computed
based on the current locations of the dependent and anchor objects, such that
the dependent object is not be shifted by this command.

The value of this argument must be a collection of a single object. Many object
classes that have physical extent, such as cells, shapes, vias, terminals,
voltage_areas, edit_groups, and so on might be specified as the anchor x
object.
```
-anchor_y_object object
```

Specifies the anchor y object, to which the y-coordinate of the dependent object
specified by the _-dependent_object_ argument is anchored. This argument might
only be specified if the anchor type is _location_x_y_ .

When the anchor y object is set, the dependent (anchored) object's
location's y-coordinate is adjusted such that the points defined
by _-dependent_object_position_ on the dependent object and
_-anchor_y_object_position_ on the anchor y object are separated by the distance
specified by the y component of the _-offset_ attribute. As the location of the
anchor y object changes, so does the dependent object's y-coordinate to
maintain the specified offset.

If the _-offset_ argument is not specified, then the offset is automatically computed
based on the current locations of the dependent and anchor objects, such that
the dependent object is not be shifted by this command.

The value of this argument must be a collection of a single object. Many object
classes that have physical extent, such as cells, shapes, vias, terminals,
voltage_areas, edit_groups, and so on might be specified as the anchor y
object.




```
-dependent_object_position center | bbox_center | bbox_ll | bbox_ul |
bbox_ur | bbox_lr
```

Specifies a reference point with respect to the dependent (anchored) object's
unrotated geometric shape. This reference point is used as the destination point
of the _-offset_ between the dependent object and the anchor objects. That is, this
reference point is constrained to always equal the reference point defined by
the _-anchor_object_position_ attribute when the anchor type is _location_, or by the
_-anchor_x_object_position_ and _anchor_y_object_position_ attributes when the
anchor type is _location_x_y_, offset by the anchor's _-offset_ attribute value. The
tool moves the dependent object to meet this constraint when necessary.

The reference point is selected as follows according to the option value, where
the "shape" is the unrotated geometric shape of the dependent (anchored)
object:

_Position Table:_
```
  "center":   The center of the largest rectangle contained
  within the
  unrotated object shape,
  "bbox_center": The center of the unrotated shape's bounding box,
  "bbox_ll":   The lower-left corner of the unrotated shape's
  bounding box,
  "bbox_ul":   The upper-left corner of the unrotated shape's
  bounding box,
  "bbox_ur":   The upper-right corner of the unrotated shape's
  bounding box,
  "bbox_lr":   The lower-right corner of the unrotated shape's
  bounding box.
```

If unspecified, the default is _center_ . The above positions are on the unrotated
shapes, such that if the position is "bbox_ll" for example, and the object has
orientation R90, then the position point appear s at the lower-right of the object's
(rotated) bounding box.

_Note:_ : For cells, if the cell's boundary is set, then the boundary is used in lieu of
the bounding box when computing the reference point.
```
-anchor_object_position center | bbox_center | bbox_ll | bbox_ul |
bbox_ur | bbox_lr
```

Specifies a reference point with respect to the anchor object's unrotated
geometric shape. This reference point is used as the sourcepoint of the _-offset_
between the dependent (anchored) object and the anchor object. That is, the
reference point defined by _-dependent_object_position_ is constrained to always
equal this reference point offset by the anchor's _-offset_ attribute value. The tool
moves the dependent object to meet this constraint when necessary.




The reference point is selected according to the _Position Table_ described in
the _-dependent_object_position_ argument description, where the "shape" is the
geometric shape of the anchor object.

If unspecified, the default is _center_ . This argument might only be specified if the
anchor type is location.
```
-anchor_x_object_position center| bbox_center| bbox_ll| bbox_ul |
bbox_ur | bbox_lr
```

Specifies a reference point with respect to the anchor x object's unrotated
geometric shape. This reference point's x-coordinate is used as the source
x-coordinate of the _-offset_ between the dependent (anchored) object's xcoordinate and the anchor x object. That is, the x-coordinate of the reference
point defined by _-dependent_object_position_ is constrained to always equal
this reference x-coordinate offset by the anchor's _-offset_ attribute value's x
component. The tool moves the dependent object to meet this constraint when
necessary.

The reference point is selected according to the _Position Table_ described in
the _-dependent_object_position_ argument description, where the "shape" is the
geometric shape of the anchor x object.

If unspecified, the default is _center_ . This argument might only be specified if the
anchor type is location_x_y.
```
-anchor_y_object_position center| bbox_center| bbox_ll | bbox_ul |
bbox_ur | bbox_lr
```

Specifies a reference point with respect to the anchor y object's unrotated
geometric shape. This reference point's y-coordinate is used as the source
y-coordinate of the _-offset_ between the dependent (anchored) object's ycoordinate and the anchor y object. That is, the y-coordinate of the reference
point defined by _-dependent_object_position_ is constrained to always equal
this reference y-coordinate offset by the anchor's _-offset_ attribute value's y
component. The tool moves the dependent object to meet this constraint when
necessary.

The reference point is selected according to the _Position Table_ described in
the _-dependent_object_position_ argument description, where the "shape" is the
geometric shape of the anchor y object.

If unspecified, the default is _center_ . This argument might only be specified if the
anchor type is location_x_y.
```
-offset distance_list
```

Specifies the offset to be maintained between the reference points defined
by the _-dependent_object_position_ and the _-anchor_object_position_ attribute
values when the anchor type is location, or the _-dependent_object_position_,




_-anchor_x_object_position_, and _-anchor_y_object_position_ attribute
values when the anchor type is location_x_y. See the descriptions
of the _-dependent_object_position_, _-anchor_object_position_,
_-anchor_x_object_position_, and _-anchor_x_object_position_ arguments for a
description of how these reference points are computed. The offset between the
reference points is constrained to be the value of this option. The tool moves the
dependent object to meet this constraint when necessary.

If unspecified, the default is "{0 0}" (no offset).
```
-anchor_orientation
```

Specifies whether to also lock the dependent object's relative orientation to that
of the anchor object when the anchor type is location, or to the anchor x object
when the anchor type is location_x_y. That is, the dependent object keeps its
current orientation when this command completes, but rotates by the same
amount the anchor object subsequently rotates.

This argument has no effect unless the dependent object's object class has a
settable "orientation" attribute.

When unspecified, there is no orientation locking of the dependent object.

**Description**

The _create_anchor_ command creates a new anchor, an object that constrains one physical
object's location to the location of another physical object. The object with the constrained
location is referred to as the "dependent" or "anchored" object. The object that constrains
the dependent object's location is called the "anchor object". Note that "anchor object" is
distinct from the object created by this command, which has the object_class "anchor".
The use case of an anchor is when you want to lock one object's location to that of another
object, and have that object automatically be moved by the tool whenever the other object
is moved.

Anchor has two types: "location" and "location_x_y". When type is location, anchor
constrains a dependent object's location to a single anchor object as described previously.
When type is "location_x_y", anchor constrains a dependent object to two different anchor
objects, where one anchor object's x-coordinate constrains the dependent object's xcoordinate, and the other anchor object's y-coordinate constrains the dependent object's
y-coordinate.

Whereas the dependent object must be in the same block as the anchor, the anchor object
might be either in the same block or in a lower level of physical hierarchy.

Anchor must always have a dependent object, and if the dependent object is removed,
then the anchor is also removed automatically. A dependent object might also be the
anchor object of another anchor, forming chains of anchorage, however dependency
cycles result in an error. An object might only be a dependent object of one anchor at a
time, and might not be a member of an edit group.




**Examples**

The following example anchors cell A to cell B:
```
prompt> create_anchor -dependent_object [get_cells A] -anchor_object
[get_cells B]
{ANCHOR0}
```

The following example anchors cell A to the lower-left of edit_group mid/EG0:
```
prompt> create_anchor -dependent_object [get_cells A] \\
-anchor_object [get_edit_groups mid/EG0] -anchor_object_position
bbox_ll
{ANCHOR0}
```

The following example anchors the lower-left of voltage_area VA0's bounding box to the
upper-right of cell mid/B's bounding box:
```
prompt> create_anchor -dependent_object [get_voltage_areas VA0] \\
-dependent_object_position bbox_ll -anchor_object [get_cells mid/B] \\
-anchor_object_position bbox_ur
{ANCHOR0}
```

The following example anchors the lower-left of cell A's bounding box to be 4 microns to
the left of the upper-right of cell mid/B's bounding box:
```
prompt> create_anchor -dependent_object [get_cells A] \\
-dependent_object_position bbox_ll -anchor_object [get_cells mid/B] \\
-anchor_object_position bbox_ur -offset {-4 0}
{ANCHOR0}
```

The following example anchors bump_region BR0 to be 3 microns to right of cell B's
center horizontally, and 4 microns above terminal TM_0's center vertically:
```
prompt> create_anchor -type location_x_y \\
-dependent_object [get_bump_regions BR0] -anchor_x_object [get_cells
B] \\
-anchor_y_object [get_terminals TM_0] -offset {3 4}
{ANCHOR0}

```

**See Also**

 - get_anchors

 - remove_anchors

###### **create_annotation_shape**

Creates an annotation_shape object of shape types circle, line, polygon, and rect in the
current design.




**Syntax**
```
collection create_annotation_shape
-type circle | line | polygon | rect
-annotation_points annotation_points
[-name annotation_name ]
[-category  category_name ]
[-width  width ]
[-start_endcap endcap_type ]
[-end_endcap endcap_type ]
[-line_arrow]
[-elbow_percentage elbow_percentage ]
[-color color ]
[-fill fill ]
[-pen_style pen_style ]
[-pen_width pen_width ]
[-label label ]
[-horizontal_alignment left | center | right]
[-vertical_alignment bottom | middle | top]
[-orientation orientation ]
[-bold_text]
[-elide_text left | middle | right]
[-wrap_text]
```

**Data Types**
```
annotation_points  list of location descriptors
annotation_name   string
category_name    string
width        float
endcap       string
elbow_percentage  float
color        string
fill        string
label        string
pen_style      string
pen_width      string
orientation     string
```

**Arguments**
```
-type circle | line | polygon | rect
```

Specifies the type of annotation shape to create.

This is a required option.




```
-annotation_points annotation_points
```

Specifies the points for the specified annotation type. The points are specified
by a tool command language (Tcl) list in which each list element is one of the
following:

   - {<coord_x> <coord_y>} a fixed, absolute {x y} point

   - {<anchor_collection>} a point that follows an anchor object

   - {<anchor_collection> <position> <offset_x> <offset_y>} a point that follows
an anchor object at the specified position and offset

   - {<offset_x><+/-> <offset_y><+/->} a point that follows the location of the
previous point in the list, at the specified offset

The first format describes a simple fixed point at an absolute coordinate.

The second format specifies that the point follow the center of the anchor object,
where “center” is the center of the largest box that can be contained within the
anchor object’s boundary.

The third format specifies that the point follow the anchor object at the specified
offset w.r.t. the specified position. The offset x & y values can either be absolute
distances or percentage values (which are appended with ‘%’). The valid
position values are as follows:

   - center: The center of the largest box within the anchor object

   - bbox_center: The center of the bbox of the anchor object

   - bbox_ll: The lower-left corner of the bbox of the anchor object

   - bbox_ul: The upper-left corner of the bbox of the anchor object

   - bbox_lr: The lower-right corner of the bbox of the anchor object

   - bbox_ur: The upper-left corner of the bbox of the anchor object

The fourth format is a relative positioning feature that specifies the point follow
the previous point at the specified offset, where ‘+’ is appended to the offset
to specify a positive relative offset, and ‘-‘ is appended to specify a negative
relative offset. This relative positioning feature is not available to the first point in
the annotation_points list, but is available to any remaining point in the list.

This is a required option.
```
-name annotation_name
```

Specifies the name of the annotation_shape. The name may not contain
the special character '/'. If unspecified, the command will generate a name




automatically using the prefix "ANNOTATION_SHAPE" with a system-generated
number appended.
```
-category category_name
```

Specifies the name of the category the annotation_shape object. The category
maybe used for grouping of annotation shapes into separate sets. If unspecified,
the category will not be assigned for the annotation_shape.
```
-width width
```

Specifies the width of line annotation shape. The value must be non-negative.

If you use this option with other annotation shape types, the tool issues an error.
```
-start_endcap endcap_type
```

Specifies the type of the start endcap of a line annotation shape.

The valid values are

   - _flush_ (the default)

Creates an endcap with square ends and no extension.

   - _full_width_

Creates an endcap with square ends that is extended by the path width.

   - _half_width_

Creates an endcap with square ends that is extended by half the path width.

   - _octagon_

Creates an endcap with octagonal ends.

   - _round_

Creates an endcap with round ends.

This option is valid only for line annotation shapes; the tool issues an error if
you use it for other shape types.
```
-end_endcap endcap
```

Specifies the type of the end endcap of a line annotation shape.

The valid values are

   - _flush_ (the default)

Creates an endcap with square ends and no extension.

   - _full_width_




Creates an endcap with square ends that is extended by the path width.

   - _half_width_

Creates an endcap with square ends that is extended by half the path width.

   - _octagon_

Creates an endcap with octagonal ends.

   - _round_

Creates an endcap with round ends.

This option is valid only for line annotation shapes; the tool issues an error if
you use it for other shape types.
```
-line_arrow
```

Specifies if to show arrow for annotation_shapes of type line.
```
-color color
```

Specifies the annotation color. You can use a predefined color string, such
as white, red, green, blue, yellow, and so forth, or a hexadecimal RGB value,
such as #AA6633. The default annotation color is white. Annotations use colors
from the qt color palette by default. Colors from other color palettes may be
used by specifying a color name qualified with a palette name. For example,
"red:highlight" specifies the red color from the highlight palette. Available
palettes are qt, highlight, highcontrast, and style. Use gui_get_color_value
command to report on color names and values available in a palette. The default
color is white.
```
-fill pattern
```

Specifies the annotation fill pattern. The supported values for this option are:
BDiagPattern, CrossPattern, Dense1Pattern, Dense2Pattern, Dense3Pattern,
Dense4Pattern, Dense5Pattern, Dense6Pattern, Dense7Pattern,
DiagCrossPattern, FDiagPattern, HorPattern, NoBrush, SolidPattern,
VerPattern. The default fill pattern is NoBrush.
```
-pen_style line_style
```

Specifies the pen style. The supported values for this option are:
CustomDashLine, DashDotDotLine, DashDotLine, DashLine, DotLine, NoPen,
SolidLine, The default line style is SolidLine.
```
-pen_width line_width
```

Specifies the pen width. The default line width is 1.




```
-label label
```

Specifies the label text.
```
-horizontal_alignment left | center | right
```

Specifies the horizonal alignment of the label text inside bounding box of
annotation shape. This option is not applicable for annotation_shapes of type
line. The default value is center.
```
-vertical_alignment bottom | middle | top
```

Specifies the vertical alignment of the label text inside bounding box of
annotation shape. This option is not applicable for annotation_shapes of type
line. The default value is middle.
```
-orientation orientation
```

Specifies the orientation of a text label.

Valid values are

   - _MX_ (mirror around the X-axis)

   - _MXR90_ (mirror around the X-axis and rotate 90 degrees)

   - _MY_ (mirror around the Y-axis)

   - _MYR90_ (mirror around the Y-axis and rotate 90 degrees)

   - _R0_ (no rotation, which is the default)

   - _R90_ (rotate 90 degrees)

   - _R180_ (rotate 180 degrees)

   - _R270_ (rotate 270 degrees)
```
-bold_text
```

Specifies to use bold text for the label.
```
-elide_text left | middle | right
```

Specifies how to elide text with an ellipsis if the text string is too long. If this
option is omitted then text is truncated.

This option is mutually exclusive with the _-wrap_text_ option.
```
-wrap_text
```

Specifies to wrap long text lines for the label. If this option is omitted then text is
truncated.

This option is mutually exclusive with the _-elide_text_ option.




**Description**

This command creates a new circle, line, polygon, or rect annotaion_shape and returns a
collection that contains the new annotation_shape.

**Examples**

The following example creates a green annotation_shape of type rect.
```
prompt> create_annotation_shape -type rect -color green \\
-annotation_points {{200 200} {777 777}}
```

The following example creates a red annotation_shape of type line with width 2.
```
prompt> create_annotation_shape -type line -color red -line_width 2 \\
-annotation_points {{123 456} {789 12} {200 200}}
```

The following example creates an orange annotation_shape of type polygon and the text
label Anno1.
```
prompt> create_annotation_shape -type polygon \\
-annotation_points {{800 700} {850 700} {900 650} {900 600} {800 600}}
\\
-color orange -label "Anno1"
```

The following example creates a white annotation_shape of type circle with center in the
middle of cell 'I_CLOCK_GEN/I_PLL_PC' and radius 50.
```
prompt> create_annotation_shape -type circle \\
-annotation_points [list [get_cells I_CLOCK_GEN/I_PLL_PCI] {50+ 0+}]

```

**See Also**

 - create_annotation_symbol

 - create_annotation_text

 - get_annotation_points

 - get_annotation_shapes

 - gui_get_color_value

 - remove_annotation_shapes

###### **create_annotation_symbol**

Creates an annotation_shape object of type symbol or fit_symbol in the current design.




**Syntax**
```
collection create_annotation_symbol
-type custom | diamond | square | triangle | x
-origin annotation_point
[-name annotation_name ]
[-category category_name]
[-fit_symbol]
[-width width ]
[-height height ]
[-size size ]
[-color color ]
[-fill fill ]
[-pen_style pen_style ]
[-pen_width pen_width ]
[-orientation orientation ]
[-file file_path ]
```

**Data Types**
```
annotation_point  location descriptor
annotation_name   string
category_name    string
width        float
height        float
size        integer
color        string
fill        string
pen_style      string
pen_width      integer
orientation     string
file_path      string
```

**Arguments**
```
-type custom | diamond | square | triangle | x
```

Specifies the type of annotation_shape of symbol. There are four built-in
symbols: diamond, square, triangle, and x (cross). For the custom symbol,
specify the input file in SVG format by using the -file option.

This is a required option.
```
-origin annotation_point
```

Specifies the annotation text origin point. The point is specified by a tool
command language (Tcl) list of the following format:

   - {<coord_x> <coord_y>} a fixed, absolute {x y} point

   - {<anchor_collection>} a point that follows an anchor object




   - {<anchor_collection> <position> <offset_x> <offset_y>} a point that follows
an anchor object at the specified position and offset

   - {<offset_x><+/-> <offset_y><+/->} a point that follows the location of the
previous point in the list, at the specified offset

The first format describes a simple fixed point at an absolute coordinate.

The second format specifies that the point follow the center of the anchor object,
where "center" is the center of the largest box that can be contained within the
boundary of an anchor object.

The third format specifies that the point follow the anchor object at the specified
offset with respect to the specified position. The x and y offset values can either
be absolute distances or percentage values (which are appended with '%'). The
valid position values are as follows:

   - center: The center of the largest box within the anchor object

   - bbox_center: The center of the bounding box of the anchor object

   - bbox_ll: The lower-left corner of the bounding box of the anchor object

   - bbox_ul: The upper-left corner of the bounding box of the anchor object

   - bbox_lr: The lower-right corner of the bounding box of the anchor object

   - bbox_ur: The upper-left corner of the bounding box of the anchor object

This is a required option.
```
-name annotation_name
```

Specifies the name of the annotation_shape. The name might not contain
the special character '/'. If unspecified, the command generates a name
automatically using the prefix "ANNOTATION_SHAPE" with a system-generated
number appended.
```
-category category_name
```

Specifies the name of the category the annotation_shape object. The category
maybe used for grouping of annotation shapes into separate sets. If unspecified,
the category will not be assigned for the annotation_shape.
```
-fit_symbol
```

Creates the rectangle based fit_symbol annotation shape.
```
-width width
```

Specifies the width of a fit_symbol annotation_shape object. The value must be
more than 0.




If you use this option without "-fit_symbol", the tool issues an error.
```
-height height
```

Specifies the height of a fit_symbol annotation_shape object. The value must be
more than 0.

If you use this option without "-fit_symbol", the tool issues an error.
```
-size font_size
```

Specifies the size of symbol in pixels. The default size of a symbol is 16. The
range is from 3 to 100.
```
-color color
```

Specifies the annotation color. You can use a predefined color string, such
as white, red, green, blue, yellow, and so forth, or a hexadecimal RGB value,
such as #AA6633. The default annotation color is white. Annotations use colors
from the qt color palette by default. Colors from other color palettes might be
used by specifying a color name qualified with a palette name. For example,
"red:highlight" specifies the red color from the highlight palette. Available
palettes are qt, highlight, highcontrast, and style. Use gui_get_color_value
command to report on color names and values available in a palette.
```
-fill pattern
```

Specifies the annotation fill pattern. The supported values for this option are:
BDiagPattern, CrossPattern, Dense1Pattern, Dense2Pattern, Dense3Pattern,
Dense4Pattern, Dense5Pattern, Dense6Pattern, Dense7Pattern,
DiagCrossPattern, FDiagPattern, HorPattern, NoBrush, SolidPattern, and
VerPattern. The default fill pattern is NoBrush.
```
-pen_style line_style
```

Specifies the annotation line style. The supported values for this option are:
CustomDashLine, DashDotDotLine, DashDotLine, DashLine, DotLine, NoPen,
and SolidLine. The default line style is SolidLine.
```
-pen_width line_width
```

Specifies the annotation line width. The default line width is 1 pixel.
```
-orientation orientation
```

Specifies the orientation of an annotation symbol.

Valid values are

   - _MX_ (mirror around the X-axis)

   - _MXR90_ (mirror around the X-axis and rotate 90 degrees)




   - _MY_ (mirror around the Y-axis)

   - _MYR90_ (mirror around the Y-axis and rotate 90 degrees)

   - _R0_ (no rotation, which is the default)

   - _R90_ (rotate 90 degrees)

   - _R180_ (rotate 180 degrees)

   - _R270_ (rotate 270 degrees)
```
-file file_path
```

Specifies the location of symbol file in SVG format. Only <path> elements
should be used to draw symbol shapes. All <path> commands with exception of
‘elliptical Arc’ are supported.

The custom symbol files can be placed in a annotation symbol directory and
accessed by file name only. Annotation symbol directory can be set with
application option: set_app_options –name gui.annotation_symbol_dir –value
<dir>.

The SVG files are parsed once and cached to make rendering fast.

The color, line style, and fill are set from the corresponding options. Any SVG
editor maybe used for creating and editing symbols.

This is a required option for symbol type "custom".

**Description**

This command creates new annotaion_shape of type symbol and returns a collection that
contains the new annotation_shape. The annotation symbol is zoom-independent and
its size does not alter when you change the zoom level for viewed physical design in the
block window.

**Examples**

The following example creates a red diamond annotation_shape symbol with CrossPattern
fill.
```
prompt> create_annotation_symbol -type diamond -origin {430.490 629.800}
\\
-name annoDiamond -size 15 -color red -fill CrossPattern \\
-line_style SolidLine -line_width 2
```

The following example creates a green square annotation_shape symbol with
SolidPatterm fill.
```
prompt> create_annotation_symbol -type square -origin {534.440 629.800}
\\

```



```
-name annoSquare -size 15 -color green -fill SolidPattern \\
-line_style DotLine -line_width 1
```

The following example creates a blue triangle annotation_shape symbol in the center of
cell 'I_CLOCK_GEN/I_PLL_PC' with Dense7Pattern fill.
```
prompt> create_annotation_symbol -type triangle \\
-origin [list [get_cells I_CLOCK_GEN/I_PLL_PCI]] -name annoTriangle
-size 15 \\
-color blue -fill Dense7Pattern -line_style SolidLine -line_width 1

```

**See Also**

 - create_annotation_shape

 - create_annotation_text

 - get_annotation_points

 - get_annotation_shapes

 - gui_get_color_value

 - remove_annotation_shapes

 - set_app_options

###### **create_annotation_text**

Creates an annotation_shape object of type text in the current design.

**Syntax**
```
collection create_annotation_text
-text text_string
-origin annotation_point
[-name annotation_name ]
[-category  category_name ]
[-font_size font_size ]
[-color color ]
[-horizontal_alignment left | center | right]
[-vertical_alignment bottom | middle | top]
[-orientation orientation ]
[-bold_text]
```

**Data Types**
```
annotation_point  location descriptor
annotation_name   string
category_name    string
color        string
font_size      integer

```



```
orientation     string
text_string     string
```

**Arguments**
```
-text
```

Specifies the annotation text string.

This is a required option.
```
-origin annotation_point
```

Specifies the annotation text origin point. The point is specified by a tool
command language (Tcl) list of the following format:

   - {<coord_x> <coord_y>} a fixed, absolute {x y} point

   - {<anchor_collection>} a point that follows an anchor object

   - {<anchor_collection> <position> <offset_x> <offset_y>} a point that follows
an anchor object at the specified position and offset

The first format describes a simple fixed point at an absolute coordinate.

The second format specifies that the point follow the center of the anchor object,
where "center" is the center of the largest box that can be contained within the
boundary of an anchor object.

The third format specifies that the point follow the anchor object at the specified
offset with respect to the specified position. The x and y offset values can either
be absolute distances or percentage values (which are appended with '%'). The
valid position values are as follows:

   - center: The center of the largest box within the anchor object

   - bbox_center: The center of the bounding box of the anchor object

   - bbox_ll: The lower-left corner of the bounding box of the anchor object

   - bbox_ul: The upper-left corner of the bounding box of the anchor object

   - bbox_lr: The lower-right corner of the bounding box of the anchor object

   - bbox_ur: The upper-left corner of the bounding box of the anchor object

This is a required option.
```
-name annotation_name
```

Specifies the name of the annotation_shape. The name might not contain
the special character '/'. If unspecified, the command generates a name




automatically using the prefix "ANNOTATION_SHAPE" with a system-generated
number appended.
```
-category category_name
```

Specifies the name of the category the annotation_shape object. The category
maybe used for grouping of annotation shapes into separate sets. If unspecified,
the category will not be assigned for the annotation_shape.
```
-font_size font_size
```

Specifies the size of an application font in points. There are approximately 72
(72.272) points in one inch. The default font size is 10. The range is from 1 to
100.
```
-color color
```

Specifies the annotation color. You can use a predefined color string, such
as white, red, green, blue, yellow, and so forth, or a hexadecimal RGB value,
such as #AA6633. The default annotation color is white. Annotations use colors
from the qt color palette by default. Colors from other color palettes might be
used by specifying a color name qualified with a palette name. For example,
"red:highlight" specifies the red color from the highlight palette. Available
palettes are qt, highlight, highcontrast, and style. Use gui_get_color_value
command to report on color names and values available in a palette.
```
-horizontal_alignment left | center | right
```

Specifies the horizontal alignment of the text with respect to the origin point. The
default is center.
```
-vertical_alignment bottom | middle | top
```
