###### **report_clock_gating**

Reports the details and summary of clock gating in the design.

**Syntax**

status _report_clock_gating_
```
[-gating_elements]
[-gated]
[-ungated]
[-type clock_gate | self_gate | fanin_seqcg]
[-origin tool_inserted | pre_existing]
[-multi_stage]
```

**Arguments**
```
-gating_elements
```

Reports the names of all clock-gating elements, along with their reference
names, connected nets, level and whether they have been inserted
automatically by the tool ("Tool-Inserted"), or manually by the user ("PreExisting").
```
-gated
```

Reports the names of all clock gated registers, along with the names of
clock-gating elements and their levels, and whether they have been inserted
automatically by the tool ("Tool-Inserted"), or manually by the user ("PreExisting").
```
-ungated
```

Reports the names of all registers that are not clock gated at all, or are
only gated by pre-existing clock gates and, the reason why they are not
gated by the tool. If self-gating is enabled through application option
_compile.clockgate.self_gating_, an additional section is displayed, showing the
reasons why self-gating was not inserted for each listed register. Similarly, when
application option _compile.clockgate.fanin_sequential_ is enabled, an additional




section is displayed showing the reasons why fanin-based sequential clock
gating was not inserted for each listed register. The additional histogram report
on ungating reasons contains a breakdown of the number of registers, the
percentage of each, the breakdown of bits, and their respective percentage
based on the ungating reason. The histogram is sorted in descending order
based on the number of registers for each ungating reason.
```
-type { clock_gate | self_gate | fanin_seqcg }
```

Specifies the type of the clock gate cells to be reported when using _-gated_ or
_-gating_elements_ options. The type can be _clock_gate_, _self_gate_, _fanin_seqcg_,
or combinations of them. Regardless of the value passed to the _-type_ option,
if there are self-gates in the current design, the self-gating summary is shown.
Similarly, if there are fanin-based sequential clock gates in the design, the faninbased sequential clock gating summary is displayed.
```
-origin { tool_inserted | pre_existing }
```

Specifies the origin of the clock gates to be reported. The origin can be
_tool_inserted_, _pre_existing_, or both. When using _tool_inserted_ combined with
_-gating_elements_ or _-gated_ options, those reports are limited to the clock gates
inserted by the tool. The summary report still includes information about all
clock gates. When using _pre_existing_ combined with _-gating_elements_ or _-gated_
options, those reports are limited to the clock gates inserted manually by the
you. The summary report still includes information about all clock gates. If
_tool_inserted_ and _pre_existing_ are used together, or neither are used, every
report considers all clock gates.
```
-multi_stage
```

Reports multi-stage clock-gating metrics, including the total number of multi
stage clock gates, the average fanout of multi stage clock gates, and the
average number of clock-gate stages.

**Description**

The _report_clock_gating_ command reports information about clock-gating cells and gated
or ungated registers in the current design. The following cells are not considered for clockgating and hence are not included in the “Total number of registers” reported:
```
• sequential cells with more than one clock pin,
• dual-edge triggered sequential cells,
• latches,
• memories, macro cells and black boxes.
```

Irrespective of the use of any option, the command always prints at the end a summary
report, including this information:
```
• The total number of clock gates in the design.
• The number and percentage of tool-inserted clock gates.

```



```
• The number and percentage of pre-existing clock gates.
• The number and percentage of gated registers.
• The number and percentage of registers gated by tool-inserted clock
gates.
• The number and percentage of registers gated by pre-existing clock
gates.
• The number and percentage of ungated registers.
• The total number of registers.
• The maximum number of clock gate levels.
```

If the design contains multibit registers, the summary report also includes information
about bitwidth, and a table with the multibit composition of the gated/ungated registers is
displayed.

The clock gate levels are counted from clock source to registers.

If the design contains self-gates, the summary report also includes an additional table with
the following information:
```
• The total number of self-gates in the design.
• The number and percentage of self-gated registers.
• The number and percentage of not self-gated registers.
• The total number of registers.
```

If the design contains multibit registers, a bitwidth column is added to the self-gating
summary table.

If the design contains fanin-based sequential clock gates, the summary report also
includes an additional table with the following information:
```
• The total number of fanin-based sequential clock gates in the design.
• The number and percentage of fanin-based sequentially-gated registers
and their bitwidth.
• The number and percentage of registers not sequentially gated and their
bitwidth.
• The total number of registers and their bitwidth.
```

Clock gates inserted by the tool are named according to the following pattern:
```
prefix_bank_name_number
```

For regular clock gates, the string 'prefix' is defined by application option
_compile.clockgate.clock_gate_name_prefix_ . For self-gates, it is controlled by application
option _compile.clockgate.self_gate_name_prefix_ . For fanin-based sequential clock gates,
'prefix' is equal to "seq_clock_gate_fi".

The string 'bank_name' typically matches the name of some of the gated registers, and the
'number' at the end is only added when it is required to prevent name collisions.

Clock gates whose name matches the described pattern are recognized as "Tool-Inserted"
clock gates, otherwise they are recognized as "Pre-Existing". Given the classification is




based on naming, it is possible that clock gates inserted by the user in the RTL might be
recognized unexpectedly as "Tool-Inserted", instead of "Pre-Existing".

**Examples**

The following example shows a summary report generated with the _report_clock_gating_
command issued without any option.

###### **report_clock_gating_check**

Displays clock gating check information for the specified pins.

**Syntax**

status _report_clock_gating_checks_
```
[-significant_digits digits ]
[-nosplit]
[ object_list ]
```

**Data Types**
```
digits    int
object_list  list
```

**Arguments**
```
-significant_digits digits
```

Specifies the number of digits to the right of the decimal point to
report. Allowed values are 0-13; the default is determined by the
_shell.common.report_default_significant_digits_ application option, whose default
is 2. Use this option if you want to override the default.
```
-nosplit
```

Most of the design information is listed in fixed-width columns. If the information
for a given field exceeds the width of the column, the next field begins on a new




line, starting in the correct column. _-nosplit_ prevents line splitting and facilitates
writing scripts to extract information from the report output.
```
object_list
```

Specifies a list of cells, pins, clocks or design objects for report.

**Description**

The _report_clock_gating_checks_ command generates two tables. The first table displays
information about all the clock gating checks, including cell, enable pin, clock pin, level,
clock (check w.r.t. a specific clock, or all clocks if none is given), attribute (inferred, or icg),
and what user settings have affected its S/H/R/F values and check level. The attribute
indicates where the clock gating check was originally defined. It can be either inferred, or
defined by library cell.

If there are multiple settings that affect a clock gating check, it is an error condition. The
conflicts should be resolved by the user.

The second table displays information about user settings that affect the clock gating
checks displayed in the first table, including netlist object of clock it is set on, S/H/
R/F check values, level, and file/line where the relevant _set_clock_gating_check_ and
_remove_clock_gating_check_ commands are defined. If there are no effective user settings
that affect clock gating checks, the second table will not display.

**Multicorner-Multimode Support**

This command works only on the current scenario.

**Examples**

The following example reports all clock gating check information.
```
prompt> report_clock_gating_checks
****************************************
Report : clock_gating_check
Design : cgbox
Scenario: default
Version:
Date  :
****************************************
Updating Clock Gating Locations
Inferring 6 clock-gating checks.
Clock gating checks:
Cell     EnablePin ClockPin High/Low Clock     Attr  User
Settings
----------------------------------------------------------------------------U4      E     CK    Low           L   1
U1      A     B     High           I   2
U2      B     A     High           I   2

```



```
U3      A     B     High           I   3
U5      A     B     High           I   3
U9      S0    B     Low           I   4
U9      S0    A     Low    clk1      I   5
Attr: I:auto inferred, L:library cell defined

User clock gating settings:
Rise     Fall
ID Object  Setup Hold  Setup Hold  High/Low  File/Line
----------------------------------------------------------------------------1  U4/CK   --   --   --   --   Low     clock_gating2.tcl,
line 79
2  U1/A   4.00  3.00  3.00  3.00  --     clock_gating2.tcl,
line 87
3  U8/Y   2.00  2.00  2.00  2.00  --     clock_gating2.tcl,
line 71

line 51

line 61
1

```

###### **report_clock_gating_efficiency**

Reports the clock-gating efficiency of a design




**Syntax**

status _report_clock_gating_efficiency_
```
[-bin_size bin_size ]
[-by_register]
[-by_clock_gate]
[-sort_by sort_criteria]
```

**Data Types**
```
bin_size  integer
sort_by  String
```

**Arguments**
```
-bin_size bin_size
```

Specify the bin size for the histogram-based gating efficiency report. By default,
the value is set to five, but the user can change it to get more efficient histogram
information. This option is mutually exclusive with the options _-by_clock_gate_,
_-by_register, and -sort_by options._
```
-by_register
```

Reports the gating efficiency for each register. The report includes the name of
a register, toggle rate for the D pins, Q pins, and the gating efficiency for each
register.
```
-by_clock_gate
```

Reports the gating efficiency for each clock gate. The report includes the name,
stage, direct child, and gating efficiency for each clock gate.
```
-sort_by { gating_efficiency | name | stage }}
```

Reports the gating efficiency based on a sorting criterion. The criteria can be
_gating_efficiency_, _name_, or _stage_ .

**Description**

This command uses toggle rates to report the gating efficiency of a design, where the
toggle saving for a register is defined as the ratio of the toggle rate at the clock pin of the
register to the toggle rate of the clock. Since the quality of the gating efficiency calculation
depends on the toggle rate, the command propagates switching activities before each
efficiency computation. The default report summarizes the effectiveness of clock gating
for a design in the form of histogram categorizing efficiency into bins. For each bin, the
number of gated registers and their equivalent bitwidth is also provided.

Detailed information about individual clock gates and registers can be gathered by using
the _by_clock_gate or by_registers option. Further, using the sort_by option provides more_
_insight into gating efficiency._




This command reports efficiency based on clock, hence the design must have valid clock
defined and at least one scenario with dynamic analysis enabled.

**Multicorner-Multimode Support**

This command works only in the current scenario.

**Examples**

The following example shows a default summary report generated by the
_report_clock_gating_efficiency_ command:

###### **report_clock_gating_enable_condition**

Reports clock gate enable signals.

**Syntax**

status _report_clock_gating_enable_condition_
```
-objects
[-nosplit]
[-flat]
```

**Arguments**
```
-objects
```

List of cells to be reported.
```
-nosplit
```

Option to display enable conditions on a single line.
```
-flat
```

Reports the enable signals of each clock gate through hierarchical ports.

**Description**

Reports the enable conditions of all clock-gating cells that are connected to registers or
to another clock gate. A Boolean equation is used to represent the enable conditions
as a sum of products: '&' is the AND operation, '|' is the OR operation and, '!' is the NOT




operation. When describing an enable function, you might use reference points (invariant
points) that require a Boolean variable. These reference points represent the following:
```
• Output pins of the register (since Q and QN pins are two different
variables)
• Ports
• Output pins of any sequential cell, black box, or unsupported cell
• Hierarchical boundaries
```

**Examples**

The following example shows a report generated with _report_clock_gating_ command
issued with -objects option
```
prompt> report_clock_gating_enable_condition -objects [get_clock_gates]
------------------------------------------------------------------------------Enable Conditions Report
------------------------------------------------------------------------------Clock Gating Bank          |     Gated Register
Clock_gate_1            |      Register[1]
|      Register[2]
|      Register[3]
Enable condition:
!a |
b & c
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

###### **report_clock_gating_objects**

Reports the object inclusion options that have been explicitly set for gating with
_set_clock_gating_objects_ .

**Syntax**

status _report_clock_gating_objects_




```
[-objects object_list ]
```

**Data Types**
```
object_list   list
```

**Arguments**
```
-objects object_list
```

Reports all objects in _object_list_, even if they have not been explicitly set for
gating with _set_clock_gating_objects_ .

**Description**

This command reports the settings that were explicitly set with the
_set_clock_gating_objects_ command. The report displays a table with the following
columns:

 - The action, set with _set_clock_gating_objects_ command, the default values or its
inherited values when applicable. The possible values are Include, Exclude or Force.

 - The enable source option, set with _set_clock_gating_objects_ command, the default
values or its inherited values when applicable. The possible values are Both, Prefer
Enable Pin, Prefer Feedback Loop, Enable Pin Only and Feedback Loop Only and "-".

 - The instance for which the setting values are associated.

**Examples**

The following examples will use a design with two hierarchies (mid1, mid2), below the top
level design, named top, and one hierarchie (bot) below mid2. The four, top, mid1, mid2,
and top, have four registers each one.

The following example uses the next settings:
```
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -include reg_top1 -enable_source
enable_pin_only
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -force reg_top3 -enable_source
feedback_loop_only
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -exclude mid1/reg_mid0
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -include mid1/reg_mid1 -enable_source
prefer_feedback_loop
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -force mid1/reg_mid2 -enable_source
prefer_enable_pin
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -exclude mid1/reg_mid3
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -include mid2/reg_mid0 -enable_source
prefer_feedback_loop
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -force mid2/reg_mid1 -enable_source
prefer_feedback_loop
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -exclude mid2/reg_mid2

```



```
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -include mid2/reg_mid3 -enable_source
feedback_loop_only
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -force mid2/bot/reg_mid0 -enable_source
prefer_enable_pin
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -exclude mid2/bot/reg_mid1
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -force mid2/bot/reg_mid3 -enable_source
prefer_feedback_loop
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -include mid2/bot -enable_source
prefer_feedback_loop
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -force mid2 -enable_source
prefer_enable_pin
prompt> set_clock_gating_objects -force top -enable_source
prefer_feedback_loop

###### **report_clock_gating_options**

Reports the options set for clock-gating using the _set_clock_gating_options_ command.

[-nosplit]

```

Report the structural options for objects in the _object_list_ . Hierarchical instances,
power domains and designs are valid objects.
```
-nosplit
```

Prevents line splitting and facilitates writing applications to extract information
from the report output. By default, information is listed in fixed-width columns.

**Description**

By default, only those settings set explicitly using the _set_clock_gating_options_ command
are included in the report.




When you use the _-objects_ option, the report shows the settings of the specified objects. In
this case, the value displayed for each object corresponds to an explicitly specified setting,
or an inherited setting. The report displays a table with the following columns:

 - The names of the objects to which the setting values are associated.

 - The value that corresponds to the Minimum cumulative Bitwidth that a clock gate
can open in each object. The value can be set using the _set_clock_gating_options_
command; if not, the default is 3.

 - The value that corresponds to the maximum number of registers that a clock gate can
open. This value can be set using the command _set_clock_gating_options_ ; if it is not
set, the fanout of a clock gate is unlimited (the default).
