location is the center point of the pin in the block coordinate system, and the
layer is the layer that the pin is created in. This is primarily used in cases where
multiple pins shapes can be created for the same port on the block (EEQ pins).
This option can only be used in combination with object_type pg_routing or
signal_routing. By default, this option is false. Note that this terminal naming
option will only be observed in the push-down of routing for nets that have NOT
been specified to allow feedthroughs.




```
-collinear_margin distance
```

Specifies a distance within which PG routes parallel to (but not overlapping) the
block boundary are considered collinear PG routes. See a complete description
of this option under _pg_routing_ in the _-object_type_ description.
```
-pin_meet_fatwire_rule true | false
```

Ensures that the size of the PG pin is big enough to trigger fat-wire spacing
rules within the block, when this option is true. By default, this option is false. For
more information, see the description under _pg_routing_ .
```
-create_pg_feedthrough true | false
```

Create PG feedthroughs for PG terminals and cells. By default, this option is
false. For more information, see the description under _pg_routing_ .

**Description**

This command sets options for the _push_down_objects_ command. You can review the
options with the _report_push_down_object_options_ command.

**Examples**

The following example sets _block_action_ to _copy_ and _create_pin_shape_ for _pg_routing_
pushing down.
```
prompt> set_push_down_object_options -object_type pg_routing \\
-block_action {copy create_pin_shape}
```

The following example sets _block_action_ to _copy_ and _create_pin_shape_ for _signal_routing_
pushing down.
```
prompt> set_push_down_object_options -object_type signal_routing \\
-block_action {copy create_pin_shape}
```

The following example sets the block actions for cell pushdown to include
retain_obsolete_ports.
```
prompt> set_push_down_object_options -object_type cells \\
-block_action {copy retain_obsolete_ports}
```

The following example sets the "cells" object-type-specific option _-allow_multi_rail_cells_ .
```
prompt> set_push_down_object_options -object_type cells \\
-allow_multi_rail_cells true

```



**See Also**

 - push_down_objects

 - remove_push_down_object_options

 - report_push_down_object_options

###### **set_pvt**

Sets operating process label, process number, temperature and voltage for one or more
corners, for hierachical instances or top level of the current design.

**Syntax**

string _set_pvt_
```
[-process_label label ]
[-early_process_label label ]
[-process_number number ]
[-early_process_number number ]
[-voltage voltage ]
[-min_voltage voltage ]
[-dynamic_voltage voltage ]
[-min_dynamic_voltage voltage ]
[-temperature temperature ]
[-min_temperature temperature ]
[-clear]
[-cells cell_list ]
[-corners corner_list ]
```

**Data Types**
```
label  string
number  float
voltage  float
temperature float
corner_list collection
cell_list  collection
```

**Arguments**
```
label

-process_label label
```

The process label to be used for late analysis. A value of "*" represents a
wildcard: any available process label will be acceptable.




```
-early_process_label label
```

The process label to be used for early analysis. When not specified, value from
-process_label option is used. A value of "*" represents a wildcard: any available
process label will be acceptable.
```
-process_number number
```

The process number to be used for late analysis.
```
-early_process_number label
```

The process number to be used for early analysis. When not specified, value
from -process_number option is used.
```
-voltage voltage
```

Specifies the operating voltage for the maximum delay(slowest) case. If the
_-min_voltage_ option is not given, this value will also be used for the minimum
delay(fastest) case.
```
-min_voltage voltage
```

Specifies the operating voltage for the minimum delay(fastest) case. If not
specified, value from _-voltage_ option is used.
```
-dynamic_voltage voltage
```

Specifies the dynamic voltage for the maximum delay case. If the
_-min_dynamic_voltage_ option is not given then, this value will also be used for
the minimum delay(fastest) case. The dynamic portion is considered during
pessimism removal. The dynamic component of voltage is provided as a
negative value in this case. The static voltage is determined by subtracting the
dynamic component from the regular voltage.
```
-min_dynamic_voltage voltage
```

Specifies the dynamic voltage for the minimum delay case. If not specified,
value from _-dynamic_voltage_ option is used.
```
-temperature temperature
```

The late operating temperature to be used. If _-min_temperature_ option is not
given then, this value is also used for early analysis.
```
-min_temperature temperature
```

The early temperature, if -temperature is not specified.
```
-corners corner_list
```

The corner(s) to apply the pvt values to. If this option is not given, the current
corner is assumed.




```
-cells cell_list
```

Specifies a collection of hierarchical cell instances to apply the pvt. If this option
is not given, the process label is applied to the top level of current the design.
When top-level PVTs are cleared, PVT values are set to library default values.
```
-clear
```

This option, clears pvt values set by previous set_pvt command(s) or individual
commands, for the specified cells using _-cells_ option. If _-cells_ is not specified,
then it clears top level pvts.

**Description**

This command is used set the process label, process number, voltages and temperatures
that will be used for timing analysis and delay calculation. The _-cells_ option specifies a
collection of hierarchical instances of 3DIC or other blocks or sub-blocks. If no _-cells_ option
is given, the given parameters will used for the top.

It is often necessary to specify one set of PVTs for the main libraries, and different
PVTs for cells(3DIC/IP blocks). In the past, this was accomplished by giving separate
_set_process_, _set_voltage_ and, _set_temperature_ commands. This command combines
process, voltage and temperature settings into a single command with simple setup
specially useful for 3DIC blocks. More complex features, like library specific labels,
voltages on PG pins and clock-network specific settings are not supported in this
command. User can continue to use separate commands for PVTs, if needed.

With -clear option, the command does not clear all pvts in the design, like reset_pvt
command. It only clears PVTs on specified instance(s) with _-cells_ option, or it clears toplevel PVTs.

**Multicorner-Multimode Support**

By default, this command works on the current corner. To specify a different corner, use
the _-corners_ option.

**Examples**

This example shows how to set the early and late process labels to the same values for
the top.
```
prompt> set_pvt -process_label WORST
```

This example shows how to set the early and late process labels to different values for an
entire design.
```
prompt> set_pvt -process_label WORST -early_process_label BEST
```

This example shows how to give process labels and temperatures for the design top, as
well as different process labels for specific cells.




```
prompt> set_pvt -late WORST -early BEST -temperature 125 -min_temperature
25
prompt> set_pvt -late LATE -early EARLY -temperature 100 -min_temperature
55 -cells [get_cells blkInst1]
```

This example shows how to give process labels, process numberis, voltages and
temperatures for the top level for corner c1.
```
prompt> set_pvt -process_label LATE -early_process_label EARLY \
-process_number 1.0 -early_process_number 1.1 \
-temperature 125 -min_temperature 25 \
-voltage 1.08 -min_voltage 0.9 \
-dynamic_voltage 1.07 -min_dynamic_voltage 1.07 -corner [get_corner
c1]
```

Following examples shows how to clear PVTs for the top level and for instance block_die1,
respectively.
```
prompt> set_pvt -clear
prompt> set_pvt -clear -cells [get_cell block_die1]

```

**See Also**

 - report_pvt

 - set_process_number

 - set_temperature

 - set_voltage

 - reset_pvt

###### **set_pvt_configuration**

Sets the allowable PVTs for the current session.

**Syntax**

string _set_pvt_configuration_
```
[-add]
[-name new_rule_name ]
[-rule rule_name ]
[-clear_filter filter_type ]
[-process_labels label_list ]
[-process_numbers number_list ]
[-voltages voltage_list ]
[-temperatures temp_list ]

```



**Data Types**
```
filter_type    string
label_list     list of string
number_list    list of float
voltage_list    list of float
temp_list     list of float
rule_name     string
new_rule_name   string
```

**Arguments**
```
-add
```

Add a new rule to the configuration, making it the current rule, and apply the rest
of the arguments to the new rule. This option is exclusive with _-rule_ .
```
-name new_rule_name
```

Used along with -add, optionally gives the new rule a specific name. Without
_-name_, new rules receive names like rule_1. This option is exclusive with _-rule_ .
```
-rule rule_name
```

Make _rule_name_ the current rule, and apply the rest of the arguments to it. This
option is exclusive with _-add_ .
```
-clear_filter filter_type
```

Specifies which filters you want to clear, that is, which of process label, process
number, voltage, or temperature you do not want filtered. This is applied to the
current rule before any of the other filters. Valid values are:

   - _all_ Clears all filters

   - _process_label_ Clears only the process label filter

   - _process_number_ Clears only the process number filter

   - _voltage_ Clears only the voltage filter

   - _temperature_ Clears only the temperature filter
```
-process_labels label_list
```

Specifies process labels that you want included in the current rule in the
configuration.
```
-process_numbers number_list
```

Specifies process numbers that you want included in the current rule in the
configuration.




```
-voltages voltage_list
```

Specifies voltages that you want included in the current rule in the configuration.
```
-temperatures temp_list
```

Specifies temperatures that you want included in the current rule in the
configuration.

**Description**

The _set_pvt_configuration_ command is used to limit the process, voltage, and temperature
combinations which are allowed in the current session. The concept is the same across all
applications using the command, but there are details which vary. These will be described
below.

The configuration is a sequence of rules, each of which specifies process labels, process
numbers, voltages, and temperatures to match. Generally, if you want all data matching a
specific set of PVTs, a single rule is sufficient. When you have a specific subset of many
PVTs that you want to match, multiple rules are needed. See examples below. New rules
are created with _-add_ . If desired, you can name a new rule with _-name_ . Otherwise, they
are automatically named. You can change the rule that the command is operating on
with the _-rule_ option. The result of the command is the name of the current rule. If neither
_-add_ or _-rule_ is used, the current rule is used. If no rules exist, an initial rule is created for
you. At least one of the filtering options - _-process_labels_, _-process_numbers_, _-voltages_,
_-temperatures_ and _-clear_filter_ - is required if you use _-add_ or _-rule_ .

By default, all PVTs are allowed. Each of the filters allows a list of values, and these add to
previous values already in the configuration. If you want to overwrite a particular filter, you
would use the _-clear_filter_ option in combinations with the other arguments which change
a rule in the configuration. You can also do the same thing in two commands: one to clear,
and one to add. Note that rules with no constraints are deleted.

The output from the _set_pvt_configuration_ command shows the current configuration. For
categories that are unfiltered in a particular rules (that is, for which you have not provided
any specific configuration), the output will say that all are included. See the examples
below. If you just want to show the current configuration, use the command without any
arguments.

**Configuration in the Library Manager**

In the library manager, the _set_pvt_configuration_ command limits the process, voltage,
and temperature combinations which a DB or .lib file can have in the session. As these
files are read, they are compared to the rules in the configuration to determine if they meet
the criteria. If they do not pass, they are excluded from the session. This allows you to
declare the needed processes, voltages and temperatures, then cast a wide net over a
set of DB or .lib files, without having to depend on a file naming convention, as the rules
are applied to the data in the file (or data added to the file when it was read). The voltage




values considered are the nominal values, that is, the values from a default operating
condition. Other voltage rails are not considered.

Note that the configuration does not apply to the aggregate, edit, or verification flows.

For all other flows, the _set_pvt_configuration_ command can be used before or after
_create_workspace_ . Changing the configuration after files have been read will enable,
disable, or reread files as needed. Changing the process of a library using _set_process_
may also have an impact on the configuration.

It is very possible to have a different number of files known to the configuration, available
from _get_libs_, or attached to the workspace (visible with _report_workspace_ ). The _get_libs_
command provides all libraries which have been successfully read (and not removed).
_report_workspace_ shows files which currently match the configuration. Finally, the
configuration internally keeps track of "greyed out" files - those which were passed to
_read_db_ or _read_lib_, may or may not have been read into memory, but do not match the
current configuration. There is an option to see the greyed out files in the GUI.

**Configuration in an Implementation Tool**

In an implementation tool, the _set_pvt_configuration_ command limits the process, voltage,
and temperature combinations which an NDM reference library can have have in the
session. In contrast to the library manager, the configuration must be established before
_open_lib_ is used. Changes made to the configuration are NOT applied to libraries that
are already open. If your current configuration blocks all panes in a particular library, a
warning will be issued for that library. If you have created a configuration, then any panes
that do match will be listed after _open_lib_ . If you have not created a configuration, all
panes match, and no messages are listed. If you have created a configuration which
is so restrictive that no panes match, a LIB-072 warning is issued. You can always use
_report_lib_ to show more information about the panes. One thing to be careful of is that if
the voltage in the design is changed or one is added. If that voltage is not covered by the
libs loaded with set_pvt_configuration, then closest match will be chosen.

**Examples**

The following example sets the configuration to allow any process label, any process
number, voltages 0.8 and 0.9, and temperatures 0, 125, and -40.
```
prompt> set_pvt_configuration -clear_filter all -voltages {0.8 0.9}
-temperatures {0 125 -40}
Current PVT Configuration
rule_1:
Process Labels : <All included>
Process Numbers: <All included>
Voltages    : 0.8, 0.9
Temperatures  : -40, 0, 125
rule_1
prompt>

```



To add the limitation for only process labels SS and FF:
```
prompt> set_pvt_configuration -process_labels {SS FF}
Current PVT Configuration
rule_1:
Process Labels : "FF", "SS"
Process Numbers: <All included>
Voltages    : 0.8, 0.9
Temperatures  : -40, 0, 125
rule_1
prompt>
```

Now if you read DB files and some are screened out you might see messages like the
following, which indicate that the file was not loaded. This would be expected based on the
setting from the previous example. The voltage does not match.
```
prompt> read_db [glob ${DBDIR}/*.db]
Information: Loading db file '/path/stdcell_ss_0.815V_0C.db' (FILE-007)
Warning: Did not load /path/stdcell_ss_0.815V_0C.db because its
PVT (label='SS', P=1.0, V=0.815, T=0) does not match the current
configuration (LM-133)
```

If you wanted to allow files which never had a process label applied, you do that with the
empty string. Assuming that all files had a process label, you would not see any messages
about file activation.
```
prompt> set_pvt_configuration -process_label [list ""]
Current PVT Configuration
rule_1:
Process Labels : "", "FF", "SS"
Process Numbers: <All included>
Voltages    : 0.8, 0.9
Temperatures  : -40, 0, 125
rule_1
prompt>
```

Numerical comparisons are made with a very tight tolerance. So 0.8 will not match 0.815..
In the library manager, if you realize that your voltages are really 0.815 and 0.92, you can
clear voltages without impact on the rest of the configuration, and apply new ones. Now,
the file that was screened out above is already known, so it is re-activated, and in this
case, re-read since it was never loaded into memory.
```
prompt> set_pvt_configuration -clear_filter voltage \\
-voltages [list 0.815 0.92]
Current PVT Configuration
rule_1:
Process Labels : "", "FF", "SS"
Process Numbers: <All included>
Voltages    : 0.815, 0.92

```



```
Temperatures  : -40, 0, 125
Information: Configuration change re-activates file
/path/stdcell_ss_0.815V_0C.db (LM-132)
Information: Loading db file '/path/stdcell_ss_0.815V_0C.db' (FILE-007)
rule_1
prompt>
```

In the library manager, if you were to remove a temperature that matches files, you would
see de-activation messages:
```
prompt> set_pvt_configuration -clear_filter temperature \\
-temperatures {125 -40}
rule_1:
Process Labels : "", "FF", "SS"
Process Numbers: <All included>
Voltages    : 0.815, 0.92
Temperatures  : -40, 125
Information: Configuration change de-activates file
/path/stdcell_ss_0.815V_0C.db (LM-132)
rule_1
prompt>
```

If you want to capture 0.88 volts but only for "SS", you could add a second rule:
```
prompt> set_pvt_configuration -add -process_label SS -voltages 0.88
rule_1:
Process Labels : "", "FF", "SS"
Process Numbers: <All included>
Voltages    : 0.815, 0.92
Temperatures  : -40, 125
rule_2:
Process Labels : "SS"
Process Numbers: <All included>
Voltages    : 0.88
Temperatures  : <All included>
rule_2
prompt>
```

Here is an example where multiple rules come into play. Let's say you have these panes in
a reference library and you want to use configuration to load panes 1 and 4:
```
Pane 0: process = "SS" (1), voltages: 0.6; temperatures: 0
Pane 1: process = "SS" (1), voltages: 1.2; temperatures: 0
Pane 2: process = "SS" (1), voltages: 1.2; temperatures: 125
Pane 3: process = "TT" (1), voltages: 0.6; temperatures: 0
Pane 4: process = "FF" (1), voltages: 0.6; temperatures: 0
Pane 5: process = "FF" (1), voltages: 0.7; temperatures: 125
Pane 6: process = "FF" (1), voltages: 0.9; temperatures: 125

```



You can use these commands and get the configuration shown:
```
set_pvt_configuration -voltages 1.2 -temperatures 0
set_pvt_configuration -add -name FF -process_label FF -voltages 0.6
Current PVT Configuration:
rule_1:
Process Labels : <All included>
Process Numbers: <All included>
Voltages    : 1.2
Temperatures  : 0
FF:
Process Labels : "FF"
Process Numbers: <All included>
Voltages    : 0.6
Temperatures  : <All included>
```

If you open this library, you will get the two panes you want:
```
prompt> open_lib p7.ndm
Information: Loading library file 'p7.ndm' (FILE-007)
Panes activated based on PVT configuration (7 possible panes):
Pane 1: process = "SS" (1), voltages: 1.2; temperatures: 0
Pane 4: process = "FF" (1), voltages: 0.6; temperatures: 0
```

You would not be able to achieve this with a single rule. If you tried to include the above
processes, voltage, and temperature in a single rule, it would match panes 0, 1 and 4. This
is where multiple rules can help.


**See Also**

 - open_lib

 - LM-133

 - LIB-070

 - LIB-071

 - LIB-072

 - LIB-073

###### **set_qor_data_metric_properties**

Specifies customized metric properties in QORsum table panels.

**Syntax**

status _set_qor_data_metric_properties_




```
-panel panel_name
-metric metric_list
[-group group_name ]
[-tooltip tooltip_text ]
[-color color_style ]
[-absolute_coloring true|false ]
[-light_threshold threshold_value ]
[-medium_threshold threshold_value ]
[-dark_threshold threshold_value ]
[-absolute_threshold abs_value ]
[-improves improve_style ]
[-visibility visibility ]
[-output output_dir ]
[-use_default_panel]
```

**Data Types**
```
panel_name       string
metric_list      list
group_name       string
tooltip_text      string
color_style      string
threshold_value    float
abs_value       float
improve_style     string
visibility       string
output_dir       string
```

**Arguments**
```
-panel panel_name
```

Specifies the name for the panel for which metric properties is customized. It
must be a summary or detailed table panel.
```
-metric metric_list
```

A list of metrics in the panel to customize. Whichever settings are applied with
this command call will be applied to all of the listed metrics.
```
-group group_name
```

Metrics can be organized into column groups in the QORsum report. Specify the
group name with this option. The default is no grouping.
```
-tooltip tooltip_text
```

Specify the descriptive text that is displayed when hovering the mouse over the
metric column header field in the QORsum report. By default, the tooltip includes
information about the metric properties but does not include any descriptive text
about the metric.




```
-color color_style
```

Specify the color style for the metric. By default, _improve_degrade_ mode is used
to show red and green coloring indicating improvement or degradation in that
metric. _none_ mode does no coloring. _different_ mode colors the metric value blue
if it differs from the baseline. _different_or_missing_ mode colors the metric value
blue if it differs from the baseline or if either that metric value or the baseline
metric value are not populated in the table.
```
-absolute_coloring true|false
```

Only relevant for _improve_degrade_ color mode. Normally coloring is done by
comparing the test run value to the baseline value and looking at the percentage
change. Red or green coloring is then applied based on the _-light_threshold_,
_-medium_threshold_, and _-dark_threshold_ values. If _-absolute_coloring true_,
then this comparison is done based on absolute values rather than percentage
values. This coloring mode is useful if you care about the absolute change in a
metric. For example, you want to color a power metric dark red if it degrades by
more than 2mW compared to the baseline.
```
-light_threshold threshold_value
```

For _improve_degrade_ style coloring, specifies the percentage delta between
the test and baseline metric value before it is colored in a light shade of red or
green. For example, a value of 2 means that a 2 percent change triggers light
coloring. The default is 0.5 (0.5 percent).
```
-medium_threshold threshold_value
```

For _improve_degrade_ style coloring, specifies the percentage delta between
the test and baseline metric value before it is colored in a medium shade of red
or green. For example, a value of 2 means that a 2 percent change triggers
medium coloring. The default is 2 (2 percent).
```
-dark_threshold threshold_value
```

For _improve_degrade_ style coloring, specifies the percentage delta between
the test and baseline metric value before it is colored in a dark shade of red or
green. For example, a value of 2 means that a 2 percent change triggers dark
coloring. The default is 10 (10 percent).
```
-absolute_threshold abs_threshold
```

For _improve_degrade_ style coloring, specifies the absolute delta between the
test and baseline metric value below which percentage-based coloring is not
applied. Any table fields with coloring suppressed by the absolute threshold
is shown in the QORsum with gray text. The default is no absolute threshold
(percentage-based coloring is not suppressed).




```
-improves improve_style
```

Specifies the way in which a method improves compared to the baseline, for the
_-color improve_degrade_ coloring mode. If a metric improves, it is colored green.
If it degrades, it is colored red. _larger_ means a metric improves as its value gets
bigger. _smaller_ means a metric improves as its value gets smaller. The default
_closer_to_zero_ means a metric improves when it approaches zero (when the
absolute value decreases).
```
-visibility visibility
```

Specified the default visibility mode for the metric. The supported visibility
modes are _visible_ and _hidden_ . A visible metric is displayed in the QORsum
report. A hidden metric is loaded into the QORsum report but is hidden by
default. Visibility must be enabled interactively through the QORsum _Metrics_
dialog box.
```
-output output_dir
```

Specifies the path to a _write_qor_data_ and _capture_qor_data_ output directory for
a run where the metrics should be configured. By default, metric configurations
are stored in memory until the _write_qor_data_ or _capture_qor_data_ commands
are called, and only then are they are stored to that commands' output directory.
```
-use_default_panel
```

If there is a name conflict between a default _write_qor_data_ panel and a custom
panel defined by _define_qor_data_panel_, by default the custom user-panel
customized. Use this option to customize the default panel instead.

**Description**

This command is used to configure the metric properties of QORsum summary and
detailed tables captured by either the _write_qor_data_ or _define_qor_data_panel_ command.
Every metric in a table (except for the frozen key column metrics of detailed tables) has
properties that affect how those metrics are displayed in the QORsum report.

This command has two required arguments _-panel_ and _-metric_ to specify the table panel
and the name of one or more metrics in that panel to configure.

The _-group_ and _-tooltip_ options affect the metric column header only, not the display of
metric values. Use _-group_ to put a metric into a group which is a collection of similar types
of metrics that are displayed together in the report. The _-tooltip_ option can be used to
give descriptive text in the tooltip that pops-up when hovering the pointer over the metric
column header in the QORsum report. This can be used to give information about how this
metric was computed or extracted from the tool, or a more complete description of what
the metric means if its name alone does not make it obvious.

The other options affect the way the metric data fields appear in the QORsum report.
The _-color_ option indicates whether to color a metric green and red as it improves and




degrades, or to color it blue when it differs from the baseline. Coloring can also be
suppressed with this option, for strictly informational metrics.

For metrics that are colored red and green, the _-light_threshold_, _-medium_threshold_, and
_-dark_threshold_ options are used to specify percentage delta thresholds between the
baseline and test run metric values at which the metric is colored with a light, medium, or
dark shade of red or green.

The _-absolute_threshold_ option is used to specify an absolute delta difference between the
baseline and test run metric below which the red and green coloring is suppressed. This
is useful for ignoring false violations due to comparing very small values. For example, if
the WNS degrades from -0.001 to -0.002, that is an insignificant change, but would show
up as a 100 percent degradation with a dark color. By specifying a reasonable absolute
thresholds, these kinds of "small change but large percentage change" violations can be
suppressed.

For metrics colored red and green, they also have an _-improves_ option to tell what way
they improve. The default is _closer_to_zero_, meaning that the metric gets better when its
absolute value decreases. This default works well for a majority of metrics whether they
have negative values (timing slack) or positive values (area). Use the _smaller_ setting to
say the metric improves as it gets smaller, or the _larger_ setting for metrics that improve as
they get larger.

By default metrics are displayed in their QORsum tables when viewing the report. Use
_-visibility hidden_ to load them into the report but hide them by default. Hidden metrics
can still be displayed by interactively toggling their display in the QORsum report Metrics
dialog box.

Metric properties also implicitly specify the order that the metric columns are shown in the
QORsum report. By default with no properties specified, they are displayed in the same
order as they appear in the table on disk. Any metrics with customized settings are shown
in columns to the left of any non-customized metrics. Customized metrics are shown in
the order they were customized by this command, from left to right. Metric groups take
precedence over these ordering rules. Groups are displayed in the order they are created,
and all metrics of a group are shown together. Their order within a group follows the
rules stated above. When customizing new metrics added to the default _write_qor_data_
summary tables with the _capture_qor_data_ command, they are always shown to the right
of any default metrics in those tables.

By default, all metric properties configurations are kept in memory until _write_qor_data_
or _define_qor_data_panel_ is called, and only then are they written to the output directory
specified by those commands. Use the _-output_ option of this command to immediately
write the metric properties to disk. This can be used to update metric properties after all
QoR data was already captured.




**Examples**
```
prompt> set_qor_data_metric_properties -panel "My Panel" -metric
"myMetric" \\
-group "My Group" -tooltip "This is my metric" \\
-absolute_threshold 0.05 -improves larger

```

**See Also**

 - write_qor_data

 - compare_qor_data

 - view_qor_data

 - set_qor_data_options

 - capture_qor_data

 - set_qor_data_metric_properties

###### **set_qor_data_options**

Configures QoR data captured by the _write_qor_data_ command.

**Syntax**

status _set_qor_data_options_
```
[-output output_dir ]
[-label_order list_of_labels ]
[-run_name name ]
[-gzip_reports true|false ]
[-dynamic_scenario scenario_name_or_object ]
[-leakage_scenario scenario_name_or_object ]
[-clock_name clock_or_skew_group_name ]
[-clock_scenario scenario_name_or_object ]
[-color_hierarchies hierarchy_list ]
[-check_drcs_from_user_shapes true|false ]
[-check_drcs_from_frozen_shapes true|false ]
[-report_global_timing_multiple_categories true|false ]
[-vt_and_device_group_report_mode standard|datapath ]
[-pba_mode none|path|exhaustive|ml_exhaustive ]
[-link_source_files true|false ]
```

**Data Types**
```
output_dir        string
list_of_labels      list
name           string
scenario_name_or_object  collection

```



```
clock_or_skew_group_name collection
hierarchy_list      collection
```

**Arguments**
```
-output output_dir
```

Specifies the QoR data output directory that is configured by this command.
This output directory should be the same as the _write_qor_data -output_ directory
where QoR data of the run is stored. By default, the configurations are saved
only when _write_qor_data_ or _capture_qor_data_ runs, and they are associated
with whatever output directory is used by those commands. If this _-output_ option
is used, then the configurations are immediately written to disk in the specified
output directory.
```
-label_order list_of_labels
```

Specifies the order in which the labels/stages captured by the _write_qor_data_
command is shown in the QORsum report created by the _compare_qor_data_
command. This option uses a Tcl list of label/stage names captured by the
_write_qor_data_ command in the QoR data output directory. Typically, label
orders do not need to be specified because the order of labels captured during
the _write_qor_data_ command is preserved and used in the QORsum report.
However, if labels are captured in the wrong order, this option explicitly specifies
a preferred label order. For example, if the _write_qor_data_ command captures
QoR data in parallel executed jobs, a later label might capture data before
another label that occurred earlier in the flow.

If you do need to modify the label/stage order with this option, be aware that
this setting only modifies the order in the output directory of the QoR data.
It does not modify the QORsum report itself. So if label/stage order must be
updated, it requires that you first call _set_qor_data_options -label_order -output_
on each run's output QoR data directory that you want to modify, and then call
_compare_qor_data_ pointing to those output directories with the _-run_locations_
option to recreate the QORsum report with the updates label/stage order.
```
-run_name name
```

Specifies the name for this data run as it appears in the QoR sum report created
by the _compare_qor_data_ command. If no name is specified for the QoR data
of a given run, the name in the QoR sum report is given a generic name, such
as Run1, Run2, or Run3. Run names can also be specified when creating the
QoR sum report using the _compare_qor_data -run_names_ command. Run
names are easier to capture with the _set_qor_data_options_ command because
a meaningful run name can be automatically derived from a flow variable or the
run directory name. If the run name is specified by the _set_qor_data_options_
command and the run name from the _compare_qor_data_ command, then the
run name from the _compare_qor_data_ command takes precedence.




Run names have strict naming restrictions to support various file systems and
URL naming rules. Valid characters include numbers (0-9), lowercase letters (az), uppercase letters (A-Z), dash (-), underscore (_), period (.), and plus (+).
```
-gzip_reports true|false
```

Specifies whether the raw text reports generated by _write_qor_data_ will be
saved to disk as a normal text file or as a gzipped file. Default behavior is to not
gzip the files.
```
-dynamic_scenario scenario_name_or_object
```

Specifies the preferred scenario for detailed power information of the QoR sum
report from the power report captured by the _write_qor_data_ command. The
power report also captures high-level summary power data to the Summary
and Power panels, such as design-level leakage, dynamic, and total power.
Summary information about internal and switching power is captured from the
scenario specified by this option.

You can specify different scenarios for the _-dynamic_scenario_ and
_-leakage_scenario_ options, which computes the summary total power using the
dynamic and leakage power information from those 2 scenarios.

If the _-dynamic_scenario_ or _-leakage_scenario_ are not specified, then the
_write_qor_data_ command determines them automatically. The tool identifies all
power scenarios. If the one or more power scenarios is active for dynamic and
leakage power, then the scenario from the set that has the highest total power is
used for both dynamic and leakage scenarios. If all active power scenarios are
active only for either dynamic or leakage scenario, the highest dynamic power
scenario is used for dynamic summary reporting and the highest leakage power
scenario is used for leakage summary reporting.

If invalid or inactive scenarios are specified for the _-dynamic_scenario_ and
_-leakage_scenario_ options, a warning is issued and the tool automatically
determine these scenarios.

If the PrimePower tool is enabled for power reporting (the default behavior), then
the _-dynamic_scenario_ and _-leakage_scenario_ options are ignored. Instead, the
power scenario set that uses the _set_rtl_power_analysis_options_ is used.
```
-leakage_scenario scenario_name_or_object
```

Specifies the preferred scenario for detailed power information of the QoR sum
report from the power report captured by the _write_qor_data_ command. See the
description for the _-dynamic_scenario_ option for more details.
```
-clock_name clock_or_skew_group_name
```

Specifies the name of the clock or skew group to use as the critical clock for
summary reports, which is used to capture high-level information about a




specific critical clock in the Summary and Clock table panel in the QoR sum
report. This option also specifies the names to identify critical clocks and critical
clock scenarios for the clock QoR report generated by the _write_qor_data_
command, which captures multiple detailed tables of QoR data for all clocks in
the design.

If a critical clock or critical clock scenario is not specified, the tool automatically
determines them. The tool first considers the clock with the highest sink count
and any other clocks within a 10 percent range. The critical clock is the lowest
clock period from the other clocks within the range. If there are multiple clocks
with the same clock period, the clock with the largest latency is chosen as the
critical clock.

This option can be used with the _-clock_scenario_ option to specify which
scenario the latency and skew data is extracted from.
```
-clock_scenario scenario_name_or_object
```

Specifies the scenario used for the summary table reports for the critical clocks
in the design. See the description for the _-clock_name_ option for more details.
```
-color_hierarchies hierarchy_list
```

Specifies a Tcl list of logical hierarchy objects or names that should be colored
by the _write_qor_data -report_list gui_placement_hierarchy_ report.

By default the hierarchies to color are automatically derived based on a heuristic
that identifies significant and large hierarchies. Using this option lets you specify
the hierarchies explicitly. Additionally, this is the only way to guarantee that
the same hierarchy has the same color in every run, so they can effectively
be compared in the QOR sum report. If you use the default coloring, it does
guarantee the same hierarchy coloring for every stage/label of that run, but not
that they match across multiple runs.
```
-check_drcs_from_user_shapes true|false
```

Controls whether _write_qor_data_ calls _check_routes_ with the
_-check_from_user_shapes_ true or false value. Default is false.
```
-check_drcs_from_frozen_shapes true|false
```

Controls whether _write_qor_data_ calls _check_routes_ with the
_-check_from_frozen_shapes_ true or false value. Default is false.
```
-report_global_timing_multiple_categories true|false
```

Controls whether _write_qor_data_ calls _report_global_timing_ with the
_-enable_multiple_categories_per_endpoint_ option. Default is false.




```
-vt_and_device_group_report_mode standard|datapath
```

Controls whether _write_qor_data_ calls _report_threshold_voltage_groups_ and
_report_device_group_ with the _-standard_cells_only_ or _-datapath_cells_only_
option. The default is _standard_ which calls those reports with the
_-standard_cells_only_ option. With that setting, clock cells will be included in the
report. With the _datapath_ setting, only datapath cells will be included and clock
cells are excluded.
```
-pba_mode none|path|exhaustive|ml_exhaustive
```

Controls whether _write_qor_data_ calls timing reports with the _-pba_mode_ option,
and which value of that option is used.

In Fusion Compiler, IC Compiler II, and RTL Architect, if this option is not
specified, then _report_qor_ and _report_global_timing_ are called with _-pba_mode_
passing the value of _time.pba_optimization_mode_ app option as the value.
This app option specifies which PBA mode postroute optimization ( _route_opt_
and _hyper_route_opt_ ) uses, and the timing reports will automatically follow that
PBA mode. For example, if you've already configured postroute optimization
to run with PBA mode 'path', you do not also need to explicitly specify
_set_qor_data_options -pba_mode_ for timing reports to use 'path' mode. It will
happen automatically.

In PrimeTime, the default behavior is to call timing reports without
the _-pba_mode_ option. If this option is specified, then _report_qor_,
_report_global_timing_, and _report_constraint_ are called using the
_set_qor_data_options -pba_mode_ setting.
```
-link_source_files true|false
```

DesignDash supports linking back to _write_qor_data_ report source files and
line numbers. This feature is not supported in the QORsum report. To enable
capture of the data that allows this linking, use this option with the true value.
Default is false.

**Description**

The _set_qor_data_options_ command is used to configure the QoR data captured by the
_write_qor_data_ command. This configuration data is stored with the QoR data in the output
directory created by either _write_qor_data -output_ or _capture_qor_data -output_ for the case
of custom data capture. By default any configuration set with this command is stored in
memory until _write_qor_data_ or _capture_qor_data_ is called, and only then written to its
output directory. Use _set_qor_data_options -output_ to force the data to immediately write
to disk. Normally this is not necessary, but can be useful if you need to update the label
order of previously captured data from _write_qor_data_ .




**Examples**

The following example uses the _set_qor_data_options_ command to name a run. Since the
_-output_ option was not specified, the QoR data in the default ./qor_data output directory
from the _write_qor_data_ command is configured.
```
prompt> set_qor_data_options -run_name ccd_high_effort
```

The following example configures the data in the ./my_qor_data directory to use the clock
(CLK) for critical clock reporting in summary tables. Because the _-clock_scenario_ option is
not specified, the scenario with clocks that have the largest latency are used.
```
prompt> set_qor_data_options -output ./my_qor_data -clock_name CLK
```

The following example configures the scenarios that are used for both leakage and
dynamic power reporting in summary tables. In this case, the same scenario is used for
each.
```
prompt> set_qor_data_options -leakage_scenario func.ff1p16v125c \\
-dynamic_scenario func.ff1p16v125c

```

**See Also**

 - write_qor_data

 - compare_qor_data

 - view_qor_data

###### **set_qor_strategy**

Applies or reports optimization metrics and application settings for the current design.

**Syntax**

status _set_qor_strategy_
```
[-high_effort_timing]
[-congestion_effort medium | high | ultra]
[-report_only]
[-diff_only]
[-reduced_effort]
[-metric timing | leakage_power | total_power]
[-mode balanced | early_design | extreme_power]
[-stage pnr | synthesis (legacy usage)]
[-stage compile | compile_initial | compile_final_place | place |
place_initial | cts | post_cts_opto | route | post_route (new usage)]
[-list_versions]

```



**Arguments**
```
-metric timing | leakage_power | total_power
```

Specifies a target metric for configuring application options. The valid metrics
are:

   - _timing_

  - Intended for designs targeting for best timing.

  - Sets application options to optimize for the best timing. For the list of settings
enabled, refer to the set_qor_strategy output.

  - Regarding power optimization: With -step synthesis, -metric timing
sets compile.flow.enable_power to false. With -stage pnr, -metric timing
sets place_opt.flow.enable_power, clock_opt.flow.enable_power,
and route_opt.flow.enable_power to false. Do not manually enable
*.flow.enable_power application options after set_qor_strategy as this will
conflict with the intent. If the design is targeting for both timing and power,
use either -metric leakage_power or -metric total_power depending on the
requirement instead.

   - _leakage_power_

  - Intended for designs targeting for best timing and leakage power without
considering dynamic power.

  - Sets application options to optimize for the best timing and leakage power. For
the list of settings enabled, refer to the set_qor_strategy output.

  - Regarding power optimization: -metric leakage_power enables power
optimization, which is done by setting compile.flow.enable_powerto
true (with -stage synthesis), and setting place_opt.flow.enable_power,
clock_opt.flow.enable_power, and route_opt.flow.enable_power to true (with
-stage pnr). Do not manually disable *.flow.enable_power application options
after set_qor_strategy as this will conflict with the intent.

In addition to set_qor_strategy, for power optimization to focus on leakage,
you must also configure scenario settings accordingly in your scripts: - There
must be scenarios with leakage power analysis enabled. - There must be NO
scenarios with dynamic power analysis enabled. (use report_scenarios to report
and set_scenario_status to configure power analysis of your scenarios)

   - _total_power_

  - Intended for designs targeting for best timing and total power.

  - Sets application options to optimize for the best timing and total power. For the
list of settings enabled, refer to the set_qor_strategy output.




  - Best results are calculated if the switching activity has been simulated and
loaded with the SAIF file.

  - Regarding power optimization: -metric total_power enables power
optimization, which is done by setting compile.flow.enable_power to
true (with -stage synthesis), and setting place_opt.flow.enable_power,
clock_opt.flow.enable_power, and route_opt.flow.enable_power to true (with
-stage pnr). Do not manually disable *.flow.enable_power application options
after set_qor_strategy as this will conflict with the intent.

In addition to set_qor_strategy, for power optimization to work on total power,
you must also configure scenario settings accordingly in your scripts: - There
must be scenarios with leakage power analysis enabled and there must also be
scenarios with dynamic power analysis enabled. (use report_scenarios to report
and set_scenario_status to configure power analysis of your scenarios)
```
-mode balanced | early_design | extreme_power
```

Specifies a target mode to configure the tool flow. Valid mode names are
_balanced_, _early_design_, and _extreme_power_ . You can specify only 1 mode
name. By default, balanced mode is set. set_qor_strategy will print a message
to indicate which mode it is running. Note that there is no application option
change corresponding to the mode being used.

   - _balanced_ is the default flow mode to start with for most designs.

   - _extreme_power_ flow mode is recommended for further improvement of total
power at the cost of larger runtime. Use either -metric leakage_power or
-metric total_power with -mode extreme_power. Note that this mode does
not work with -metric timing. Command falls back to balanced mode if -metric
timing and -mode extreme_power are both specified.

   - _early_design_ flow mode is only intended for designs with early design
collaterals.
```
-high_effort_timing
```

Enables the high-effort timing flow in the compile_fusion initial_opto step. This
option only works with the set_qor_strategy synthesis stage.
```
-congestion_effort medium | high | ultra
```

Specifies the congestion flow effort level. Valid effort levels are _medium_, _high_,
and _ultra_ . You can specify only one effort level.

   - _"high"_ enables high effort congestion flow and is intended
to be only used on highly congested designs. With _"-stage_
_synthesis"_, compile.place.congestion_effort is set to ultra,
compile.optimization.congestion_effort is set to high, and
place_opt.place.congestion_effort is set to ultra. In addition,




_create_placement_ and _create_buffer_trees_ are enabled before
the compile_fusion initial_placement stage. With _"-stage pnr"_,
place_opt.place.congestion_effort is set to ultra.

   - _"medium"_ runs the medium effort congestion flow. With _"-stage_
_synthesis"_, compile.place.congestion_effort is set to medium,
compile.optimization.congestion_effort is set to medium, and
place_opt.place.congestion_effort is set to medium. No addtional commands
are enabled before the compile_fusion initial_placement stage. With _"-stage_
_pnr"_, place_opt.place.congestion_effort is set to medium. (Note that when
-congestion_effort is not used at all, with _"-stage pnr"_, set_qor_strategy by
default sets place_opt.place.congestion_effort to high.)

   - _"ultra"_ currently behaves the same as _high_ but is subject to change in a
future release. If you have been running with _ultra_, please switch to _high_
instead.
```
-report_only
```

Writes out the application options to the console in tabular format.
```
-diff_only
```

Writes out the application options to the console in tabular format for application
options that are not set to their target settings.
```
-reduced_effort
```

Calculates the specified metric target from the _-metric_ option with reduced effort
performance. This option trades performance for runtime in designs that are
easier to close with faster runtime by lowering tool engine efforts. This command
option only works when mode is set to balanced.
```
-stage pnr | synthesis (legacy usage)
```

Specifies the stage name. You can only specify one stage name at a time. Valid
stage names are _synthesis_ and _pnr_ .
```
-stage compile | compile_initial | compile_final_place | place |
place_initial | cts | post_cts_opto | route | post_route (new usage)
```

Specifies the stage name. You can only specify one stage name at a time.
Valid stage names are _compile_, _compile_initial_, _compile_final_place_, _place_,
_place_initial_, _cts_, _post_cts_opto_, _route_, and _post_route_ . This is the new
usage. The legacy set_stage command should not be used when you run
set_qor_strategy with this new usage. Recommended usage:

   - set_qor_strategy -stage compile_initial

  - To be used before compile_fusion initial_map (for compile_fusion-based flow)




  - Replaces legacy usage 'set_qor_strategy -stage synthesis + set_stage -step
synthesis'

   - set_qor_strategy -stage compile_final_place

  - To be used before compile_fusion final_place (for compile_fusion-based flow)

  - Replaces legacy usage 'set_stage -step compile_place'

   - set_qor_strategy -stage place_initial

  - To be used before place_opt (for place_opt-based flow)

  - Replaces legacy usage 'set_qor_strategy -stage pnr + set_stage -step
placement'

   - set_qor_strategy -stage cts

  - To be used before clock_opt build_clock

  - Replaces legacy usage 'set_qor_strategy -stage pnr + set_stage -step cts'

   - set_qor_strategy -stage post_cts_opto

  - To be used before clock_opt final_opto

  - Replaces legacy usage 'set_stage -step post_cts_opto'

   - set_qor_strategy -stage route

  - To be used before route_auto

  - Replaces legacy usage 'set_stage -step route'

   - set_qor_strategy -stage post_route

  - To be used before hyper_route_opt/route_opt

  - Replaces legacy usage 'set_stage -step post_route'

   - set_qor_strategy -stage compile and -stage place

  - -stage compile is equivalent of the legacy -stage synthesis, and -stage place is
equivalent of the legacy -stage pnr.

  - -stage synthesis and -stage pnr are being retained for backward copatability
but will be remvoved in a future release.
```
-list_versions
```

List the versions supported. When this is specified, all other options are ignored.




**Description**

This command applies metric-specific and mode-specific settings to the current design
and sets the application options for the synthesis, placement, and routing engines for
better timing, leakage power, and total power metrics performance.

The _-congestion_effort_ high option applies application options for highly congested
designs. For _-stage synthesis_, _-stage compile_, or _-stage compile_initial_, it also enables
_create_placement_ and _create_buffer_trees_ before the compile_fusion initial_place stage.
If the compile_fusion command is run in multiple sessions, for example, _compile_fusion_
_initial_place_ in one session followed by _compile_fusion initial_drc_ in a new session,
etc, _set_qor_strategy -congestion_effort high_ must be reapplied again before the
compile_fusion command in a new session.

By default, the command applies the application option settings to the design based on
the _-metric_, _-mode_ and _-stage_ options and sets the target metric attribute on the block to
the specified metric. This command uses the _set_technology_ command to apply the best
settings for the node. It is recommended to run the _set_technology_ command first.

Metric and mode restrictions: The _-metric_ and _-mode_ options can't be modified when used
along with _-stage synthesis_, _compile_, or _compile_initial_ after _compile_fusion initial_place_ is
done. Also they can't be modified when used along with _-stage pnr_, _place_, or _place_initial_,
after _place_opt initial_place_ is done. The _-metric_ and _-mode_ options can be modified
when used along with _-stage pnr_, _place_, or _place_initial_ after _compile_fusion_ is done. They
can't be modified when used along with _-stage pnr_, _place_, or _place_initial_ after _clock_opt_
_build_clock_ is done.

If the _-mode_ and _-metric_ command options are not specified, then the command uses
the previously set value for metric_target and mode_target from the current block. If
the attributes have not been set then the timing metric and balanced mode are used by
default.

If _-mode_ is set to _early_design_, some post-route features and the their standalone
commands would be disabled to reduce runtime on early designs.

Use the _-report_only_ option to preview the application option settings before applying
them to the design. The _-report_only_ option writes out the application option settings to the
console.

The -diff_only option is applicable only to -stage _synthesis_, _compile_, _pnr_, and _place_ .

The command can also read the RM Tcl variables to enable special features. If these
variables are defined and set to the correct values then it enables the application options




for those features. These are set in the RM setup scripts to configure the RM flow. The
following variables are supported :

ENABLE_PERFORMANCE_VIA_LADDER

For stage compile_initial or place_initial, if this is true
and the design is 7 nm or smaller, it sets the application
options _route.auto_via_ladder.update_during_route_,
_place.legalize.enable_via_ladder_checks_, and _vl.flow.enable_convergence_flow_
to true. It also runs the _setup_performance_via_ladder -effort high_ command
and source a file output from the command. For stage post_cts_opto, if
this is true and the design is 7 nm or smaller, it sets the application option
_opt.common.enable_via_ladder_insertion_ to true.

ENABLE_MULTIBIT

For -stage compile_initial or place_initial, if this is true then the application
options for multibit register banking are enabled. For -stage compile_initial,
it sets the _compile.flow.enable_multibit_, _place_opt.flow.enable_multibit_, and
_place_opt.enable_multibit_debanking_ to true. For -stage place_initial, it only sets
the _place_opt_ application options.

ENABLE_DPS

For -stage compile_initial or place_initial, if this is set to true the
_opt.common.power_integrity_ application option is set to true and the
_ccd.dps.flow_reporting_ application option is set to {*}. This feature also requires
a Digital-AF license and checks for its availability before enabling the application
options.

ENABLE_SPG

For -stage place_initial, if this is set to true, the _place_opt.flow.do_spg_
application option is set to true for the _place_opt_ flow.

CTS_STYLE

For -stage place_initial,, if this is set to MSCTS then it sets the application option
_place_opt.flow.enable_multisource_clock_trees_ to true. It also checks if the
variable TCL_REGULAR_MSCTS_FILE is defined and is pointing to a valid file
path. This is sourced during place_opt.tcl.

ENABLE_HIGH_UTILIZATION_FLOW

For -stage place_initial, in place_opt.tcl a special feature flow is enabled and this
turns the _time.delay_calc_waveform_analysis_mode_ to disabled.

ENABLE_IRDP

For -stage post_cts_opto, if this is set to true then _clock_opt.flow.skip_placement_
is set to false to ensure placement is not skipped. This feature also requires a




Digital-AF license and checks for its availability before enabling the application
options. This feature also checks if the TCL_IRDP_CONFIG_FILE variable is
defined and is pointing to a valid file path.

ENABLE_CREATE_SHIELDS

For -stage post_cts_opto, if this is set to true then
_route.common.reshield_modified_nets_ is set to reshield. For -stage post_route,
if this is set to true then _set_extraction_options -virtual_shield_extraction false_ is
set.

**Version support**

When _flow.set_qor_strategy.version_ is set to a suppported version (other than the default
version), _set_qor_strategy_ enables additional PPA features per the specified version
and prints out the message "Strategy-Info: set_qor_strategy version <version> applied
successfully." accordingly.

- To specify a version, set the application option _flow.set_qor_strategy.version_ before
_set_qor_strategy_

- To show the list of supported versions, use _set_qor_strategy -list_versions_

- To preview the list of addtional PPA features to be enabled for a given version, use
_set_qor_strategy -report_only_

**Examples**

The following example writes the application option settings to the console for the _timing_
metric and the _place_initial_ stage without changing the application option settings.
```
prompt> set_qor_strategy -metric timing -stage place_initial -mode
balanced -report_only
Strategy-Info: Evaluating single metric strategy for timing metric_target
Strategy-Info: technology_node is undefined for the current block.
Strategy-Info: Auto-detected closest technology node established.
Strategy-Info: Reporting set_qor_strategy settings for technology node
established.
Strategy-Info: Metric(s) : timing
+----------------------------------------------------+---------------+-----------+------------+------------+
|      Option Name               | Metric Group |
Tool   | Current  | Target  |
|                          |        |
Default  | Setting  | Setting  |
+----------------------------------------------------+---------------+-----------+------------+------------+
| time.enable_clock_to_data_analysis         | *All metrics* |
false   | true    | true    |

```



```
| route.global.timing_driven             | *All metrics* |
false   | false   | true    |
(Only partial table is shown)
```

The following example applies the application option settings for the _total_power_ target
metric for the _cts_ stage.
```
prompt> set_qor_strategy -stage cts -metric total_power
prompt> clock_opt
```

The following example sets and enables the _set_qor_strategy_ version.
```
prompt> set_app_options -name flow.set_qor_strategy.version -value
SQS-20240701
prompt> set_qor_strategy -stage cts
prompt> clock_opt

```

###### **set_query_rules**

Defines query rules.

**Syntax**
```
status set_query_rules
[-hierarchical_separators separators ]
[-bus_name_notations bus_notations ]
[-class class_list ]
[-regsub regsub ]
[-wildcard]
[-suffix suffix_list ]
[-nocase]
[-verbose]
[-show]
[-reset]
```

**Data Types**
```
separators      list
bus_notations     list
class_list      list
regsub        list
suffix_list      list

```



**Arguments**
```
-hierarchical_separators separators
```

Specifies a list of equivalent hierarchy separators in object names. There must
be at least two elements in the list. The default list is {/ _ .}. The elements are
preferably all single characters, although at most one multi-character element
is allowed. No more than one alphabetical character a-z or A-Z is allowed as a
hierarchical separator. The alphabetical character is also mutually exclusive with
the multi-character element. The following special characters are not supported
as hierarchy separators nor are they allowed as one of the characters for the
multi-character hierarchy separator: 0-9, '*', '?', '\\\\', '+', '^', '[', ']'.
```
-bus_name_notations bus_notations
```

Specifies a list of equivalent bus name notations in object names. There must
be at least two elements in the list, and the list element must be two characters.
The first character of the element is the opening bus name character, and the
second character is the closing bus name character. The default list is {[] __ ()}.
No more than one matching pair of alphabetical characters a-z or A-Z is allowed
as bus name notations. The following characters are not supported as opening
or closing bus name characters: 0-9, '*', '?', '\\\\', '+', '^', and '/'. Bracketed bus
notations must be paired. For example, "[)" are not properly paired brackets,
so they are not supported. For nonbracket bus name notations, the opening
and closing bus name character must be the same. For example, "-_" is not a
supported bus name notation.
```
-class class_list
```

Specifies a list of object class names for which the query rules are applied.
The following object classes are supported: _cell_, _port_, _pin_, _net_, _power_domain_,
_supply_net_, _supply_set_, _supply_port_, and _power_switch_ . You can specify a
subset of the above object classes. By default, the command applies the query
rules to all supported classes.
```
-regsub regsub
```

Specifies a list of options for the _regsub_ Tcl command. Each list should include
three string elements {{switches} {match_regexp} {substitution_exp}}. The
_-regsub_ option can be specified multiple times in one _set_query_rules_ command.

In addition to the Tcl built-in switches, the { _-class cell | pin | net | port_ } and
_-cumulative_ switches are supported to enable object class-specific regsub rules.
When multiple _-regsub_ options are used with any _-cumulative_ switch for an
object class, the regsub rules for that object class will have a cumulative effect
in the sense that the subsequent regsub rule is applied to the output of the
previous regsub rule. Without the _-cumulative_ switch, the regsub rules for the
object class are applied independently.




This option is applicable to pin, port, net or leaf level cells. In case the option
is given for cell, it could also be applied to the cell of a pin. If _-regsub_ is used
without other query rules, the default values for the other options are still used.
In order to save runtime, use this option only if the existing rule-based matching
scheme fails to match an object.
```
-wildcard
```

Enables wildcard support.
```
-suffix suffix_list
```

Predefined suffix rules {_reg _tri} could be enabled with this option to match
register or tri-state cells. This rule is not applicable to other type of cells.
```
-nocase
```

Enables case-insensitive rule-based matching.
```
-verbose
```

Enables verbose messages.
```
-show
```

Shows the current definition of the query options. When _-show_ is used alone,the
existing query rules are not cleared in the current design. If used with other
options, the new query options will be set first and then displayed.
```
-reset
```

Resets query rules to the program default.

**Description**

The _set_query_rules_ command allows you to define query rules. The purpose of the
rule-based matching is to resolve naming differences, such as differences in hierarchical
separators and bus naming notations.

This command clears all query rules in the current design, and then sets the new query
rules in the current design. The new rule settings will replace the previous settings.

**Examples**
```
# Show program default.
prompt> set_query_rules -show
*************************
Query Rules
*************************
Rule Type  Rule Value
-------------------  -------------------Hierarchy Separator  {/ _ .}

```



```
Bus Notation  {[] __ ()}
Object Class  {cell port pin net power_domain power_switch
supply_net supply_set supply_port}
Nocase  false
Wildcard  false
Verbose  false
1
# Non-default
prompt> set_query_rules \\
  -hierarchical_separators {/ _} \\
  -bus_name_notations {[] ||} \\
  -class {cell port} -show
*************************
Query Rules
*************************
Rule Type  Rule Value
-------------------  -------------------Hierarchy Separator  {/ _}
Bus Notation  {[] ||}
Object Class  {cell port}
Nocase  false
Wildcard  false
Verbose  false
1
# Use alphabetical characters
prompt> set_query_rules \\
  -hierarchical_separators {/ x} \\
  -class {cell port} \\
  -bus_name_notations {[] __ || xx} -show
*************************
Query Rules
*************************
Rule Type  Rule Value
-------------------  -------------------Hierarchy Separator  {/ x}
Bus Notation  {[] __ || xx}
Object Class  {cell port}
Nocase  false
Wildcard  false
Verbose  false
1

# Setting regsub rules
prompt> set_query_rules -show \\
  -class {port cell pin net} \\

```



```
  -regsub {{-class cell} {(.*)\\[(\\d+)\\]} {\\1_\\2} } \\
  -regsub {{-class net} {RED} {3}}
*************************
Query Rules
*************************
Rule Type  Rule Value
-------------------  -------------------Hierarchy Separator  {/ _ .}
Bus Notation  {[] __ ()}
Object Class  {cell port pin net}
regsub  {{-class cell} {(.*)\\[(\\d+)\\]} {\\1_\\2}}
regsub  {{-class net} {RED} {3}}
Nocase  false
Wildcard  false
Verbose  false
1

```

###### **set_rail_command_options**

Add or replace rail command options to pass to RedHawk-SC / RedHawk.

**Syntax**

collection _set_rail_command_options_
```
-command RedHawk-SC / RedHawk_command |
{-script_file file -order before_the_command | after_the_command} |
-default
[-option RedHawk-SC_command_option ]
[-value RedHawk-SC / RedHawk_command_option_value ]
[-pre_script_file RedHawk-SC / RedHawk_pre_script_file ]
[-post_script_file RedHawk-SC / RedHawk_post_script_file ]
[-die Die_instance_name ]

```



**Data Types**
```
RedHawk-SC / RedHawk_command        string
RedHawk-SC_command_option         string
RedHawk-SC / RedHawk_command_option_value string
file                    string
tag                    string
rail_scenario               string
Die_instance_name             string
```

**Arguments**
```
-die Die_instance_name
```

Specifies the die instance name whose run script would be modified by this
command (Only required in 3dic design).
```
-command RedHawk-SC / RedHawk_command
```

Specifies the RedHawk-SC / RedHawk command whose options are to be
added or replaced in the run script.
```
-option RedHawk-SC_command_option
```

Specifies the RedHawk-SC command option to be replaced in the run script for
the command specified in the option _-command_ .
```
-value RedHawk-SC / RedHawk_command_option_value
```

Specifies the RedHawk-SC / RedHawk command option value to be added or
replaced for the command specified in the option _-command_ and the option
specified in the option _-option_ .
```
-script_file file
```

Specifies the script file to source before or after the specified command.

Requires -order.
```
-order before_the_command | after_the_command
```

Specifies the order in relation to the specified command to source the specified
script file.

If the value is before_the_command, then the script file is sourced before the
call to the specified command.

If the value is after_the_command, then the script file is sourced after the call to
the specified command.
```
-pre_script_file file
```

Specifies the script file to source at the beginning of the run script.




```
-post_script_file file
```

Specifies the script file to source at the end of the run script.
```
-tag tag
```

Specify a tag to the rail command option.
```
-rail_scenario rail_scenario
```

Specify a Rail Scenario.
```
-default
```

Resets all rail command options.

This option does not require an argument.

**Description**

The _set_rail_command_options_ command adds or replaces rail command options to pass
to RedHawk-SC / RedHawk.

For the same command but different command options, the behavior is to add. For the
same command and the same command option, the behavior is to replace. For the same
command but no command options, the behavior is to replace.

Not all command options can be added or replaced. Only the command options listed
below are supported.

Use _report_rail_command_options_ to print the currently configured rail command options
to screen.

Requires one of the following command options: -command, -script_file, or -default.

Usage #1: SYNTAX: set_rail_command_options -pre_script_file _PRE_SCRIPT_
-post_script_file _POST_SCRIPT_

Code-gen: Generates include(' _PRE_SCRIPT_ ') at beginning of analyze_rail.py Generates
include(' _POST_SCRIPT_ ') at end of analyze_rail.py

3D-SYNTAX: set_rail_command_options -die _DIE_ -pre_script_file _PRE_SCRIPT_
-post_script_file _POST_SCRIPT_

Code-gen: Generates include(' _PRE_SCRIPT_ ') at beginning of _DIE_ parts in analyze_rail.py
Generates include(' _POST_SCRIPT_ ') at end of _DIE_ parts in analyze_rail.py

Usage #2: SYNTAX: set_rail_command_options -command _COMMAND_ -script_file
_SCRIPT_FILE_ -order {before_the_command | after_the_command}

Code-gen: If use before_the_command, generates include(' _SCRIPT_FILE_ ')
before _COMMAND_ in analyze_rail.py If use after_the_command, generates
include(' _SCRIPT_FILE_ ') after _COMMAND_ in analyze_rail.py




3D-SYNTAX: set_rail_command_options -die _DIE_ -command _COMMAND_ -script_file
_SCRIPT_FILE_ -order {before_the_command | after_the_command}

Code-gen: If use before_the_command, generates include(' _SCRIPT_FILE_ ') before
_COMMAND_ at the _DIE_ parts in analyze_rail.py If use after_the_command, generates
include(' _SCRIPT_FILE_ ') after _COMMAND_ at the _DIE_ parts in analyze_rail.py

Usage #3: SYNTAX: set_rail_command_options -command _COMMAND_ -option _OPTION_
-value _VALUE_

Code-gen: Overrides the original value with _VALUE_ for the _COMMAND OPTION_ pair in
analyze_rail.py. Appends _VALUE_ to the original value if _OPTION_ is empty.

3D-SYNTAX: set_rail_command_options -die _DIE_ -command _COMMAND_ -option _OPTION_
-value _VALUE_

Code-gen: Overrides the original value with _VALUE_ for the _COMMAND OPTION_ pair at
the _DIE_ parts in analyze_rail.py. Appends _VALUE_ to the original value if _OPTION_ is empty.

###### **set_rail_probes**

Creates a virtual region that draws power during rail analysis.

**Syntax**

status _set_rail_probes_




```
-die die_name
[-region x1 y1 x2 y2 ]
-cell cell_ref_name | -side upper | lower
-net die_net_full_name
-layer die_layer_name
-current current_in_amps
-max_array_size {cols rows}
```

**Data Types**
```
die_name      string
x1 y1 x2 y2    bbox
cell_ref_name   string
upper       string
lower       string
die_net_full_name string
die_layer_name   string
current_in_amps  float
cols        int
rows        int
```

**Arguments**
```
-die
```

Specifies probes by die.

This option is required when app-option rail.enable_3dic is set to true.
```
-region
```

Specifies region filter for creating probes. Optional; Default full block; Coordinate
system is global.
```
-cell
```

Specifies probes by cell master. -cell and -side are mutually exclusive.
```
-side
```

Specifies the side of TSV cells or vias to create probes on. Directionality is
based on mask order.
```
-net
```

Specifies die-local net fullname filter for creating probes. The parent cell of this
net must match the die name specified by -die.
```
-layer
```

Specifies die-local layer name filter for creating probes. If -cell is specified, this
layer must be a metal layer. If -side is specified, This layer must be the TSV
layer or a via layer.




```
-current
```

Specifies probes current. Unit is in Amps. Value must be negative for power net
probes and positive for ground net probes.
```
-max_array_size
```

Specifies maximum via array size in terms of rows and columns for creating
probes. Optional; Default {1 1}; Values for rows and columns must be greater
than one.

**Description**

set_rail_probes creates current sink probes on specified objects within a region. Current is
divided by the number of probes created per invocation.

If -cell is specified, probes are created at the center of the overlap region between pin
shapes of cells of the specified cell master with shapes on the specified layer (excluding
via metal enclosure shapes), of the specified net, within the specified region. Otherwise,
-side is required for below cases:

If -layer specifies the TSV layer, probes are created at the center of the overlap region
between pin shapes on the specified side of TSV cells, cells with pin shapes on layers
above and below the TSV layer, with shapes of the specified net, within the specified
region.

If -layer specifies a via layer, probes are created at the center of the metal enclosure on
the specified side of vias on the specified via layer, of the specified net, within the specified
region.

In the case of via arrays, the same number of probes up to the number specified by
-max_array_size are created as there are via cuts, and evenly distributed about the
overlap region of upper and lower metal enclosures.

NOTE: If -cell is specified, only lateral connections within the same layer as pin shapes of
cells of the specified cell master are considered for overlap regions as probes placement
candidates. This means via metal enclosure shapes aren't considered. If vertical
connections through adjacent via layers are needed, please use -side.

**EXAMPLE**

The following example creates probes at the center of the overlap region between pin
shapes of cells of cell master uBUMP with shapes on layer MB, of net MEM/VDD1, and
within the region {{5330 499} {5334 503}}.
```
prompt> set_rail_probes -die MEM -region {{5330 499} {5334 503}} -cell
uBUMP -net MEM/VDD1 -layer MB -current -100

```



The following example creates probes at the center of the lower metal enclosure of vias on
the via layer VIA1, of net MEM/VDD1, within the region {{5277.0800 454.5700} {5286.9200
547.4300}}.
```
prompt> set_rail_probes -die MEM -region {{5277.0800 454.5700} {5286.9200
547.4300}} -side lower -net MEM/VDD1 -layer VIA1 -current -100
-max_array_size {4 4}
```

The following example creates probes at the center of the overlap region between pin
shapes on the lower side of TSV cells, cells with pin shapes on layers above and below
the TSV layer, with shapes of net MEM/VDD1, within the region {{4850 499} {4854 503}}.
```
prompt> set_rail_probes -die MEM -region {{4850 499} {4854 503}} -side
lower -net MEM/VDD1 -layer TSV -current -100

```

**See Also**

 - analyze_rail

 - set_rail_probes
