###### **write_taps**

Writes existing taps into a text file for later reuse.

**Syntax**

status _write_taps_
```
-file file_name
[ taps ]
```

**Data Types**
```
string file_name
list taps
```

**Arguments**
```
-file file_name
```

Specifies the name of the file to which the tap points are written.
```
taps
```

Specifies the tap points to be written. The tap points can be specified as name
patterns or collections of taps.




**Description**

The command writes a file containing the location and associated supply net for each
inserted tap, which can be read into a later session with the _create_taps -import file_
command.

The tap points written to the file can be limited to specific types by using the filter option
with the _get_taps_ command. For example, you can capture the set of tap points that were
inserted in _top_pg_ type.

The following is the format of the output file:

_supply_net_name layer_number X_coordinate Y_coordinate [R(R_value)] [L(L_value)]_

_[C(C_value)]_

Lumped RLC values will be written to the tap file if they are specified for the taps. The
units are Ohm for resistance, Henry for inductance, and Farad for capacitance. In the
following example, no lumped RLC value is written to the tap file:
```
VDDY 39 746.800 469.400
VDDY 39 0.200 469.400
VDDY 39 0.200 548.600
VDDY 39 0.200 627.800
VSS 39 746.800 51.800
VSS 39 0.200 51.800
VSS 39 746.800 131.000
VSS 39 746.800 210.200
VSS 39 746.800 368.600
```

In the following example, the lumped RLC value is written to the tap file:
```
VDDY 39 746.800 469.400 R(0.001) L(1.0e-9) C(2.0e-12)
VDDY 39 0.200 469.400
VDDY 39 0.200 548.600
VDDY 39 0.200 627.800
VSS 39 746.800 51.800
VSS 39 0.200 51.800
VSS 39 746.800 131.000
VSS 39 746.800 210.200
VSS 39 746.800 368.600
```

**Multicorner-Multimode Support**

This command has no dependency on scenario-specific, mode-specific, or corner-specific
information.

**Examples**

The following example writes a file containing the taps that were inserted via the lib_cell
reference.
```
prompt> write_taps [get_taps -filter type {libcell_pg}] -file ./MyTapFile

```



**See Also**

 - create_taps

 - remove_taps

 - report_taps

 - get_taps

###### **write_test_protocol**

Writes a STIL test protocol file.

**Syntax**
```
status write_test_protocol
[-output file_name ]
[-test_mode mode_name ]
[-pattern_exec pattern_exec_name ]
[-program program_name ]
[-single_si enable | disable]
[-instruction list_of_instructions ]
[-register list_of_registers ]
[-target pdl ip_instance ]
[-filter_pll_structures list_of_occ ]

```



**Data Types**
```
file_name      string
mode_name      string
pattern_exec_name  string
```

**Arguments**
```
-output file_name
```

Specifies the file to which the protocol is written.
```
-test_mode mode_name
```

Specifies the test mode in which the protocol is extracted.
```
-pattern_exec fIpattern_exec_name
```

Specifies the macro definitions and clock structures of the test mode explicitly.
```
-program program_name
```

Applies the defined SPF constraints to the specified test mode. After you run
the _write_test_protocol_ command with this option, you will see a message that
indicates whether you have defined the SPF constraints or not.
```
-single_si enable | disable
```

Specifies the single SI/SO protocol configuration. The default is _disable_ .
```
-instruction list_of_instructions
```

```

```

Specifies the list of registers for the test protocol.
```

```

```
-filter_pll_structures list_of_occ
```

Specifies the list of OCC names that must be filtered out.

**Description**

The _write_test_protocol_ command outputs the Standard Test Interface Language (STIL)
test protocol from the memory to the disk in text format. This allows you to customize the
test protocol. The scan test protocol defines the sequence in which the design is tested
using the scan-in, parallel, and scan-out vectors. The protocol defined for a design is used
to drive the scan test and design rule checking.

_Note_ : The _-test_mode_ and _-patternexec_ options are mutually exclusive.

###### **write_topology_constraints**

Generate Tcl statements to add and/or reset multicycle constraints for topology plan
objects

**Syntax**

int _write_topology_constraints_
```
[-filename filename ]
[-include_reset]
[-only_reset]
[-overwrite]
[-use_object_lookup]
[topology plans]

```

**Data Types**
```
filename        string
topology plans     collection of topology plans
```

**Arguments**
```
-filename filename
```

Specifies the name for the Tcl output filename to write the multicycle constraints.
Use stdout as the filename to write to the console instead.
```
-include_reset
```

Include _reset_paths_ statements in the output to undo / remove the multicycle
path constraints set by this command.
```
-only_reset
```

Only include the _reset_paths_ statements - do not include any multicycle path
statements. This option implies _-include_reset_ .
```
-overwrite
```

Overwrite any files that may already exist with the given filename.




```
-use_object_lookup
```

When specified, include Tcl calls to _get_pins_ or _get_ports_ (as appropriate) when
passing objects to the _set_multicycle_path_ or _reset_paths_ commands. The
default is just to pass the object name and let the command determine the
object(s) being referenced.
```
topology plans
```

Specifies a collection (or list of names) of topology plans to be included in the
report. The default is all topology plans belonging to the current block.

**Description**

This command creates Tcl statements of the form: set_multicycle_path -setup <count>
-from <object> [-through <object>] -to <object>. and set_multicycle_path -hold <count-1>
-from <object> [-through <object>] -to <object>.

for any stages of a given topology crossing through any virtual sequential repeaters
(registers) that do not have any netlist implementation or do not have associated netlist
objects. Timing paths default to values of "-setup 1" and "-hold 0", which is equivalent to
crossing through zero virtual registers, and therefore, if all sequential topology repeaters
of a given topology plan have associated std cell objects, then no statements will be
generated for that topology plan. That is, statements of the form "-setup 1" and "-hold 0"
will not be skipped since they are assumed by default.

The generated statements can then by used to apply suitable multicycle path constraints
to the nets / objects of a topology plan when used with _report_timing_ .

The reset options generate statements of a similar form, but using "reset_paths" instead of
"set_multicycle_path" as the command.

Note: if the first/last object of an applicable multicycle path is a sequential element
(register), then the first/last part of the path statement will be -from <clkObject> / -to
<clkObject>. However, if the object is a port or block pin (non-sequential object), the first/
last parts of the path statement will use "-through" instead of "-from" and "-to".

**Examples**

The following example writes constraints to the file named topo:
```
prompt> write_topology_constraints -filename topo
```

The following example writes constraints for the specified topology plan TP to the file
named topo:
```
prompt> write_topology_constraints TP -filename topo

```



**See Also**

 - report_timing

 - report_topology_plans

###### **write_topology_plans**

Writes topology plan information in Tcl format for the current design.

**Syntax**

int _write_topology_plans_
```
[-log]
[-include_objects]
[-pins_locations]
[-current_block]
[-backward_compatibility]
[ topology_plan_list ]
[-filename file name ]
```

**Data Types**
```
topology_plan_list  collection
filename       string
```

**Arguments**
```
-log
```

Writes out topology plan information to the console and log file.
```
-include_objects
```

Includes Tcl commands to create bundles and supernets in the output.
```
-pins_locations
```

Write out pins locations, not actual pins names if topology node has pins objects
```
-current_block
```

Only writes out topology plans for current block.
```
-backward_compatibility
```

Exclude newest objects/attributes (do not exist in old versions).
```
-filename file name
```

Specifies the file name for the topology plans output file.




```
topology_plan_list
```

Specifies a list of topology plans to write out. The list can contain topology
plan names, patterns, or collections. A collection can be specified by using the
_get_topology_plans_ command.

**Description**

The _write_topology_plans_ command generates a script that contains the Tcl commands to
re-create the topology plans in the design. The script includes the topology plan name and
topology edges and topology nodes. If _topology_plan_list_ is specified, the command writes
only the specified topology plans. If _topology_plan_list_ is not specified, the command
writes out all topology plans in the design. Topology plans with invalid topology nodes
( _is_valid_ attribute) will be skipped from output.

**Examples**

The following example writes out information for the topology plan named "topo_5".
```
prompt> write_topology_plans topo_5 -include_objects -log
# icc2 Q-2019.12 Oct 1, 2019
# design: GPU_TOP_DG
# Fri Oct 18 13:37:16 2019
set _curr_ [current_block]
### NER (per block)
current_block GPU_TOP_DG
remove_net_estimation_rules -reset default -quiet
remove_net_estimation_rules -reset rule1 -quiet
set_net_estimation_rule rule1 -parameter "layer" -horizontal_value "M4"
-vertical_value "M5"
### plan name: topo_5
current_block GPU_TOP_DG
if {[sizeof_collection [get_topology_plan topo_5 -quiet]] != 0}
{ remove_topology_plan topo_5 }
create_bundle -name bundle_B2A_08
[get_nets { TOP_MVECO_n8539 TOP_MVECO_n8540 TOP_MVECO_n8541
TOP_MVECO_n8542 TOP_MVECO_n8543 TOP_MVECO_n8544 TOP_MVECO_n8545
TOP_MVECO_n8546 }]
set _objLst_ [get_bundles { bundle_B2A_08 }]
create_topology_plan -name topo_5 -objects $_objLst_ -net_estimation_rule
rule1 -allow_feedthrough select_on -allow_feedthrough_select [get_cells
{ F E E/sub_E }]
create_topology_node -plan topo_5 -name node1 -objects [get_cells { A }]

```



```
-constraint_type side -side W -start 190.000 -end 200.000
create_topology_node -plan topo_5 -name node3 -objects [get_cells { E }]
-constraint_type edge -edge {4}
create_topology_node -plan topo_5 -name node4 -objects [get_cells { E }]
-constraint_type edge -edge {2}
create_topology_node -plan topo_5 -name node2 -objects [get_cells { B }]
-constraint_type edge -edge {4} -start 120.000 -range 10.000
create_topology_edge -plan topo_5 -name edge1 -nodes {topo_5/node2
topo_5/node3}
create_topology_edge -plan topo_5 -name edge1_1 -nodes {topo_5/node3
topo_5/node4}
create_topology_edge -plan topo_5 -name edge1_2 -nodes {topo_5/node4
topo_5/node1}
current_block $_curr_
1

```

**See Also**

###### **write_verilog**

Writes a Verilog description of the current design. Please note that it is enabled on nonanalysis type designs (cannot be run on "analysis" type designs, i.e. with rtl_opt).

**Syntax**

string _write_verilog_
```
[-compress method ]
[-top_module_first]
[-hierarchy scope ]
[-module_top module ]
[-shadow_netlist_only]
[-split_bus]
[-include include_list ]
[-exclude exclude_list ]
[-force_reference blocks_and_lib_cells ]
[-force_no_reference blocks_and_lib_cells ]
[-switch_view_list views ]
[-only_master_variant]
[-shell_only]
[-module_list]
[-exclude_modules modules_to_exclude_list ]
[-mask_shifted_suffix_without_constraint suffix_string ]
[-rename_cell cell_renaming_files ]
[-exclude_cells cells_to_exclude_list ]
[-encrypt]
[-key_file toolkeys ]
verilog_file_name

```

**Data Types**
```
method          string
scope          string
module          string or collection
include_list       list
exclude_list       list
blocks_and_lib_cells   list
views          list
suffix_string      string
cell_renaming_files   list
cells_to_exclude_list  list
toolkeys         string
verilog_file_name    string

```



**Arguments**
```
-compress method
```

Specifies file compression format. Formats currently supported are _zstd_ and
_gzip_ . A .zst or .gz extension is appended to the file name if no extension is
specified. By default, the command does not compress the Verilog file.
```
-top_module_first
```

Writes the modules hierarchically in a top-down approach, so that the top
module appears first in the output file. By default, modules are written
hierarchically in the bottom-up approach, with the top module appearing last in
the file.
```
-hierarchy scope
```

Writes only the modules in the specified scope. The default _scope_ value is
_design_ . Following are the valid settings for the _scope_ :
```
  top     Writes only the top module in the design.
  design   Writes the design, stopping at its design boundary.
  design_lib Writes the design, stopping at its design library
  boundary.
  all     Writes the design, including modules in the reference
  libraries.
-module_top module
```

When a module is specified by this option, it will be written out along with it’s
hierarchies (sub modules contained within this module) in the verilog file. Note
that this option will not set the specified module as the top module of the current
design. It will only write out the specified module as the top module in the output
file (i.e. it will either be a first module or last module of the file depending on the
option -top_module_first). This option will work only if current_design is linked.
```
-shadow_netlist_only
```

Writes only the shadow objects and the objects in the path to the shadow
objects. Shadow objects are nets, cells, and pins of reference ports which have
a shadow_status attribute value other than normal (i.e., their is_shadow attribute
value is true). If a cell is a shadow object, all of the cell's pins are also shadow
objects. If a module definition is output (because there is a shadow object
referencing the module and the module is within the scope of the -hierarchy
option), the module's full port interface is output.
```
-split_bus
```

Writes bus ports and nets as individual bits. The bus port and net names are
treated as scalar names and escaped.




For example, if you have the following module definition:
```
  module top (out, in);
  output [3:0] out;
  input in;
  wire [3:0] n;
  ...
  endmodule
```

It is written as follows:
```
  module top(\\out[3], \\out[2], \\out[1], \\out[0], in);
  output \\out[3] ;
  output \\out[2] ;
  output \\out[1] ;
  output \\out[0] ;
  input in;
  wire \0 ;
  wire \0 ;
  wire \0 ;
  wire \0 ;
  ...
  endmodule
-include include_list
```

Specifies a list constructs and objects to include in the output. When this option
is specified, the Verilog file contains the basic logic netlist and only the types of
constructs and objects specified with this option. The valid values are,
```
  all
  all_physical_cells
  analog_pg
  corner_cells
  cover_cells
  diode_cells
  empty_modules
  end_cap_cells
  feedthrough_cells
  filler_cells
  flip_chip_driver_cells
  flip_chip_pad_cells
  ftv_cells
  leaf_module_declarations
  pad_cells
  pad_spacer_cells
  pg_netlist
  pg_objects
  physical_only_cells
  scalar_wire_declarations
  shadow_netlist
  spare_cells
  supply_statements

```



```
  unconnected_flip_chip_pad_cells
  unconnected_ports
  user_pg
  well_tap_cells
```

For a description of each construct and object type, see the DESCRIPTION
section. The default behavior is to include everything except for scalar wire
declarations, leaf module declarations, PG objects, connections to unconnected
ports and unconnected flip chip pad cells.
```
-exclude exclude_list
```

Specifies a list of constructs and objects to exclude from the output. When
this option is used, the Verilog file contains everything except for the types of
constructs and objects specified with this option.

The valid values are:
```
  all_physical_cells
  analog_pg
  corner_cells
  cover_cells
  diode_cells
  empty_modules
  end_cap_cells
  feedthrough_cells
  filler_cells
  flip_chip_driver_cells
  flip_chip_pad_cells
  ftv_cells
  leaf_module_declarations
  pad_cells
  pad_spacer_cells
  pg_netlist
  pg_objects
  physical_only_cells
  scalar_wire_declarations
  shadow_netlist
  spare_cells
  supply_statements
  unconnected_flip_chip_pad_cells
  unconnected_ports
  well_tap_cells
-force_reference blocks_and_lib_cells
```

Specifies blocks and lib_cells to write to the Verilog file. The
_blocks_and_lib_cells_ argument is either a collection or a name list of blocks and
lib_cells. Instances of the block or lib_cell are written regardless of the design
types specified by the _-include_ or _-exclude_ option. The module declaration of the
block is written. The module declaration of the lib_cell is also written if you use
the _-include leaf_module_declarations_ option.




The forced blocks and lib_cells are not written if they are outside the scope
specified by the _-hierarchy_ option.
```
-force_no_reference blocks_and_lib_cells
```

Specifies blocks and lib_cells to omit from the Verilog file. The
_block_and_lib_cells_ argument is either a collection or name list of blocks and
lib_cells. Instances of the block or lib_cell are omitted regardless of the design
types specified by the _-include_ or _-exclude_ option. The module declaration of the
block is omitted. The module declaration of the lib_cell is also omitted, even if
you use the _-include leaf_module_declarations_ option.

The _-force_reference_ and _-force_no_reference_ options can be used
simultaneously. However if a block or lib_cell is listed in both options, it is
omitted because the _-force_no_reference_ option has precedence.
```
-switch_view_list
```

Specifies the reference block views for hierarchical block instances to be
opened. The view at the head of the list is in higher priority.
```
-only_master_variant
```

Indicates that all the instances of variants are replaced by instances of the
masters.
```
-shell_only
```

Writes a Verilog shell netlist that contains only the module definitions and ports;
it does not include any cell instances. The _-shell_only_ option cannot be used
with the following options:
```
  -compress
  -force_reference
  -force_no_reference
  -split_bus
  -switch_view_list
  -top_module_first
-module_list
```

Lists the modules to be defined in the output Verilog file. Definitions for all other
modules are omitted. This option has precedence over all other options in
controlling which module definitions appear in the output Verilog file. This option
does not control the output of the module contents, such as the inclusion or
exclusion of module instances.

If the _-module_list_ is not specified, all modules within the specified hierarchy
scope are written (see _-hierarchy_ option).




The _-module_list_ option cannot be used with the following options:
```
  -hierarchy
  -shell_only
  -exclude_modules
-exclude_modules modules_to_exclude_list
```

Specifies the list the modules whose module declarations are to be excluded
from the output. However, their instances are written out into the file. The
_-exclude_modules_ option cannot be used with _-module_list_ option.
```
-mask_shifted_suffix_without_constraint suffix_string
```

Specifies the suffix string used to generate reference cell name when doublepatterning mask shifting enabled in the flow. If a cell instance has the mask_shift
attribute set to none zero value, this option writes the reference name of this
instance as "original_reference_name_suffix_string". Without this option, the
reference name of the instance with nonzero mask_shift is the original name.
```
-rename_cell cell_renaming_files
```

Specifies a file that contains the mapping from original mask shifted cell names
to new cell names. The renaming works for both reference library cells and
design blocks.

The name mapping comprises three sections: MASKSHIFTLAYER,
MASKSHIFTPATTERN, and CELLMAP.

For example, to rename the cell A with mask shifting on layer M1 or/and M2,
enter the following:
```
  <MASKSHIFTLAYER>
  M1 M2
  </MASKSHIFTLAYER>
  <MASKSHIFTPATTERN>
  00 01 10 11
  </MASKSHIFTPATTERN>
  <CELLMAP>
  A AM2B NONE AM1BM2B
  </CELLMAP>
```

MASKSHIFTLAYER specifies the relevant metal layers, in order, on a single
row.

MASKSHIFTPATTERN specifies the mask shift combinations to apply to the
metal layers. The digits in each combination correspond to the metal layers
listed in MASKSHIFTLAYER, respectively. For example, the 00 combination
represents a shift value of 0 on layers M1 and M2; the 01 combination
represents a shift value of 0 on layer M1 and 1 on layer M2; the 10 combination
represents a shift value of 1 on layer M1 and 0 on layer M2; and so on.




The number of mask shift combinations is less than or equal to pow(m, n),
where n is the number of layers specified in MASKSHIFTLAYER and m is the
count of the shift values. For 2-mask layers, valid shift values are 0 and 1, so m
is 2. In the example above, two metal layers are specified (M1 M2), so there are
four mask shift combinations (00 01 10 11).

CELLMAP specifies the cell mappings that correspond to each mask shift
pattern for a given cell. (Each row specifies the mappings for a single cell,
so the number of mappings in each row corresponds to the number of
MASKSHIFTPATTERN combinations.) The _write_verilog_ command renames a
cell based on the cell's mask_shift attribute and the mapping file content.

In the previous example, cell A is mapped to A, AM2B, NONE, and AM1BM2B
when its mask_shift attribute is set to 0 on both layers (00), set to 1 on layer M2
(01), set to 1 on layer M1 (10), and set to 1 on both layers (11), respectively.
When a mask-shifted cell is not expected for a particular mask shift combination,
the cell name is mapped to NONE and _write_verilog_ errors out. When a maskshifted cell is undefined, the mapping file does not contain the corresponding
name mappings and _write_verilog_ errors out.

By default, the original cell name is preserved in the output Verilog file.
```
-exclude_cells cells_to_exclude_list
```

Specifies the list of cells whose instantiation are to be excluded from the output.
```
-split_ftv_nets
```

Specifies if the Verilog writer will split the logical nets connected to ftv cells
based on the physical data. When this option is specified, FTV cells are implicitly
included in the output verilog. This option will result in an error if FTV cells are
explicitly excluded from the output using -exclude option.
```
-encrypt
```

specifies that the Verilog file should be encrypted. When using this option,
use .vp suffix for the file_name. This suffix helps in distinguishing between
encrypted and unencrypted Verilog files.
```
-key_file toolkeys
```

This option is used with option "-encrpyt" to accept user specified key file. This
option is effective only when -encrypt option is specified. The following `pragma
protect expressions are required inside the key file: key_keyowner Identifies
the owner of the key encryption key. key_method Specifies the key encryption
algorithm, the asymmetric method for encrypting or decrypting. Support “rsa”
only. key_keyname Specifies keyowner’s key name. key_public_key Specifies
the public key for key encryption.




key file example: `pragma protect key_keyowner="Intel",
key_method="rsa", key_keyname="INTEL-RSA-1", key_public_key
<content_representing_the_public_encryption_key>
```
verilog_file_name
```

Specifies the name of the Verilog file to be written. Any existing file of the same
name is overwritten. If the name ends with the .gz extension, it is compressed
using the gzip format.

**Description**

This command writes a hierarchical Verilog netlist from the current design. The current
design is automatically linked if it is not already linked. The modules are ordered in
bottom-up by default, or top-down manner if you use the _-top_module_first_ option. If the
design is not linked and autolinking fails, then only the modules of the current design are
written.

Before you use the _write_verilog_ command, to change the names of objects in the
design to conform to Verilog naming conventions, use the _change_names -rules verilog_
command.

When you use the _-include_ option, the command writes out the basic logic netlist and only
the objects specified with this option. When you use the _-exclude_ option, the command
writes out everything except for the objects specified with this option. If you use neither of
these options, the output includes everything except scalar wire declarations, leaf module
declarations, PG objects, connections to unconnected ports, unconnected flip chip pad
cells, and FTV cells. This is equivalent to specifying,
```
-exclude { scalar_wire_declarations leaf_module_declarations
pg_objects unconnected_ports
unconnected_flip_chip_pad_cells
ftv_cells }
```

Following are the valid values for the _include_list_ and _exclude_list_ :
```
GENERAL
----------------------------empty_modules       Module declarations for hierarchical (nonleaf)
cells, which might have port declarations, but
no
internal module instances and net connections
regardless of dangling nets in it.
Both the empty module and its cell instances
are
included or excluded.
leaf_module_declarations Module declarations for leaf-level cells. These
module declarations contain port declarations,
but
no internal module instances.
scalar_wire_declarations Scalar wire declarations.

```



```
shadow_netlist      Shadow netlist cells, nets, ports, and pins.
unconnected_ports     Connections to unconnected ports on module
instances. These connections are written out
with a net named "SYNOPSYS_UNCONNECTED_"
plus a unique integer.
POWER AND GROUND
---------------analog_pg         Analog power and ground nets, ports, and
pin connections.
pg_netlist        Power and ground nets, ports, and pin
connections.
pg_objects        All power and ground objects. Specifying this
value
is equivalent to specifying the analog_pg,
pg_netlist, and supply_statements values.
supply_statements     Supply1 and Supply0 declarations for power and
ground nets.
user_pg          Power and ground nets, ports, and pins,
along with tie nets, which have is_user_pg
attribute values set to true .
CELL TYPE
----------all_physical_cells        Physical cells in any of the following
categories.
Specifying this value is equivalent to
specifying
all of the other following individual
values.
corner_cells           Physical cells with design_type
"corner".
cover_cells           Physical cells with design_type "cover".
diode_cells           Physical cells with design_type "diode".
end_cap_cells          Physical cells with design_type
"end_cap".
feedthrough_cells        Physical cells with design_type
"feedthrough".
filler_cells           Physical cells with design_type
"filler".
flip_chip_driver_cells      Physical cells with design_type
"flip_chip_driver".
flip_chip_pad_cells       Physical cells with design_type
"flip_chip_pad".
ftv_cells            Physical cells with design_type "ftv".
pad_cells            Physical cells with design_type "pad".
pad_spacer_cells         Physical cells with design_type
"pad_spacer".
physical_only_cells       Physical cells which are physical-only
(that is, cell is_physical_only
attribute is set to true ).
spare_cells           Physical cells which are unconnected or
only

```



```
connected to constant nets.
unconnected_flip_chip_pad_cells Physical cells with design_type
"flip_chip_pad" and whose pins are
not connected to any nets.
well_tap_cells          Physical cells with design_type
"well_tap".
```

The _include_list_ also allows the following value:
```
all            All of the objects in the other categories
```

**Examples**

The following example writes a Verilog file:
```
prompt> write_verilog my_output.v
```

The following example writes a Verilog file with all constructs and objects:
```
prompt> write_verilog -include {all} my_output.v
```

The following example writes a Verilog file with everything except cover and well tap cells.
```
prompt> write_verilog -exclude {cover_cells well_tap_cells} my_output.v
```

The following example writes a Verilog file with everything except scalar wire declarations
and leaf module declarations. It implicitly includes all physical cells, the PG netlist, and
supply statements.
```
prompt> write_verilog -exclude \\
 { scalar_wire_declarations leaf_module_declarations} my_output.v
```

The following example writes a Verilog file with everything except scalar wire declarations,
leaf module declarations, and supply statements. It implicitly includes all physical cells and
the PG netlist.
```
prompt> write_verilog -exclude {scalar_wire_declarations \\
 leaf_module_declarations supply_statements} my_output.v
```

The following example writes a Verilog file containing the user-defined PG netlist and
associated supply statements, but omits the PG netlist that are not user-defined.
```
prompt> write_verilog -include {user_pg supply_statements} my_output.v
```

The following example writes a Verilog file containing the modules mid and bot.
```
prompt> write_verilog -module_list {mid bot} my_output.v
```

The following example writes a Verilog file without the module mid.
```
prompt> write_verilog -exclude_modules { mid } my_output.v
```

The following example writes a Verilog file without the cell U427.




```
prompt> write_verilog -exclude_cells [ get_cells U427 ] my_output.v
```

The following example writes a Verilog file with module 'myAlu' as it's top module.
```
prompt> write_verilog -module_top myAlu my_output.v

```

###### **write_virtual_pad_file**

Saves all existing virtual pad locations and layers to a file.

**Syntax**

status _write_virtual_pad_file_

```
     file_name

```

**Data Types**
```
file_name  string
```

**Arguments**
```
file_name
```

Specifies a file name into which to write all existing virtual pad locations and
layers.

**Description**

This command saves all existing virtual pad locations and layers to a file.

**Multicorner-Multimode Support**

This command is not supported in a multi-scenario design flow.

**Examples**

The following example saves all existing virtual pads to a file name test.vpad.
```
prompt> write_virtual_pad_file test.vpad

```

###### **write_waiver_containers**

Writes DRC error waiver containers to a file on disk.

**Syntax**
```
status write_waiver_containers
-file_name file_name
[-overwrite]
drc_error_waiver_file

```

**Data Types**
```
string   file_name
collection  drc_error_waiver_file
```

**Arguments**
```
-file_name file_name
```

Specifies the name of the error waiver container TCL file to create.
```
-overwrite
```

Overwrites an existing file with the same name as the specified output file.

By default, the command fails is a file exists with the same name.
```
drc_error_waiver_file
```

Specifies the DRC error waiver container object to export to a file.

**Description**

The _write_waiver_containers_ command writes error waiver container object to an external
error waiver container file with the specified file name. The command fails if the specified
error data file already exists.

The command returns 1 if successful; 0 otherwise.




**Examples**

The following example exports the DRC error waiver container file that is named
"containFile.tcl".
```
prompt> write_waiver_containers -file_name containFile.tcl \\
[get_waiver_containers] -overwrite
1

```

**See Also**

 - create_waiver_container

 - get_waiver_containers

 - remove_waiver_containers
